world: #4 SOCIAL (age 15): Instagram content creation, 10M+ views, 2K+ followers

concepts.name: Feed Jackpot
concepts.oneLiner: The infinite feed is secretly a slot machine. Your own scroll spins eight hot-chrome columns of posts into neon light-bars, then they slam to a stop one by one until the feed itself spells 10,000,000+.

palette.role: Void Navy: backdrop and the gaps between reels
Electric Cobalt: main holo gradient and the smeared light-bars
Hot Magenta: second gradient, landing flashes, 2-frame background invert
Chrome Silver: chrome type, digit cards, stickers
Holo Cyan: foil sheen, RGB-split fringe, ticker
Josh Lime (site accent): used only for the jackpot '+' and the PAYOUT tray

concepts.typography: Unbounded 800–900 for the headline and the jackpot digits. Chrome comes from CSS background-clip:text with a banded steel→white→cobalt gradient, plus a holo-cyan foil sheen that sweeps every 3s and a hard 3-step extrusion from stacked text-shadows. Headline words are split with SplitType, and their scaleY is bound to Lenis velocity (1→1.5, springing back to 1 when you stop). Bungee for stickers, the lime '+', the PAYOUT tray and the punchline lines; these are always slapped on with squash-and-stretch (back.out(2.2)) at a random −6° to 8° tilt. Martian Mono (variable, wdth 75–112.5) for the marquee ticker and HUD labels; its width axis stretches with scroll speed.
concepts.atmosphere: Y2K holo-chrome night. Deep void-navy sits behind everything, with a slow holographic aurora (a conic gradient cycling cobalt→magenta→cyan) bleeding through the gaps between reels. CRT scanlines, soft bloom and fine grain on top. Chrome bubble stickers (sparkle stars, puffy hearts, 'NEW' pills, never numbers) drift at three parallax depths. The posts are procedurally generated 9:16 cards: hot gradients, blobby SDF shapes, code-drawn cartoon faces and one-word captions ('WAIT', 'NO WAY', 'POV', '?!'). They carry no logos, no platform UI and no fake metrics, so the only numbers on screen are Josh's real ones. There is no gambling iconography: no cherries, coins or cabinet. The slot machine exists only in how the reels move.
concepts.heroMoment: THE JACKPOT STOP. At 50% scroll all reels (8 on desktop, 4 on phones) are spinning at full speed, smeared into neon light-bars. Between 50% and 68% each reel gets its own ~2%-wide stop window, left to right. In that window a critically damped spring with a deliberate 6% overshoot lands the column's pre-seeded landing row, a giant chrome digit card, dead-center. Each landing fires four things: a 70ms hit-stop (the shared gsap.ticker timeScale drops to 0, so the still-spinning reels freeze mid-smear), a 2-frame additive white flash on that column, a 5px screen shake that decays, and a burst of chrome 'clack' sparkles. While digits land, stickers and the ticker dim to 40% so the chrome owns the frame. Desktop landings spell 1-0-0-0-0-0-0-0; commas pop in between reels 2|3 and 5|6, then a lime Bungee '+' slaps on with squash-and-stretch. On phones the 4 reels land on '1', '0', 'M', '+'. On the final landing the background hard-inverts magenta↔cobalt for 2 frames and hearts erupt from the '+'. The wall that was the feed is now the number.
supporting: Procedural post atlas: a seeded Canvas2D generator draws ~48 unique 9:16 posts plus 10 chrome digit cards and a comma into one atlas at runtime. Nothing is a real image, logo or platform UI string.

Velocity is the brush: Lenis velocity drives per-column vertical motion-blur taps, RGB split and the headline's scaleY. Flick hard and the wall melts into light-bars; stop and it springs back to crisp.
The baseline's 'columns at different speeds' (alternating up/down, 0.7×–1.8×) are secretly slot reels. That is only revealed when they start landing on digits.
Chrome Y2K sticker storm: sparkle stars, puffy hearts and 'NEW' pills in three depth layers with mouse parallax and a holo-foil sweep on hover.
Payout paint trails: after the jackpot, hearts bounce off the bottom edge on a non-clearing canvas and leave smeared color trails across the wall, then a horizontal chrome shine wipes them clean.
Marquee ticker along the top and bottom edges ('POST ✦ PRAY ✦ REFRESH ✦ REPEAT ✦'). Its speed and Martian Mono width axis are tied to scroll velocity.
scrollBeats: 0–8%: The Rubik's world's phone-shaped portal opens and we dive into a logo-free lock screen: a chrome '15' clock (labeled AGE) on a cobalt→magenta holo gradient, with one notification pill dropping in on a springy bounce.

8–22%: The pill flicks up and the lock screen shatters into the feed wall: 8 reels (4 on phones) of generated posts sliding at different speeds and directions. The chrome headline builds word by word on a void-navy caption bar so it stays legible, and stickers drift in at three depths.

22–50%: Spin-up. The reels accelerate past your scroll while blur taps and RGB split ramp with velocity until the posts smear into neon light-bars. The ticker races and 'Every post was a pull of the lever.' slaps on in Bungee.

50–68%: HERO, the Jackpot Stop. Reels slam to a stop left to right with hit-stop, flash and shake, each landing on a chrome digit. Commas pop in, the lime '+' slaps on, and the wall reads 10,000,000+ views.

68–85%: Payout. Hearts bounce and paint trails across the wall while a small tray slides in underneath: 'PAYOUT: 2K+ followers.' Then: 'Views are the jackpot. Followers are the payout. The math is humbling.'
85–100%: The wall spins one last time and its light-bars converge into the next world's portal silhouette, which opens. Dive. (The pinned section is about 3.2 viewport-heights.)
concepts.portalIcon: A phone: a tall rounded rectangle (~9:19.5, corner radius about 14% of the width) with a small pill notch punched out near the top, as a single evenodd path. For a clean handoff, the Rubik's world's center sticker can stretch from a square into this shape before it opens.
concepts.titleCard: A logo-free lock screen on a cobalt→magenta holo gradient. An enormous chrome '15' sits where the clock would be, with a tiny Martian Mono label reading AGE. One notification pill drops in with a springy bounce: 'NEW OBSESSION · now: get strangers on the internet to look at you.' A beat later the pill flicks up and the feed floods in.

copy.headline: Before I knew what a startup was, I was already trying to get strangers on the internet to pay attention.
lines: Age 15. Instagram. The game: make a stranger's thumb stop on you.
Every post was a pull of the lever.
10M+ views.
Payout: 2K+ followers.
Views are the jackpot. Followers are the payout. The math is humbling.

concepts.tech: No live 3D needed: the whole feed wall is ONE full-screen fragment shader, drawn either by a lazy-loaded WebGL2 hook (~200 lines) or by an R3F <Canvas orthographic> with a single ShaderMaterial plane if three is already loaded for another world. Columns are computed per pixel (col = floor(uv.x*N)). Each column's offset and velocity live in uniform arrays written from JS. The tile at (col,row) is picked from a runtime Canvas2D atlas (2048² desktop, 1024² mobile) by hash(col,row), except each column's landing row, which is forced to its digit tile. Vertical motion blur takes N taps along y scaled by |velocity| (12 on desktop, 4 on mobile); RGB split offsets the R and B taps; saturation and flash are uniforms. Slot logic lives in JS: each reel integrates its own velocity, and inside its stop window a damped spring lands the landing row at screen center. Because the landing row is chosen ahead of the current offset, the stop is always forward and deterministic, and scrolling back up respins the reels. One clock: gsap.ticker drives Lenis.raf, the render, and the 70ms hit-stop through timeScale. ScrollTrigger uses scroller '#scroll-container' with pin and scrub:1 for progress. The DOM overlay holds the headline, SVG stickers, ticker and copy as semantic text; the canvas is aria-hidden and paused offscreen through IntersectionObserver. Payout trails run on a separate non-clearing 2D canvas (≤40 sprites on desktop, 12 on mobile). Phones get 4 reels spelling '10M+', DPR ≤1.25, 4 blur taps and no RGB split. With prefers-reduced-motion there is no spin, blur, shake or trails: a static wall of posts already shows '10,000,000+' (desktop) or '10M+' (phones), with 'PAYOUT: 2K+ followers' and every line visible.
concepts.risk: Feed columns and a counter are still the baseline's vocabulary, the slot metaphor can read as cynical 'gambling', and velocity-coupled warp blur can cause motion discomfort. Mitigation: make the reels-become-the-number mechanic the undeniable star by prototyping the stop rhythm (timing, hit-stop, overshoot) first. Keep gambling iconography out entirely. Clamp blur strength, and fall back to the static wall under reduced motion. Make the landed digits the only crisp chrome objects at the climax so the number reads instantly at 375px.

concepts.name: Eyes On Me
concepts.oneLiner: Attention, made literal. One cartoon eye opens and looks at you, then thousands more pop open in powers of ten until 10M+ views are staring at your cursor. Then everyone blinks, and only the 2K+ who stayed open their eyes again and literally follow you.

palette.role: Bubblegum: the entire flat field (no gradients anywhere in this world)
Ink Plum: outlines, pupils, lash lines, hard sticker shadows, all type
Sclera Cream: eye whites and the cursor post card
Violet: iris family A
Sunflower: iris family B
Follower Lime (site accent): irises of the 2K+ who stayed, and nothing else

concepts.typography: Anybody (variable: wdth 50–150, wght 100–900, ital) for the title, headline and counter digits. Its font-variation-settings are tweened by the same scroll timeline: the more eyes are open, the wider and heavier the words get (wdth 60→150, wght 300→900), so the type literally swells under attention and deflates on the blink. Every text reveal is an eyelid wipe (scaleY 0→1 opening from an ink lash line) with saccadic timing: an 80ms snap, then a hold, never a smooth slide. Bagel Fat One for the bubbly punchlines ('They follow. Literally.'), stamped with a 3px hard plum offset shadow. IBM Plex Mono 500 for tiny HUD labels (VIEWS / FOLLOWERS / WORLD 04). On phones 'LOOK AT ME.' stacks onto two lines (LOOK / AT ME.) so the O-eyes stay huge.
concepts.atmosphere: Flat, saturated bubblegum pink: a deliberate anti-gradient so the eyes are the only texture. Every eye is a vinyl sticker with chunky ink outlines and a hard offset plum shadow (no blur), plus a faint procedural risograph grain over the field. The motion language is saccadic: eyes never glide, they dart (80ms) and hold (150–700ms, randomized), with idle micro-blinks rippling at random. Nothing else decorates the screen: no hearts floating, no notification bubbles, no phone frames. The crowd IS the design.
concepts.heroMoment: THE BLINK. At ~58% the screen is a wall-to-wall sea of eyes (about 100K procedural cells on desktop, about 20K on phones), all staring at your cursor, with the counter locked at '10M+ views'. Crossing the trigger fires a blink wave from the cursor: the blink-radius uniform tweens from 0 to the screen diagonal over a short stretch of scrubbed scroll. As the wavefront passes each cell, its lids slam shut in 60ms (openness 1→0, the ink lash line stays). 250ms later the closed eyes shrink and sink into the pink (scale 1→0 with a slight downward drift); the crowd 'scrolls on'. The field keeps receding during the wave (cells ×4), so the closing sea reads as endless. Behind the wavefront, exactly 2,000 lime-iris eyes (an instanced layer placed on deterministic cell centers) pop back open 300ms after the wave passes them, with a squash-and-stretch (0→1.3→1) and a 4-point sparkle, scattered like a constellation against the empty pink. The HUD flips with an eyelid wipe to '10M+ looked. 2K+ stayed.' and the headline deflates. Then the 2,000 lift off and swarm the cursor as literal followers.
supporting: Live-eye title: in 'LOOK AT ME.' both O's are SVG cartoon eyes that find your cursor the instant the portal finishes, blink once slowly, and blink again on click.

The cursor is the post: inside this world the site's custom cursor morphs into a tiny logo-free 9:16 post card with a lime play-triangle, the thing every eye is watching. You are standing where Josh stood. On touch, the card parks wherever you last tapped.

Powers-of-ten pop rings: each power of ten pops a new ring of eyes outward from the center with squash-and-stretch, while the field recedes from one giant eye to a shimmering sea in sync with the odometer.
Heart pupils: eyes within ~120px of the post-cursor swap round pupils for heart SDFs and get pink blush, a 'like' with no platform UI. Clicking makes every eye in range heart at once.
Attention-inflated type: Anybody's width and weight axes are bound to how many eyes are open, so the headline physically swells with each wave and collapses on the blink.
Saccadic grammar everywhere: eye gaze, text reveals and HUD updates all move in dart-and-hold rhythms, and if the pointer sleeps for 3s the whole field glances in unison toward the scroll hint.
scrollBeats: 0–8%: The eye-shaped portal opens like an eyelid and we dive through the pupil. The title card 'LOOK AT ME.' appears, and both O's are live eyes that find your cursor and blink once.

8–18%: The title eyelid-wipes into a corner tag. One giant closed eye fills the screen; scrolling opens it and it looks straight at you. The counter reads 1 view, and the headline opens line by line with eyelid reveals.

18–48%: Powers of ten. Every ~4% of scroll a new ring pops open (10 → 100 → 1K → 10K → 100K…) as the field recedes. Every eye saccades to your post-cursor, heart pupils bloom near it, the headline swells with each wave, and the counter rolls on a log scale.

48–58%: Full stare. The screen is a wall-to-wall sea of eyes, the counter slams to '10M+ views', and every eye snaps to you on the same frame. Copy: 'This is what 10M+ views feels like from the inside.'
58–72%: HERO, The Blink. A lid wave rolls out from your cursor; the sea closes and sinks; 2,000 lime eyes open again with sparkles. Copy: '10M+ looked. 2K+ stayed.' The headline deflates.

72–90%: Followers. The lime eyes lift off as a swarm and follow your cursor or finger everywhere. Copy: '2K+ followers. They follow. Literally.' then 'Attention is easy to get and hard to keep. Noted, for later.'
90–100%: The swarm streams into the next world's portal silhouette, outlines it in lime, and the shape irises open. Dive. (The pinned section is about 3.5 viewport-heights.)
concepts.portalIcon: An almond eye: a pointed vesica/lens outline with a solid round iris centered and the pupil punched out (single evenodd path). It opens like an eyelid: the mask scales from a 2px horizontal slit to the full almond, then the camera dives through the pupil.
concepts.titleCard: A bubblegum-pink field with a giant ink-plum 'LOOK AT ME.' in Anybody (wdth 150, wght 900). Both O's are live cartoon eyes (cream sclera, violet irises, chunky outlines) that snap to your cursor as the portal finishes opening, then blink once, slowly. Underneath, in IBM Plex Mono: 'WORLD 04 · AGE 15 · INSTAGRAM'.

copy.headline: Before I knew what a startup was, I was already trying to get strangers on the internet to pay attention.
lines: Age 15. Instagram. One goal: get looked at.
10M+ views. This is what that feels like from the inside.
Then everyone blinks.
10M+ looked. 2K+ stayed.
2K+ followers. They follow. Literally.
Attention is easy to get and hard to keep. Noted, for later.

concepts.tech: This world is pure 2D shading, so it needs no scene graph: a lazy-loaded WebGL2 canvas (a ~200-line hook), or an R3F <Canvas orthographic> with a ShaderMaterial plane plus an InstancedMesh if the page already ships three for other worlds. It mounts only within ±1 viewport through IntersectionObserver and pauses offscreen. Two draw calls in total. Layer 1, the field: ONE full-screen fragment shader draws every eye procedurally per grid cell (fract(uv*cells) with hash jitter and a minimum gap). Each cell gets a vesica-SDF sclera, an iris with angular-noise striations, a pupil (or a heart SDF near the post-cursor), a fixed specular highlight, an ink outline with a hard offset shadow, and a lid squash from per-cell openness. 'cells' is a log-scale uniform scrubbed from 1 to ~100K, so thousands of eyes cost the same as one. Below ~6px per cell it crossfades to averaged iris color plus sparkle so it never aliases. Gaze is normalize(gazeTarget[hash%8] − cellCenter); the 8 gaze-target uniforms are updated on the CPU with staggered saccade timing (80ms dart, 150–700ms hold), which gives organic group glances. Blink is a wave origin plus radius uniform, with openness computed in-shader, so there is no per-eye CPU work. Layer 2, the followers: 2,000 instanced quads using the same eye shader in lime, spawned on cell centers computed with the same grid math in JS. A CPU boids sim (seek the cursor, separation and alignment on a uniform-grid spatial hash, ~0.3ms/frame) drives them. Exit targets are 2,000 points sampled from the next portal's SVG path with getPointAtLength. The DOM layer holds the title, headline (Anybody axes via font-variation-settings), counter and copy as semantic text, with the canvas aria-hidden. One GSAP timeline (ScrollTrigger, scroller '#scroll-container', Lenis-synced, pin plus scrub:1) drives cells, the wave and the DOM, and rendering is called from gsap.ticker so everything runs on one clock. Phones: DPR ≤1.25, a cell cap of about 20K, boids at 30Hz with interpolation. Eyes track the last touch, or else an autonomous drift around the headline. Reduced motion: no canvas at all. Instead, a static SVG composition of ~60 sticker eyes (a dozen lime) all looking at the headline, with counters at their final values ('10M+ views', '2K+ followers'), every line visible, and no blink, swarm or tracking.
concepts.risk: A wall of eyes can tip from delightful into creepy or trypophobic, and a full-screen shader can choke low-end phones. Mitigation: keep it strictly cartoon (big round irises, chunky ink outlines, lashes and blush, no veins or realism), use jittered loose spacing with a minimum gap, and hold the densest stare for under one viewport of scroll, rendered below 6px as shimmering texture rather than legible holes. Heart pupils, the post-cursor and the jokes keep it warm. A GPU-tier check lowers the cell cap and DPR, and the static SVG version is the guaranteed floor.

why: Eyes On Me is stronger. It turns the literal headline (get strangers to pay attention) and the honest gap between 10M+ views and 2K+ followers into one unforgettable hero: the mass blink, after which only the followers open their eyes again and then literally follow you. Its flat, saccadic, eye-shaped language also contrasts with the page's portal fly-throughs instead of repeating them, whereas Feed Jackpot, for all its upgrades, still speaks the baseline's language of feed columns and counters.

world: #2 Sports (age 14): roller skating (state level) + yoga (state level), 20–25 medals combined

concepts.name: Laps Become Medals
concepts.oneLiner: Your scroll becomes Josh's training. Every lap around a top-down night rink paints a neon guilloche, and at 'state level' that exact pattern is struck into a real engraved medal whose reverse is a lotus drawn by yoga breaths. Medals are just receipts for laps.

palette.role: Ultramarine rink floor and world background (blue and metal, not the synthwave purple)
Hot pink: the comet skater's wheel glow and the first laps of the trail
Tangerine: mid-trail laps, kinetic statements, start-line chequer
Site lime: the final laps, the lap counter and the 20–25 odometer (ties back to the site chrome)
Warm struck-metal base under an iridescent thin film. Deliberately non-ranked: never gold, silver or bronze. Also used for Cinzel inscriptions
Breath lilac: lane lines, yoga lotus strokes, the haze of the calm beat

concepts.typography: Monoton, on the title card only: its parallel inline strokes rhyme with the lap trails, and each letter draws on stroke by stroke like laps. Unbounded (variable 300–900) for every kinetic statement: weight, horizontal stretch (scaleX up to 1.35) and skew follow scroll velocity like a skater leaning into a turn, then spring back upright at rest. Cinzel for everything struck: the medal rim inscriptions and the 'state level' lines. The fast type turns into carved type at the strike. Geist Mono (site) in lime tabular numerals for the lap counter and the 20–25 odometer.
concepts.atmosphere: A top-down night rink, flat and graphic, with no synthwave grid. Saturated ultramarine floor with a slow-roaming overhead-light sheen, procedural grain, lilac lane lines, a candy chequered start line, and the comet's glow pooling on the floor around it. As laps stack up, fine-line moiré makes the whole rink shimmer and seem to rotate. After the strike the house lights drop to ultramarine-black and the iridescent medal is the only light, throwing disco glints across the rink walls. The yoga beat cools to a lilac haze: the grain softens and everything slows to breathing speed.
concepts.heroMoment: THE STRIKE. The section is pinned for about 1.6 viewports, and scroll distance equals skating distance. A comet skater (pink glow head with two tiny LED wheels aligned to its tangent) laps a top-down oval. Each lap the oval precesses by 180°/N (7.5° at 24 laps). A stride wobble adds a 7-lobe ripple, with its amplitude sampled from smoothed scroll velocity. The trail is drawn with additive blending and its hue steps hot pink → tangerine → lime per lap, so it builds a dense guilloche rosette with live moiré while the lime lap counter climbs. On 'I reached state level.' the final lap closes, the house lights cut, and a coin-press strike lands: one white frame (single, never repeated), a radial shockwave ring and a 6px shake. The exact rosette the visitor just drew becomes the face of a heavy medal in R3F. The same canvas that was the neon emissive map becomes its bump map, tweened from 0 to 1 so the lines visibly press into iridescent heat-tinted metal. A raised bevelled rim reads 'ROLLER SKATING · STATE LEVEL ·' in Cinzel. The disc tilts up toward the camera. Moving the pointer (or scrolling on touch) tilts it ±12°, so a rainbow sheen rakes across the engraved lines like real engine-turned metal. Fast scrollers mint a wilder rosette, so no two visitors' medals are quite identical.
supporting: Speed-stretch type: Unbounded statements widen, gain weight and lean into the curve with scroll velocity, then spring back upright when you stop. The type skates.
Live moiré bloom: hundreds of 1px additive lines interfere, so the finished rosette shimmers and appears to rotate even while the comet sits still. It is an optical effect a screenshot can't capture.

Rink furniture as the graphic system: lilac lane lines, painted lap numbers, a pink/tangerine chequered start line, two-wheel tread marks, and at most 60 spark flecks (20 on phones) flicking off the comet on the turns.
Disco-ball nod: as the struck medal tilts, it throws 24 four-point light stars across the rink walls. The roller-disco ball is reinvented as the medal itself.

Breath lotus on the reverse: yoga is drawn by breathing. Eight slow lilac petal strokes, an 'inhale / exhale' ring, then a soft strike with no flash and no shake. One medal, two sides, both state level.
Honest receipts: 20 struck medals plus 5 dashed ghost outlines, and an odometer that can't decide (20…25…22…24) before it lands on '20–25'. The range is shown as design, not hidden.
scrollBeats: 0–8% PORTAL LANDING: the roller-skate mask from World 1 expands, and its two wheel holes match-cut onto the rink oval's two turns. Title card: Monoton 'SPORTS' draws on like laps, with 'AGE 14 — I tried to go pro.' and a lime LAP 00. The comet skater idles on the chequer.

8–40% THE LAPS: scroll equals skating. The comet laps the oval (24 laps on desktop, 16 on phones), each lap precessing and painting the next hue. The lap counter climbs. 'Roller skating. Lap after lap after lap.' stretches and leans with scroll speed. Moiré builds until the whole rink shimmers.

40–52% THE STRIKE (hero): the final lap closes, the lights cut and the press hits. The rosette becomes the embossed iridescent medal face with the rim 'ROLLER SKATING · STATE LEVEL ·', and 'I reached state level.' sets in Cinzel beneath. The pointer tilts the medal to rake the sheen.

52–72% BREATH: the medal flips to a blank reverse and the scroll-to-progress ratio slows about 3x. 'inhale / exhale' prompts pulse while eight breath strokes draw a lilac lotus. A soft strike embosses it with the rim 'YOGA · STATE LEVEL ·'. Copy: 'Yoga: the exact opposite sport. Also state level.'

72–88% THE RECEIPTS: the medal tosses up and multiplies into 25 hanging on striped ribbons: 20 struck, 5 dashed ghosts. The odometer flickers and lands on '20–25'. Copy: 'I won medals. 20–25 of them, combined.' then 'Medals are just receipts for the laps.' The medals swing with scroll velocity, throwing glints.

88–100% ANOTHER DIRECTION: the medals lift out of frame and one fresh comet starts a lap. On 'Then life moved in another direction.' it breaks off the oval along its tangent, makes three hard 90° turns, and its trail squares the circle into the next world's cube silhouette. That is the portal into World 3 (Rubik's), and the camera dives through.
concepts.portalIcon: Side-profile quad roller skate: chunky high-top boot, flat plate, two big round wheels with punched-out hubs, and a toe-stop nub. One closed compound path that reads at 40px. As the mask expands, the wheel holes land on the rink oval's two turns. On phones the mask rotates 90° while growing so they land on the portrait oval.
concepts.titleCard: Through the skate-shaped hole: an ultramarine night rink seen straight down from the rafters, with lilac lane lines, a pink/tangerine chequered start line and one comet skater idling with two glowing LED wheels. Centred in the infield, 'SPORTS' in Monoton's parallel neon strokes, 'AGE 14 — I tried to go pro.' in Unbounded beneath it, and a lime LAP 00 counter blinking like a scoreboard waiting for the start.

copy.headline: I tried to go pro.
lines: Roller skating. Lap after lap after lap.
I reached state level.
Yoga: the exact opposite sport. Also state level.
I won medals. 20–25 of them, combined.
Medals are just receipts for the laps.
Then life moved in another direction.

concepts.tech:
Pin: GSAP ScrollTrigger (about 350vh) with scroller '#scroll-container', pinType 'transform', and lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update).

Laps: Canvas 2D drawing a rotated-ellipse rosette, P(t) = Rot(lap·180°/N)·(a·cos t, b·sin t)·(1 + ε·sin 7t), with ε taken from smoothed Lenis velocity. Points are stored in a Float32Array so scrolling back un-draws them. Each redraw is one stroke per lap with 'lighter' compositing, plus a wide low-alpha glow pass on desktop only.

Strike and medals: the R3F chunk is dynamic-imported when the section is about one viewport away, with frameloop 'demand' invalidated by scroll and pointer. On the strike frame the 2D canvas hides and an R3F disc, aligned to the same screen rect, takes over with no visible seam. The same CanvasTexture serves as the disc's emissiveMap (neon) and bumpMap (relief). The strike tweens emissiveIntensity 1→0, bumpScale 0→1 and metalness 0→1 on a MeshPhysicalMaterial (roughness about 0.25, iridescence 1). The rim ring and the Cinzel inscription are drawn into the same canvas, so they emboss for free. Reflections come from a drei <Environment> built only from coloured <Lightformer>s, so no HDR files are needed. The reverse face uses a second canvas for the lotus. The 25 medals are an InstancedMesh (20 struck) plus 5 instanced ghost rings, about 3 draw calls.

Performance and phones: DPR clamped to [1, 1.75]. Phones get 16 laps, a portrait oval, no glow pass, a 512² texture, at most 20 sparks, and on low-end devices a standard material without iridescence. If WebGL fails, a 2D canvas emboss fallback takes over.

Reduced motion: no pin, scrub, flash or shake. The finished rosette medal (obverse plus lotus reverse), the 20 + 5 row and all copy render as a static, readable composition, and the exit portal becomes a crossfade.
concepts.risk: It could read as abstract generative art rather than 'Josh skated', and the quality of the strike material makes or breaks it. Mitigation: keep the first beat literal (rink lines, start chequer, two-wheel skater head, lap counter, huge copy) before the pattern gets dense. Prototype the strike first on a mid-range Android and ship the 2D emboss fallback. Strike the medals in iridescent, non-ranked metal so the visuals never imply gold placings the facts don't state. If Josh's discipline was artistic rather than speed skating, swap the oval for a precessing figure-eight. Same technique, equally striking rosette.

concepts.name: The State Level Arc
concepts.oneLiner: Josh's sports years retold as a sports-anime season printed as a fluorescent risograph zine, with speed lines, giant SFX and impact frames. The skater physically bursts off the paper at 'STATE LEVEL', yoga is the one silent page, and the season ends on 'NEXT ARC →'.

palette.role: Newsprint paper: page ground
Fluoro pink ink: speed lines, SFX fills, the skater's top ink layer
Riso blue ink: halftone shadows, screentones, the single-ink Zen page
Yellow ink: highlights, sparkle stars, impact-frame scribble outlines
Fluoro orange ink: the medal haul (deliberately not gold, so no placings are implied) and the 'NEXT ARC' tab
Ink black: gutters, outlines, impact-frame ground

concepts.typography: Dela Gothic One for SFX and episode titles, set enormous with a 3-ink extruded offset (pink, blue and yellow layers) and velocity-driven skew, with outlines that boil on twos. Zen Kaku Gothic New (Bold/Black) for narration in classic rectangular caption boxes, revealed word by word with stepped timing. Gochi Hand for Josh's handwritten margin asides and arrows. No fake Japanese anywhere: every SFX is an original English onomatopoeia (WHRRRRR, SKRRRT, KA-CHING, HAAAAH).
concepts.atmosphere: Off-white newsprint with riso grain and paper fibre. Three fluoro ink layers multiply with living misregistration. Halftone dot gradients and screentones, thick hand-inked gutters with a slight wobble, and speed-line bursts. Printer's crop marks, registration targets, colour bars and the page number 'p.14' sit in the margins. Everything on the character side animates 'on twos' (12fps) like real anime while the camera glides at 60fps. Outlines gently boil, and sweat drops and sparkle stars punctuate the beats.
concepts.heroMoment: PANEL BREAK → IMPACT FRAME. A six-panel manga page with angled gutters is pinned. Scroll pushes the camera into panel 4 (a skate-wheel close-up with a 'WHRRRRR' SFX), and scroll velocity thickens the speed lines. At the pin's midpoint the panel's inked border cracks into 9 pre-cut clip-path shards that fly at the camera (translateZ 400–900px, random rotate3d). The page plane tilts back in CSS 3D while the skater silhouette, its three riso ink layers splitting 8px apart, bursts off the paper at a higher translateZ, scaling from 30vh to 140vh across every gutter. Then the IMPACT FRAME holds for about half a viewport of scroll. The whole screen inverts to ink black. The skater becomes a fluoro pink/yellow scribble outline boiling on twos (SVG turbulence displacement re-seeded at 12fps). Radial speed lines erupt from the front wheel, and 'STATE LEVEL' slams in at about 38vw in Dela Gothic One with a three-ink extruded shadow over the caption box 'Roller skating. I reached STATE LEVEL.' Scrolling on snaps it back to paper as the shards settle into the gutters of the next page.
supporting: The eyes strip: a full-width letterbox panel of determined eyes built from pure SVG geometry (two sharp almond shapes, star glints that rotate with scroll, one sweat drop) under 'Age 14. I tried to go pro.'
SFX as architecture: giant WHRRRRR, SKRRRT, KA-CHING and HAAAAH letterforms with 3-ink extrusion that overlap the gutters, skew with scroll velocity and boil on twos. The sound is part of the layout.
Living misregistration: every artwork is three multiplied ink layers that drift 1–2px with noise and split up to 8px when you scroll fast, so the print itself reacts to speed.

The Zen Page (yoga): a hard cut to a single-ink riso-blue page that is 80% empty. One tiny balanced silhouette, a screentone circle breathing 4s in and 6s out, the speed lines gone. 'Yoga. Also state level.' This is the quietest moment in a maximal world.
The haul spread: medals printed in fluoro inks with halftone shine and sparkle stars. Twenty are fully inked and five are left as blue-pencil underdrawing, with a margin note: 'the range is honest'.
Printer's furniture as decoration: crop marks, registration targets, colour bars and the page number 'p.14'. A final 'NEXT ARC →' tab triggers a 3D page curl.
scrollBeats: 0–10% COVER: the skate-shaped portal opens onto the riso manga cover: 'EPISODE 02 · THE STATE LEVEL ARC', a skater silhouette in a pink speed-line burst, and 'JOSH, AGE 14'. The inks slide into registration as you arrive.

10–28% TRAINING PAGE: page 1 pins and the camera dives panel to panel: the eyes strip ('Age 14. I tried to go pro.'), the wheel close-up ('WHRRRRR'), then a stride silhouette crossing two panels ('SKRRRT'). Scroll velocity thickens the speed lines and splits the ink layers.

28–45% PANEL BREAK → IMPACT FRAME (hero): the shards fly, the skater bursts off the paper, the screen inverts and 'STATE LEVEL' slams in over 'Roller skating. I reached STATE LEVEL.' Then it snaps back to paper.
45–62% THE ZEN PAGE: a single-ink blue page, a tiny balanced silhouette and a breathing screentone circle scrubbed by scroll. Copy: 'Meanwhile, in the quietest sport alive… Yoga. Also state level.'

62–82% THE HAUL: a double-page spread slides in. Medals pop in on twos with KA-CHING SFX and sparkle stars: 20 fully inked, 5 left as pencil underdrawing. Copy: 'I won medals. 20–25 of them, combined.'

82–100% SEASON FINALE: in the last panel the silhouette turns toward the page edge. 'Then life moved in another direction.' A 'NEXT ARC →' tab appears and the page curls up in 3D to reveal a cube-shaped die-cut hole in the page beneath. That is the portal into World 3 (Rubik's), and the camera dives through.
concepts.portalIcon: Side-profile roller skate in a hard forward lean, two wheels with punched hubs, and three speed-slash cut-outs trailing off the heel. One compound path, so the portal itself reads like a manga action panel.
concepts.titleCard: A risograph-printed manga cover on newsprint. 'EPISODE 02' sits in a black tab and 'THE STATE LEVEL ARC' towers in Dela Gothic One, printed in three misregistered fluoro inks. A silhouetted skater mid-stride explodes out of a pink speed-line burst, a corner caption box reads 'JOSH, AGE 14', and crop marks and colour bars fill the margins.

copy.headline: Episode 02: The State Level Arc
lines: Age 14. I tried to go pro.
WHRRRRR—
Roller skating. I reached STATE LEVEL.
Meanwhile, in the quietest sport alive… Yoga. Also state level.
THE HAUL: I won medals. 20–25 of them, combined.
Then life moved in another direction.
NEXT ARC →

concepts.tech:
No WebGL: 3D doesn't earn its place here. The world is DOM, SVG and Canvas 2D.

Pin and camera: GSAP ScrollTrigger pin (about 350vh, scroller '#scroll-container', pinType 'transform'). The 'camera' is a scale/translate on the page wrapper, targeting panel rects measured on resize.

Riso: each artwork is 3 inline-SVG ink layers (mix-blend-mode multiply) whose offsets come from shared noise plus Lenis velocity. Grain is a noise tile generated once (feTurbulence → canvas → blob URL). Halftones are CSS radial-gradients applied through mask-image. No live SVG filters run while scrolling, except during the impact frame.

Speed lines: Canvas 2D redrawn on twos (12fps), 140 lines on desktop and 50 on phones.

Panel shards: 9 precomputed clip-path polygons animated with translate3d/rotate3d.

Impact frame: CSS invert plus a feDisplacementMap boil re-seeded on twos. Phones swap 3 pre-baked boil frames instead.

Page curl: CSS 3D page halves with gradient shading.

Fonts: via next/font with the Latin subset.

Phones: the page reflows into a vertical webtoon strip, and the camera dives panel to panel vertically.

Reduced motion: a static, readable manga sequence in reading order, with no inversion flash, frozen speed lines and a fade instead of the curl.

Photosensitivity: one inversion per pass, never strobing.
concepts.risk: It lives or dies on illustration quality. It can tip into cringe pastiche or start to resemble a specific anime. Mitigation: silhouette-only figures plus one geometric eyes strip, type-led original SFX, no fake Japanese and no borrowed meme devices. Keep one hero (the panel break), with the Zen page as deliberate silence. Make fluoro inks plus speed lines its signature so it doesn't blur into the page's other paper-based worlds.

why: Laps Become Medals turns the visitor's own scrolling into Josh's training and strikes it into an engraved medal. That one 'how did they build that' hero belongs only to Josh and carries every fact: the skating laps, yoga on the reverse, and 20 + 5 honest receipts. It also turns 'another direction' into a literal tangent exit, and it is fully procedural with no illustration risk. The State Level Arc is louder and funnier, but it depends on genre pastiche and on the quality of hand-drawn art to land.

concepts.name: Tinsel Shockwave
concepts.oneLiner: The red-velvet cliché is swapped for a school-function stage dressed to the max (foil-fringe tinsel, marigold swags, neon rangoli), and the kid's 'MIC ON.' blasts a full-screen curtain of foil strips open. His voice is the force that starts the show.

palette.role: House-dark aubergine: background and hall
Foil magenta: main tinsel color, extrusion layer 1
Marigold: garlands, extrusion layer 2, confetti
Spotlight gold: beam, headline face, glints
Rangoli cyan: powder floor, tinsel accent, extrusion layer 3
Tally lime: the mic's LIVE light and stage directions (site accent)

concepts.typography: Shrikhand is the display face for 'MIC ON.' and the big beats. It's a fat, swashy italic with roots in Indian hand-lettering. Set it huge (about 22vw on desktop; stacked 'MIC / ON.' at about 30vw on phones) with a 10-layer extruded offset-shadow stack cycling magenta → marigold → cyan, like a hand-painted signboard. The letters light up one at a time like marquee bulbs (a brightness flicker, then hold), and the shadow stack pumps outward on every mic tap. Kalam, a handwriting face from Indian Type Foundry, is for the cue cards. Each line writes on with a clip-path 'pen' wipe, with a highlighter swipe behind the key word. Geist Mono (the site's own font) in lime caps carries the stage directions, such as [HOUSE LIGHTS: DOWN] and [PAUSE FOR APPLAUSE], and they blink like a teleprompter.
concepts.atmosphere: A deep aubergine hall with one volumetric follow-spot (layered conic and radial gradients, screen blend, dust drifting in the beam) and a procedural glitter grain that twinkles at random. Before the blast the frame holds exactly three things: darkness, one beam and the tinsel. Keeping it that bare is what lets the blast land. After the blast come a neon-powder rangoli floor in CSS-3D perspective, marigold swags overhead and fairy-light strings chasing down the wings. The ambient motion never stops: the tinsel breathes and twists, catching the beam. Over this world the site's custom cursor turns into a tiny follow-spot iris.
concepts.heroMoment: THE TINSEL BLAST. A full-bleed traveler curtain of foil strips (3 depth rows; about 1,200 strips on desktop, about 360 on phones) hangs closed, idly swaying and glinting. The pointer, or the scrolling thumb on phones, brushes through it, and the strips swing apart and flash. At about 35% scroll, the stand mic hidden behind the curtain taps twice: the strips shiver in sync, the frame dips 2px, and the mic's lime tally light glows through the gaps. Then 'MIC ON.' fires a radial shockwave from the mic. Each strip gets an impulse delayed by distance ÷ waveSpeed, so you see a ring travel outward over about 450ms while strips whip up, twist and flare through the whole palette in the spotlight. Behind the ring, the curtain's anchors ride the traveler track outward (scrubbed by scroll, so it reverses), bunching into two dense, still-swinging columns that frame the stage. On the same wave radius the rangoli lights up outward, and 'MIC ON.' slams up from the floor as the extruded signboard. The kid's voice literally blows the curtain open.
supporting: Gobo-projected copy: the early lines are 'projected' onto the tinsel. The strips sample a canvas texture of the text in screen space, so the words ride the fringe and break into slivers when you brush through or the strips twist.
Signboard headline: Shrikhand 'MIC ON.' with the 10-layer tinsel-colored extrusion, marquee-bulb light-up, and a pump on every mic tap.
Neon-powder rangoli floor: a seeded, 8-fold symmetric pattern under the mic that draws itself outward in step with the shockwave radius. The powder grit comes from feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap.

Marigold swags and fairy-light chase: verlet garlands of procedural pom-pom flowers whip with the blast and swing with scroll speed. Jhalar-style bulb strings (the baseline's marquee bulbs, evolved) chase faster the faster you scroll.
Cue cards: the facts arrive as an 11-year-old's handwritten index cards (Kalam) that drop into the light on strings, with stage directions in lime mono.
Applause made physical: foil-confetti cannons fire from the wings in proportion to scroll speed. The baseline's applause meter becomes actual confetti.
scrollBeats: 0–8%: The hero's stand-mic portal swells, and you dive into a black-aubergine hall. Title card: one follow-spot on the closed, glittering tinsel, a cue card dangling in the beam, the mic's tally light dark.

8–30%: Play. You brush the tinsel and the spot lazily follows. '[HOUSE LIGHTS: DOWN]' blinks, then 'Age 11. Somebody handed me a mic.' and the emcee opener are gobo-projected onto the strips and shatter as you brush.

30–42%: 'tap · tap'. Two thumps, and the tally light glows through the gaps. Then 'MIC ON.' and THE TINSEL BLAST: the traveler opens (scrubbed), the rangoli and fairy lights light up on the wave, and the headline slams in.
42–70%: The stage is revealed and the garlands swing. Cue cards drop one by one: 'Grade 6: school anchor.' → 'Grade 7: renewed for season two.' → 'Job description: talk until the next act is ready.'
70–88%: '[PAUSE FOR APPLAUSE]'. Confetti cannons fire from the wings in proportion to scroll speed, the fairy lights chase faster, and the spot tightens on the mic.
88–100%: The last cue card reads 'Please welcome our next act…'. The follow-spot pool on the stage floor contracts and morphs into the Sports icon silhouette, which becomes the portal. Dive.
concepts.portalIcon: A stage mic on a stand, upright and solid. Ball head (Ø 1.0) → short tapered clip → straight pole, thickened to about 0.16 head-widths so the mask stays readable → flat oval base (2.0 × 0.3). Make it one compound path. Scale the mask from the center of the ball head, so the round head reads first and the pole stretches the opening into a tall keyhole as it grows. The same mic then sits behind the curtain as the source of the shockwave.
concepts.titleCard: Darkness, and one gold follow-spot on a closed, glittering tinsel curtain that shivers as you arrive. A handwritten cue card dangles in the beam reading 'WORLD 01 — ANCHORING · AGE 11', and at the curtain's hem the mic's lime tally light sits dark. The room is waiting.

copy.headline: MIC ON.
lines: [HOUSE LIGHTS: DOWN]
Age 11. Somebody handed me a mic.
“Respected Principal, teachers and my dear friends—”
Grade 6: school anchor.
Grade 7: renewed for season two.
Job description: talk until the next act is ready.
[PAUSE FOR APPLAUSE]
Please welcome our next act…

concepts.tech:
Level 4–5a on the craziness ladder: one live WebGL material you can touch; everything else is DOM, SVG or Canvas 2D.

Scroll: the section is pinned for about 300vh with GSAP ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container'; pinType 'transform' for the non-root scroller). Lenis is ticked from gsap.ticker, with lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update).

Tinsel canvas: a lazy-loaded R3F chunk (next/dynamic, ssr:false), mounted by an IntersectionObserver one viewport early. It uses frameloop='never' with advance() called from gsap.ticker, so the physics, the scrub and the DOM all run on one clock (M2/M14). The canvas is transparent and layered over the DOM/SVG stage, so the stage and the tally light show through the gaps.

Tinsel build: one InstancedMesh of 1×16-segment planes. CPU springs (angle, velocity, twist) live in Float32Arrays and are pushed each frame as InstancedBufferAttributes. A ShaderMaterial bends each strip (curvature ∝ angle·(1−uv.y)²) and shades it as foil: a view-dependent specular band, a thin-film hue shift and a hash-noise sparkle. Rendering uses ACES filmic tone-mapping. Desktop gets bloom from three's own UnrealBloomPass; phones get additive sparkle sprites instead.

Shockwave: each strip gets an impulse delayed by distance/waveSpeed, fired once when the scroll threshold is crossed. The traveler opening is scrubbed, so scrolling back re-closes the curtain softly. Every beat uses a fast attack and a long settle (expo.out, about 1.1s).

Gobo text: a CanvasTexture sampled at gl_FragCoord.xy / resolution.

Everything else: garlands are Canvas 2D verlet chains (3 × 30 nodes) using a pre-rendered flower sprite. The rangoli is a seeded SVG generated once and revealed by stroke-dashoffset tied to the wave radius. Cue cards use Framer Motion springs. Confetti is Canvas 2D (60 pieces on phones, 220 on desktop).

Phones: about 360 strips, DPR capped at 1.5, no twist, no bloom, no powder filter, and the garlands become CSS-swayed SVG. The thumb's position while scrolling (passive touchmove) brushes the tinsel.

Perf guard: drop the sparkle and twist if frame time goes over 20ms.

Accessibility (M20): the canvas is aria-hidden, and all copy also exists as semantic DOM (sr-only where it is projected).

Reduced motion: no WebGL. Show a static SVG of the opened curtain as two shimmering bunches, with the headline and rangoli fully drawn and the cue cards as a readable stack. No shake, confetti or physics; the portal becomes a crossfade.
concepts.risk:
The biggest risk is decor overload drowning the one hero, plus tinsel physics on mid-range phones. To handle it:
- Sequence strictly: only the beam and the tinsel exist before the blast; the garlands, rangoli and lights enter after it, at reduced intensity.
- Tier the strip count by device, with a Canvas 2D fallback.
- Keep the perf guard.

A second risk: the school-function dressing (marigold, rangoli, fairy lights) and the 'Respected Principal…' opener assume an Indian school stage. Confirm that with Josh, and swap to generic carnival dressing if it's wrong. The copy never names an event or place.

concepts.name: Up To Eleven
concepts.oneLiner: Age 11, volume 11: the scroll is a volume knob wired to every pixel. Type swells from a whisper to a shout and ink floods blank paper one pass at a time, until the needle slips past a hand-scrawled '11' and 'MIC ON.' clips the entire page.

palette.role: Paper silence: the world at volume 0
Ink black: type, knob, mic
Ultramarine pass: waveform, linework, first halftone (vol 1–3)
Lime pass: vol 4–7 and the low VU segments (site accent)
Amber pass: vol 8–10 and the high VU segments
Clip red: the vol-11 flood, the CLIP rails, the marker '11'

concepts.typography: Anybody, a variable font (wdth 50–150, wght 100–900), is the instrument. Every line's width and weight are mapped to volume, so the copy literally goes from a whisper (wdth 50, wght 100, small lowercase) to a shout (wdth 150, wght 900, caps that fill the viewport). The emcee opener runs along the live waveform on an SVG textPath and gets fatter as the wave grows. Permanent Marker appears exactly once: the red '11 ← (me)' scrawled past the end of the knob's printed scale. Geist Mono (the site's font) handles the knob numerals, dB readouts, VU labels, the CLIP flags and a corner print slug that reads 'INK 0/4' at the start and climbs to '4/4'.
concepts.atmosphere: 'Loudness is ink': this world is a print run that gets louder. It opens on near-silent off-white paper with faint procedural grain (feTurbulence at about 4%) and print registration marks in the corners. Nothing exists that the volume hasn't printed yet. Each notch adds an ink pass: ultramarine linework and halftone at 1–3, lime at 4–7, amber at 8–10, and at 11 a red pass floods everything, slightly out of register. Giant concentric-ring speaker cones, cropped by the viewport edges, pump to an idle beat whose amplitude is the volume, and halftone 'sound-pressure' dots radiate from them. The waveform keeps breathing even at rest. The site cursor becomes a level dot that grows with the volume and turns red at the clip.
concepts.heroMoment:
THE CLIP. A GSAP detent makes the knob grind against the printed 10 for a stretch of scroll: it vibrates while the VU ladder flickers amber and red. Then it snaps past into the hand-scrawled 11, and everything happens in that frame:
- The red pass floods the paper.
- 'MIC ON.' is set in Anybody at wdth 150 / wght 900 and scaled about 1.35× taller than the 'headroom' band, so two hairline rails flagged CLIP slice it flat top and bottom. The letters look exactly like a clipped waveform.
- The full-width oscilloscope line squares off against the same rails.
- The halftone dots overgrow their cells and fuse into solid ink.
- The ultramarine, lime and amber passes jolt up to 8px out of register for 250ms, then snap back.
- The speaker cones punch forward, and four feedback rings (one per ink) radiate from the mic.
- The site's own frame buzzes and flashes red.
Then comes a dead 300ms freeze, and one tiny line types in: 'Age 11. Volume 11.'
supporting: The Knob: a chunky, generic amp-style knob (SVG, knurled edge, conic-gradient sheen) that is the scroll position. Its scale is printed 0–10 in Geist Mono, with a red-marker '11 ← (me)' past the end. It starts center-stage on the title card, then slides to the bottom-right corner as the world fills in.
Ink passes: halftone 'sound-pressure' fields where dot radius = volume × falloff from the cones. Each volume zone prints them in a new ink, until they fuse solid at 11.

Voice-shaped type: Anybody's width and weight track the volume. The opener “Respected Principal, teachers and my dear friends—” rides the waveform on a textPath, coming out of a small ink mic at center (the portal's silhouette, landed).
VU ladder as the world's progress bar: 12 LED segments going ultramarine → lime → amber → red, with mono dB labels (−∞ … 0 … +3 CLIP).
Fourth-wall buzz: from volume 9 the site's own rounded frame starts to jitter (1–3px), and at 11 its border flashes clip-red.

Open mic (opt-in): after the clip, a pill asks 'Your turn. Mic on?'. The visitor's real voice then drives the knob, type and ink through an AnalyserNode. It is processed on the device and never recorded or sent anywhere, and it stops automatically when the section scrolls off-screen.
scrollBeats: 0–6%: The hero's handheld-mic portal opens onto silence: off-white paper, a flat hairline waveform, the knob at 0 with its marker '11 ← (me)', and a whisper-thin 'is this thing on?'.

6–20% (vol 0→2): 'tap. tap.' Two spikes hit the line, each kicking the knob up a notch. The ultramarine pass prints its first specks, 'Grade 6: school anchor.' appears in thin condensed type, and the knob slides to its corner.

20–50% (vol 2→7): The voice finds its level. The opener rides the swelling waveform, the type widens and fattens, the cones slide in from the edges and start pumping, the lime pass prints and the VU ladder climbs.
50–68% (vol 7→10): The amber zone. 'Grade 7: encore.' then 'Inside voice: uninstalled.' The halftone fields bloom, the site frame starts to buzz and the knob grinds against the printed 10.
68–78% (vol → 11): THE CLIP. Red flood, flat-sliced 'MIC ON.', square wave, misregistration jolt, cones punching, feedback rings. Then a 300ms freeze → 'Age 11. Volume 11.'
78–92%: Open mic. The world holds at 11 but settles into a confident hum, and the 'Your turn. Mic on?' pill pulses. Talk, and the page answers.
92–100%: 'Please welcome our next act…' rides the waveform. The center cone's dust cap morphs into the Sports icon silhouette, and the camera dives through the speaker.
concepts.portalIcon: A handheld ball mic, upright. Ball head (Ø 1.0, with an optional thin grille-band notch) on a body tapering from 0.62 to 0.36 wide over 1.6 tall. Add two concentric sound arcs (about 0.16 thick, spanning about 60°) at its upper right, as separate solid paths. Stagger the mask so the arcs scale in about 120ms after the body; the 'sound' then seems to blow the portal open. The silhouette then lands as the small ink mic that emits this world's waveform.
concepts.titleCard: Silence on off-white paper: one flat hairline waveform across the screen, a small ink mic at its center, and a chunky black volume knob set to 0. Its printed scale stops at 10, with '11 ← (me)' scrawled past the end in red marker. Whisper-thin lowercase reads 'is this thing on?', with the mono label '01 — ANCHORING · AGE 11'.

concepts.tech:
Level 2–3 on the craziness ladder, with zero WebGL: DOM, SVG and one Canvas 2D. That lets the first world after the hero load instantly on phones.

Scroll: the section is pinned for about 320vh with GSAP ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container', pinType 'transform'). Lenis is ticked from gsap.ticker, so there is one clock (M14).

The volume value: the timeline tweens a single proxy {vol: 0→11} with a detent ease (a slow grind at 10, then an expo snap to 11). onUpdate writes CSS vars on the section root (--vol, --v from 0 to 1, --clip) plus the ink colors, interpolated in OKLCH in JS. The one-shot effects (the misregistration jolt, the freeze, the rings) fire from ScrollTrigger callbacks on the same ticker and reverse on scroll-back. Every beat uses a fast attack and a long settle (expo.out, about 1.1s).

Type: Anybody loads via next/font with the wdth axis. font-variation-settings is driven by --v, quantized to 0.25-notch steps inside contain: layout paint. Phones quantize to whole notches and fill the gaps with transform: scale.

Canvas 2D (DPR capped at 1.5) draws two things:
- the waveform: summed sines × volume, hard-clamped to the rails at 11;
- the halftone: about 2,400 dots on desktop and 700 on phones, batched into one path per ink.

The knob, VU ladder, cones, mic and rings are SVG with transforms.

The clip: an overflow-hidden headroom band with the type scaled past it. The misregistration is three ink-colored copies behind the black type, offset by up to 8px × --clip. The frame buzz is a CSS var on <html>, reset when the section is left.

Open mic: getUserMedia → AudioContext AnalyserNode RMS → smoothing → vol = max(scrollVol, voiceVol). It needs an explicit button press, stays local, has a stop control and stops automatically off-screen.

Optional opt-in sound effects are synthesized in WebAudio (two thumps, a filtered-noise roar at the clip) and fire from the same timeline (M15); there are no audio files.

Licensing: no amp-brand styling (no script logos, tolex or gold piping) and no film quotes; only the 'up to eleven' idiom.

Accessibility: all copy is real DOM text, and the canvas is aria-hidden.

Reduced motion: no jitter, jolt, pumping or frame buzz. Scroll steps between three still compositions (silence, mid, clip) with crossfades, and the end state is the static red clip poster with every line readable. The open mic only moves the knob and the VU ladder.
concepts.risk:
The joke has to land, and the quiet opening must not read as empty. Keep the silence under half a viewport with the first tap immediate, show the marker '11 ← (me)' from the title card onward, and pay it off at the climax ('Age 11. Volume 11.').

Other risks:
- Animating a variable font can stutter on phones; quantize the axis updates and contain layout.
- Clip-red could read as an error state; the four-ink feedback rings and the joke copy turn it into a celebration.
- The opener line assumes an Indian school stage; swap it if that's wrong.
- Mic access must stay strictly opt-in.

why: Up To Eleven is the stronger idea. It turns the headline into the whole mechanic: age 11 becomes volume 11, and one value driven by scroll prints, stretches and finally clips the entire world. Visitors can even turn their own mic on, and the clip climax is a hero no portfolio has done. It also needs zero 3D, so the first world after the hero loads instantly on phones, and it stays out of the podium-and-stage territory the MUN world will want. The tinsel stage is gorgeous, but at heart it is still a curtain reveal.

concepts.name: From My Angle
concepts.oneLiner: A candy-sunset voxel sky island sits inside a storm of 2,500 blocks that look random. As your scroll swings the camera around it, the chaos snaps into crisp block-letter words that can only be read from one exact viewpoint. From outside, Josh's obsession looks like noise. From his angle, it looks like a plan.

palette.role: Void indigo: the bottomless void, deep shadows, reduced-motion background
Ultraviolet: upper sky gradient, island rock voxels, ambient fill, caption plates
Sunset ember: horizon band, key/rim light, the glowing cube-sun
Wool magenta: alien grass tops, the voxel bed, BEDWARS lock color, and the 'ALMOST' that never locks
Diamond cyan: waterfall, SKYWARS lock color, crosshair and mining-crack glow
Gold ore: '~400' lock color, alignment rail fills, the white-gold heat of 'WENT COMPETITIVE.'

concepts.typography: Nabla (a Google Fonts COLRv1 isometric block color font) is used only for the giant title-card '16'. Its EDPT extrusion axis animates from 0 to max as the portal opens. Its EHLT edge-highlight axis flashes on every lock. A custom @font-palette-values swaps it to the active lock color. Under @supports not font-tech(color-COLRv1) it falls back to Silkscreen with a stacked text-shadow extrusion. Silkscreen 700 is drawn to an offscreen canvas and becomes the pixel source for every anamorphic voxel word, so the letterforms are original pixel glyphs and never a game font. Silkscreen also sets the HUD kickers ('WORLD 07 — MINECRAFT', 'BLOCKS MINED 007'). Pixelify Sans (variable 400–700) sets the readable captions at 18–20px on a 1px-bordered ultraviolet plate, bottom-left; its weight ticks from 400 to 700 as each word locks. The word MINECRAFT only appears as flat Silkscreen HUD text. It is never extruded or built from voxels, so nothing echoes the game's logo.
concepts.atmosphere: An original candy-sunset voxel dimension. It deliberately avoids the game's green-and-brown look: magenta grass, ultraviolet rock, cyan water. A shader sky dome runs from an ember horizon through ultraviolet to an indigo void, with a few square stars below the island. The sun is a huge, slowly tumbling emissive cube, with fake god-ray quads slicing through the block storm. Flat cuboid clouds drift at three parallax depths. A voxel waterfall pours off the island's edge into the void. A separate 'weather' layer of about 200 wind-blown cubes keeps the sky alive between locks and parts like a curtain at each vantage. Finish: ACES tone-map, bloom on emissive edges, fine grain and a vignette. There is no distance fog on word cubes, because fog would break the illusion. The whole grade swaps on each lock: hot magenta → cold cyan → a single RGB strobe → gold → white-hot.
concepts.heroMoment: THE SNAP: anamorphic voxel type. Each word (BEDWARS, SKYWARS, MONTAGES, ~400, ALMOST WENT COMPETITIVE.) is drawn in Silkscreen Bold to an offscreen canvas and thresholded into a bitmap about 8px tall. Each word owns a vantage pose C on the camera path. For every lit pixel: take its point P on an image plane d0 in front of C, pick a random depth factor k in [0.35, 2.4], place a cube at C + k·(P − C), scale it by k, and orient it to the vantage camera's axes. By similar triangles every cube's faces project to the same tile. From the vantage, about 200 cubes spread through 40m of sky read as one crisp, extruded block word. One step away, parallax shears it back into debris. The word cubes are static (apart from a tiny idle bob that fades to zero near their vantage); only the camera moves. Scroll drives the camera along a CatmullRom path with plateau easing, so it hits each vantage exactly and holds it for about 0.35 of a viewport of scroll. On lock, that word's cubes recolor to its lock color and pulse 1→1.06→1 in 120ms, a chromatic-aberration ping fires, and the DOM caption types in. Peak: from a high 'god vantage', 'WENT COMPETITIVE.' locks dead-still in white-gold. 'ALMOST' sits above it and never fully locks: its cubes keep a 2–4px screen-space tremble, done as an offset in the camera plane scaled by k. It is literally almost.
supporting: Mineable sky: inside the world the site cursor becomes a pixel crosshair. Hold on any floating block for about 350ms and a procedurally generated 3-stage crack spreads across it. Then it bursts into 8 mini-cubes that tumble into the void, and a Silkscreen HUD counter ticks up ('BLOCKS MINED 007'). Uses a raycast on the InstancedMesh (instanceId). On phones, tap to mine.

World reactions inside the scene: when BEDWARS locks, a bed-defense dome builds itself around the island's little voxel bed, layer by layer (magenta wool → cyan glass → ultraviolet stone). When SKYWARS locks, a bridge builds itself block by block off the island's edge into the void, one block per scroll tick.

Per-lock world re-grade (M24): each lock re-lights the whole dimension in its lock color through sky-dome uniforms, key-light color, bloom tint and the Nabla font-palette. Five locks feel like five micro-biomes inside one world.

Set dressing built entirely from code: a voxel waterfall into the void made of recycled instances, a tumbling emissive cube-sun with fake god rays, cuboid clouds at three parallax depths, and the wind-blown weather layer that parts at each vantage. During flights, the nearest blocks (k≈0.35) whip past the lens for speed.

Alignment rail (the baseline's XP bar and hotbar, evolved): five hollow isometric mini-cubes sit bottom-center, and each fills with its lock color when its word snaps. They are real buttons (aria-current, keyboard focus, :focus-visible) that scroll to their vantage, so they double as accessible navigation.
scrollBeats: 0–8% (section ≈350vh, sticky 100vh stage). PORTAL IN: the stepped sky-island silhouette from Moving Homes swallows the screen and we drop into a candy-sunset sky. Nabla '16' extrudes toward the camera (EDPT 0→max), with the kicker 'WORLD 07 — MINECRAFT' and the line 'Age 16. Obsessed with Minecraft.' Behind it, 2,500 blocks orbit the island as pure noise.

8–24%: the camera banks left around the island. Nearby blocks whip past the lens, the parallax slows, and the debris SNAPS into 'BEDWARS' (magenta lock, hot-pink grade). The bed-defense dome builds itself. Caption: 'Guard your bed. Break everyone else's.'

24–40%: dive beneath the island, past the stepped underside and the waterfall. Against the open void, 'SKYWARS' snaps (cyan lock, cold grade) while a bridge builds itself off the edge. Caption: 'Spawn on an island. Bridge over nothing. Don't look down.'

40–54%: climb back through the cloud layers. 'MONTAGES' snaps with an edit-style hit: a 1.06 zoom punch, an RGB split, and a single 2-frame RGB strobe of the grade. Caption: 'Made montages. Clipped the fights, cut them to the beat.'
54–68%: swing past the tumbling cube-sun. '~400' snaps in giant gold digits. Caption: '~400 YouTube subscribers. Small channel. Big montage energy.'

The biggest cloud locks white-gold: 'WENT COMPETITIVE.' holds dead-still while 'ALMOST' above it keeps trembling and never quite locks. Caption: 'Almost went competitive. The almost is doing a lot of heavy lifting.' Closer: 'From outside: a kid playing a block game. From my angle: the whole plan.'

88–100%: EXIT. The camera slides off-axis and every word shears back into noise. One last ring of blocks aligns into the hollow outline of the next world's icon (Startups), generated from the shared portal SVG path. Its interior hands off to the shared SVG mask, which scales up and dives us out.
concepts.portalIcon: A floating voxel sky island drawn only with right angles: a flat, wide grass slab on top (9 blocks wide), one chunky blocky tree (2×2 canopy on a 1-block trunk) on its left third, and an underside that steps inward in 4 stairs down to a single-block tip. It is one closed orthogonal path of about 24 vertices. It reads as 'sky island' at 24px and at 4000px, carries no game-specific detail, and has enough mass to fly through.

Behind the type, 2,500 colored blocks orbit the floating island as unreadable noise, which sets up the first snap.

concepts.tech: Level 5a: one live R3F scene, used where 3D genuinely earns it. Loading: the canvas is lazy-mounted with next/dynamic and an IntersectionObserver. It mounts one viewport early, switches to frameloop='demand' when offscreen, and unmounts after it leaves. Scroll: a 350vh section with a sticky 100vh stage inside #scroll-container. GSAP ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container', scrub) runs on the shared Lenis/GSAP ticker and writes progress to a ref, which useFrame reads. Cubes: one InstancedMesh (BoxGeometry, about 2,500 instances on desktop, about 1,100 on phones) with an onBeforeCompile material. Per-instance attributes are color, wordId and seed; uniforms uLock[6] and uTime drive the lock recolor, the pulse, the idle bob and ALMOST's tremble. Cube transforms are computed once on the CPU from Silkscreen bitmaps after document.fonts.load. They are regenerated (debounced) when the aspect ratio crosses portrait/landscape: portrait wraps words onto two lines, e.g. BED/WARS, and widens the vertical FOV. Generation uses rejection sampling so no cube occludes another word from its vantage, and k is capped so cubes sit in front of the island. Camera: a CatmullRom position path plus quaternion slerp, driven by a plateau-eased parameter (flat dwell segments with smootherstep between them) so every vantage is exact. The island, waterfall and weather layer share a second InstancedMesh, and the sky is one shader dome. Desktop post-processing: a single EffectComposer with Bloom, a ChromaticAberration ping, Noise and Vignette. Phones: no composer, DPR ≤1.5, no god rays, one cloud layer, a 60-cube waterfall, tap to mine. Reduced motion: no flight. The camera jump-cuts between parked vantages as each caption scrolls into view, so every word is perfectly aligned and nothing moves; the tremble is off and ALMOST renders steady in magenta. Accessibility: the canvas is aria-hidden, every fact is mirrored in a semantic <ol>, and the rail is made of real buttons. If WebGL fails, the words render as DOM Silkscreen text in their lock colors. Fonts load through next/font/google (Nabla with axes EDPT/EHLT, Silkscreen, Pixelify Sans).
concepts.risk: The anamorphic lock is unforgiving. Any mismatch in camera pose or aspect ratio turns a word into mush, and a fast scroller could fly straight past a vantage. Mitigation: positions are generated from the live camera aspect (and regenerated on resize). The plateau easing holds each word perfectly still for about a third of a viewport of scroll. Other clouds dim during a lock. Every word is also a DOM caption, so the story never depends on the illusion landing.

concepts.name: Velocity Edit
concepts.oneLiner: Josh's Minecraft era, cut as one of his own PvP montages. The section is an ultraviolet edit suite where your scroll is the playhead, until the beat drop time-remaps the scroll itself into bullet time and the whole site takes the hit.

palette.role: Edit-bay ultraviolet: UI background and panels (deliberately not the site's #0a0a0a)
Clip magenta: V1 clips, selections, title ghost echoes
Playhead cyan: playhead, beat waveform, velocity graph
Title yellow: title track, keyframe diamonds, slam type
Hit red: damage tint, REC dot, shake-frame flash tint
Sunset orange: the in-preview sky and void glow, which the monitor spills onto the UI

concepts.typography: Bungee Shade for the opening world title. Bungee for every title slam. Bungee Outline for the ghost echoes: outline-only copies that trail the shake by 2–3 frames, offset along the velocity. Martian Mono (variable wdth and wght) for timecodes, clip filenames and track labels; its wdth axis is bound to playback speed, so the timecode squeezes narrow in slow-mo and stretches wide at 4×. Silkscreen for the in-preview killfeed and HUD lines, so the game layer and the editor layer use visibly different type.
concepts.atmosphere: A deep-ultraviolet edit suite with a faint 1px grid. The large preview monitor's light spills onto the UI through a CSS var that holds the preview's average color, sampled from a downscaled canvas readback each time t changes. The preview gets scanlines and grain. Neon overlay layers fire from the FX track: procedural SVG lightning bolts, lens-flare quads and sparkle bursts. Letterbox bars wait at the screen edges, the REC dot pulses, and there is a vignette. Inside the preview is an original sunset sky-island voxel world.
concepts.heroMoment: THE DROP: a velocity edit applied to your scroll. Scroll progress maps to montage time through a monotone time-remap curve, drawn live as a velocity graph under the tracks. Approaching the DROP marker, the curve dives to about 0.15×. Every scroll tick now moves the playhead a sixth as far, so the scroll literally feels heavy, and the preview drops into bullet time. Josh's original blocky avatar, knocked off a sky island, hangs over the void while the camera orbits 180° past frozen arrows and debris. The UI desaturates, letterbox bars crush in, the Martian Mono timecode squeezes to its narrowest width, and 'ALMOST…' types onto the title track. Then he places a block under his own feet (the clutch) and the curve spikes to about 4×, so one flick covers four beats. On the kick: a trauma shake (trauma², decaying over about 600ms) on the R3F camera, the NLE stage AND the site's own frame border via a CSS var; an RGB split; a 1.08→1 zoom punch; ONE 60%-white flash frame; and 'WENT COMPETITIVE.' slams in under 'ALMOST…' in Bungee, with Bungee Outline ghosts trailing the shake.
supporting: The timeline tells the story. V1 clips are named like a real project folder ('bedwars_rush', 'skywars_bridge', 'clutch_FINAL_final_REAL'). V2 holds FX chips (SHAKE / RGB / ZOOM / FLASH) that light as they fire. V3 is the title track, and A1 is a procedural beat waveform. On entry, the clips drop onto the tracks with a block-place squash (back.out(1.7)).

Live velocity graph: the time-remap curve is drawn as an SVG bezier under the tracks from the same keyframes that drive the mapping, with a glowing dot riding it. Viewers can SEE why the scroll suddenly feels heavy, then weightless.
Killfeed of facts, top-right of the preview in Silkscreen: 'JOSH joined BEDWARS', 'JOSH joined SKYWARS', 'MONTAGE rendered', 'SUBSCRIBERS ~400', each line sliding in on a beat.

Export → upload outro: the timeline zooms out to show the whole edit, and an 'EXPORTING montage_FINAL_final_REAL' bar fills with scroll. Then a generic, unbranded video card's counter scrambles and settles on '~400 subscribers', never landing on any other number.
Razor cursor: over the timeline the site cursor becomes a blade. Clicking slices the nearest clip with a cyan spark and a 'CUT' stamp. It is a cosmetic toy and changes no state.

Opt-in sound behind a 'SOUND OFF' toggle. When on, a WebAudio-synthesized kick, snare and hi-hat fire whenever the playhead crosses a beat marker, forwards or backwards. Hits are low-passed and pitched down in slow-mo, with a full kick on the drop. Muted by default and nothing is preloaded.
scrollBeats: 0–8% (section ≈350vh, sticky 100vh stage). PORTAL IN: through the notched-block silhouette we land on a frozen preview frame. REC blinks, and the timecode reads 00:16:00:00. The NLE tracks slide up and clips drop in like placed blocks. Bungee Shade 'WORLD 07 — MINECRAFT' slams in with outline echoes. Line: 'Age 16. Obsessed with Minecraft.'

8–28%: playback at 1×. BEDWARS clip: the avatar sprints across a bridge to an enemy island, the camera cuts every second beat, and the bed bursts into cubes ('BED: GONE.' in the killfeed). The title track flashes BEDWARS.
28–42%: SKYWARS clip: a lone-island spawn, then speed-bridging over the void with a block placed on every hi-hat. Title: SKYWARS. Line: 'Bedwars. Skywars. One more game, every game.'

42–52%: MONTAGES clip, where the edit edits itself. Each FX chip on V2 fires on a beat and the preview gets exactly that treatment (shake, RGB, zoom, flash) as it is named. Line: 'Made montages: shakes, flashes, velocity, the works.'

52–72%: HERO, THE DROP. The velocity curve dives (scroll about 6× heavier) into a bullet-time orbit around the falling avatar through frozen arrows, and 'ALMOST…' types in. The clutch block appears, the curve spikes to about 4×, and the whole site shakes, with an RGB split, a zoom punch and one flash. 'WENT COMPETITIVE.' slams in under it.

72–90%: EXPORT. The timeline zooms out to the whole edit, the export bar fills, and the generic upload card settles on '~400 YouTube subscribers'. Line: 'Export complete. Saved as montage_FINAL_final_REAL.'
90–100%: EXIT. The razor cursor auto-traces the next world's icon (Startups) on the preview. The cut-out becomes the shared SVG portal mask and we dive through the monitor.
concepts.portalIcon: A chunky isometric voxel block (a pointy-top hexagon silhouette) with a stair-stepped bite mined out of its top-right edge. It is one closed path of about 14 vertices. The pixel-staircase bite separates it from a plain cube (such as a Rubik's silhouette) and reads as 'block mid-mining' at any size.
concepts.titleCard: Through the notched-block portal: a frozen preview frame of Josh's original blocky avatar (cube head with a wraparound cyan visor, not the game's default skin) mid-air over a sunset void. A REC dot blinks and the timecode reads 00:16:00:00. Bungee Shade 'WORLD 07 — MINECRAFT' slams in with magenta Bungee Outline echoes, then the NLE tracks slide up beneath it.
