concepts.tech: Level 5a-lite: R3F inside a DOM editor. Scroll: a 350vh section with a sticky 100vh stage in #scroll-container. GSAP ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container', scrub) runs on the shared Lenis/GSAP ticker and maps progress p to montage time t through a monotone cubic (Fritsch–Carlson) time-remap; the same keyframes render the SVG velocity graph. Preview: a lazy-mounted R3F canvas with a deterministic shot list. Every shot is a pure function of t (camera pose, avatar pose, props), so scrubbing backwards is exact, and frameloop='demand' + invalidate() renders only when t changes. The avatar is 6 boxes with procedural poses. The island, bridges, debris and bed burst are instanced cubes, and the arrows are thin boxes. Desktop: one EffectComposer (ChromaticAberration keyed to the FX track, Bloom, Noise, Vignette). Shake is trauma² noise on the camera plus a --shake CSS var read by the stage and, optionally, the site frame (transform only). NLE: DOM + Tailwind, with the track strip at translateX(−t·pxPerBeat) under a fixed centre playhead and Martian Mono's 'wdth' bound to dt/dp. Phones (375px): a 9:16 vertical preview, since current edit culture is vertical, with every shot authored with a portrait framing. Two tracks plus the velocity graph, no composer (CSS shake and flash only), DPR ≤1.5. Reduced motion: no scrub, shake or flash. Instead, a contact sheet of 6 frames rendered once from the deterministic scene, each captioned, ending on 'ALMOST WENT COMPETITIVE.' Photosensitivity: one flash only, at most 60% white, never 3 per second. Accessibility: the canvas is aria-hidden and all facts are mirrored in a semantic list. Fonts load through next/font/google (Bungee, Bungee Shade, Bungee Outline, Martian Mono, Silkscreen).
concepts.risk: This has the most moving parts of any world (editor UI, choreographed 3D, FX and optional audio), and an editor can read as 'video software' before it reads as 'Minecraft'. Mitigation: the preview owns at least 65% of the frame and opens on a voxel avatar over the void, and the NLE chrome stays thin and quiet. Build the deterministic shot list first; if time runs short, cut shots rather than polish.

why: From My Angle is stronger because the mechanic is the message: the obsession looks like random noise from outside and a clear plan from Josh's angle, and the honest punchline is built into the effect itself, since 'ALMOST' never quite locks. It is also the leaner, safer build (static instanced cubes, one draw call, only the camera moves, phone-friendly), while Velocity Edit risks reading as editing software before Minecraft and has the most moving parts on the page.

concepts.name: Stage Separation
concepts.oneLiner: One rocket built from Josh's three startups. Each stage is a startup's name, burns that startup's own receipts as exhaust, then blows its bolts and tumbles away so the next stage can fire.

palette.role: Launch tangerine: troposphere band, Stage 1 burn
Hot magenta: stratosphere band, Stage 2 burn
Ultraviolet: mesosphere band, Stage 3 burn
Void navy: space, fairing reveal, ink
Plume cream: rocket hull, exhaust core, type on dark
Site lime: telemetry, bolt flashes, 'nominal' ticks (ties back to the main site)

concepts.typography: League Gothic for the stage names, set vertically up each hull like aerospace livery. Its wdth axis squeezes from 100 to 75 under Max-Q and springs back the moment a stage separates, so the names look like they feel the G-force. Tilt Warp for the giant countdown numerals; its XROT/YROT axes are scrubbed so each number pivots toward you as it ticks. Martian Mono for telemetry and for the spec plates printed on the backs of the stages (wdth 75 during Max-Q, 112 at rest).
concepts.atmosphere: A 1970s sci-fi paperback cover come alive. The sky is hard-edged flat gradient bands, not photoreal. Paper-cutout clouds with offset hard shadows sit in three parallax depths, a huge flat sun sinks behind the pad, and 6% riso grain covers everything. Altitude rolls the bands past: tangerine troposphere, magenta stratosphere, ultraviolet mesosphere, then silent navy space with a pinprick starfield. Ambient motion: heat shimmer above the pad, drifting clouds, and a telemetry ticker crawling along the bottom edge.
concepts.heroMoment: THE STAGING SEQUENCE. A vertical rocket made of type stands centre-frame: three stacked SVG hull cylinders (cream, cylinder-shaded, riveted) whose bodies ARE the names. STARSCALE sits at the bottom, FRAGS N FLAVS in the middle, LAZYBULL on top, so the stack reads in chronological order from the bottom up; a fairing caps it. After liftoff the rocket holds at about 55% of viewport height while the sky scrolls past, and each stage owns one third of the remaining scroll. (1) Burn: a Canvas-2D plume of word sprites cut from THAT stage's facts (₹70K · 3 CLIENTS · SHIPPED) flows through a curl-noise field, heat-graded cream to tangerine to magenta. Emission rate equals Lenis scroll velocity. (2) At 85% of the slice, separation fires: a 120ms lime-white flash ring at the seam, about 10 debris shards, and a trauma-shake spike that decays as trauma². The spent stage first drifts away slowly, as real stages do, rotating 35–60° while a CSS-3D rotateY flip turns it to its stencilled spec plate ('STAGE 1 · STARSCALE · 2025 · HIGH-END ANIMATED WEBSITES · ₹70K ACROSS 3 CLIENTS · SHIPPED'). The plate stays readable for about 40% of the slice, then the stage accelerates out of frame (power2.in) and the plume words swap to the next stage's facts. Stage 3 (LazyBull, built in 2 days) goes supersonic before it separates: a vapour-cone collar and a boom ring. The whole sequence reverses: scroll up and the stages fly back and re-dock with a magnetic snap.
supporting: Stack = countdown: a crane lowers each stage onto the pad and it clanks home (squash + dust puff), ticking a Tilt Warp numeral taken straight from the facts. T–3 '3 clients', then T–3 '3 months' (it stutters, captioned '(yes, two threes)'), then T–2 '2 days', then T–1 '1 kid' as the fairing caps the stack.

Receipt exhaust: the plume is made of the burning stage's own facts (₹70K, 3 CLIENTS, SHIPPED, then ₹42K, 3 MONTHS, LIVE + SOLD IRL, then 2 DAYS, FOR SALE). Scrolling back up fires comic retro-rockets.
Altitude chapters: each sky band carries a 30vw outlined label that slides past like a mile marker: TROPOSPHERE · STAGE 1, STRATOSPHERE · STAGE 2, MESOSPHERE · STAGE 3.

Mission patches (these replace the holo cards): each separation sews an original embroidered patch onto a jacket-sleeve strip docked bottom-left. The satin-stitch border is drawn with a dashed-stroke animation, and a thread-sheen gradient follows pointer or gyro.

Max-Q + supersonic: every separation spikes a decaying shake, with RGB-split on the type and the League Gothic squash. LazyBull's stage breaks the sound barrier with a Prandtl-Glauert vapour cone before it drops.

Downlink ticker (this replaces the LED marquee): a Martian Mono strip whose statuses flip like a state machine: STG1 STARSCALE ▸ SHIPPED ✓ · STG2 FRAGS N FLAVS ▸ LIVE + SOLD IRL ✓ · STG3 LAZYBULL ▸ FOR SALE ◎.
scrollBeats: 0–10%: Arrival through the rocket-shaped portal. Dusk pad, an empty gantry with 'Then I started building.' stencilled up its spine, flat tangerine sky, heat shimmer.
10–30%: The stack is the countdown. STARSCALE is craned in (T–3 · 3 clients), then FRAGS N FLAVS (T–3 · 3 months, stutter), then LAZYBULL (T–2 · 2 days), then the fairing (T–1 · 1 kid).
30–38%: Ignition. Gantry arms swing away, the pad flashes, the word plume erupts, liftoff; the sky starts rolling.

38–56%: Stage 1 STARSCALE burns through the tangerine troposphere, then separates. It tumbles to its spec plate (2025 · high-end animated websites · ₹70k across 3 clients · shipped) and patch 1 sews on.
56–74%: Stage 2 FRAGS N FLAVS burns through the magenta stratosphere, then separates. Spec plate: Jan–Mar 2026 · premium instant gifting · ₹42k in 3 months · live + sold IRL. Patch 2 sews on.

74–90%: Stage 3 LAZYBULL goes supersonic (vapour cone, boom ring, Max-Q squash), then separates into ultraviolet and on into silent navy space. Spec plate: 2026 · AI-simplified trading · built in 2 days · for sale. Patch 3 sews on.
90–100%: Silence. The fairing opens like a clamshell; the payload is the next world's icon, glowing. 'Payload: the next obsession.' Dive.
concepts.portalIcon: A stocky three-stage rocket drawn as one closed path: ogive nose cone, three stacked hull segments marked by shallow V-notches on both edges (the stage seams), two swept fins, and a three-tongue flame tail. No inner holes. It reads at 24px and stays bold at full screen.

concepts.tech: Level 2–3 with no WebGL. R3F is never loaded in this world, which leaves GPU budget for the worlds that need 3D. One pinned ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container', pinType 'transform', scrub 0.8, about 4vh) owns a master GSAP timeline. Each separation is a nested, labelled sub-timeline, so the whole sequence scrubs and reverses (M2). The rocket is inline SVG: gradient-shaded hulls, rivet patterns, vertical text. Separations use CSS 3D (perspective 900px, rotateY flip to the spec-plate face). The sky is one tall CSS gradient strip translated by progress, plus three SVG cloud layers parallaxed by depth. The plume is one Canvas-2D layer (DPR capped at 1.5) drawing pre-rasterised word sprites from an offscreen atlas with 'lighter' compositing: about 400 particles on desktop, 120 on mobile, moved by cheap curl-noise. Everything ticks on the shared Lenis RAF (M14), and an IntersectionObserver pauses the canvas when it is offscreen. Mobile: rocket 62vh tall, one cloud layer, patches inline under the rocket, no RGB split. prefers-reduced-motion: no pin. Instead a static 70s-poster composition shows the rocket mid-separation, three labelled stage callouts carrying every fact, all three patches sewn on, and the legend '3 · 3 · 2 · 1'; the portal becomes a crossfade. Each stage's facts also sit in a semantic <article> for screen readers, and the canvas is aria-hidden (M20).
concepts.risk: The rocket is the most overused startup symbol there is. Make it clearly Josh's: the hull is built from his startups' names, the countdown from his own numbers, and the exhaust from his receipts. Commit to flat 70s-paperback art rather than glossy stock 3D. Two smaller risks: too many beats in about 4vh, and tumbling plates that are hard to read. Fold the stacking into the countdown, give each plate a slow first drift, and keep the telemetry ticker as a record of the facts that is always readable.

concepts.name: The Receipts
concepts.oneLiner: The page promises 'Not a résumé. Just the receipts.', so this world prints them: a live thermal receipt feeds out as you scroll, gets stamped, gift-wrapped and price-gunned, then is torn off and flung at the camera.

palette.role: Thermal paper: the hero surface, the one calm thing on screen
Receipt ink: print, stamp shadows, final field
Day-glo orange: arrival field + price-gun stickers
Riso blue: StarScale flood (star-shaped halftone)
Fluoro pink: Frags n Flavs flood + satin ribbon
Site lime: LazyBull flood (up-arrow halftone) + print-head glow (ties back to the main site)

concepts.typography: Doto (dot-matrix, variable; fallback DotGothic16) for receipt headers and amounts. Its ROND axis turns square dots round as each line burns in. Space Mono at 13–15px for line items, with dotted leaders, so they stay legible at 375px. Rubik Mono One for the rubber stamps, distressed by an SVG displacement filter that uses a fresh seed on every slam. Anybody for 40vw background overprints; its wdth axis snaps from 50 to 150 on every stamp impact.
concepts.atmosphere: A risograph print shop at full volume: flat ink fields with heavy paper grain, halftone dot screens, two-ink misregistered overprints, rubber-stamp ink bleed. The white receipt is the only calm surface, and it casts a soft contact shadow onto the colour field. Ambient motion: the slot glows and dims like breathing, halftone dots drift and rotate almost imperceptibly, a thermal shimmer hangs over the print head, and stray price stickers flutter past.
concepts.heroMoment: THE LIVE PRINTOUT. A fat, glowing printer slot spans the bottom edge of the viewport, and a thermal receipt (84vw on phones, 440px on desktop) rises out of it. Scroll drives the paper feed, scrubbed inside a pin of about 3.5vh, with short holds while stamps land. The receipt is about 44 real DOM rows in a preserve-3d column. Every frame, each row's rotateX/translateZ comes from a damped spring chain anchored at the slot. Scroll velocity sends a wave travelling up the paper, and a hard flick whips the free top end like a party streamer. The angle is clamped to ±28° and settles flat while a block is being read. Per-row shading runs off a CSS variable and the paper casts a soft contact shadow, so it reads as real curling paper while the text stays crisp and selectable. Rows print at the slot: a clip-path sweep runs left to right behind a 2px lime-hot print head, and the ink darkens from 30% grey to full black like thermal paper. Finale: the barcode prints and a red laser sweeps it ('BEEP.'). The paper rips at the slot along a jagged zigzag clip-path, springs up 30px, then flips toward the camera (rotateX −70° to 0, plus translateZ until it fills the viewport). It becomes the white sheet that the next world's portal is punched through.
supporting: Stamp slams: SHIPPED (StarScale), LIVE + SOLD IRL (Frags n Flavs) and FOR SALE (LazyBull) drop from off-camera at 1.6× and slam to 1× with a back.out overshoot, a random tilt of up to ±8°, ink spatter and a 90ms decaying shake. The ink texture uses a new SVG-turbulence seed every time, and a stamp never covers a number.

Halftone shockwaves: one full-screen fragment shader sits behind the receipt. Each stamp sends halftone dots out from its impact point that recolour the world: riso-blue STARS for StarScale, fluoro-pink BOWS for Frags n Flavs, lime UP-ARROWS for LazyBull. A second ink plate offset by 6px gives the riso misregistration.

Gift-receipt gag (Frags n Flavs): a satin ribbon wraps the receipt and ties a bow, a 'GIFT RECEIPT' tag flips over, and a black bar hides the amount. Then the bar slides off: 'kidding: ₹42k in 3 months.'

Turbo print + swing tag (LazyBull): the print head runs 6× faster for 'built in 2 days', with motion-blurred rows, speed lines and a whipping paper. A day-glo FOR SALE swing tag drops on a string and swings on a damped pendulum driven by scroll velocity.

Price-gun cursor: the site cursor becomes a price-tag gun. Each click or tap slaps a day-glo sticker carrying a real fact (₹70K, 3 CLIENTS, ₹42K, 3 MONTHS, 2 DAYS, SHIPPED, FOR SALE) anywhere in the world. Maximum 24; the oldest peel off.
Overprint type: behind the paper, 40vw words in two misregistered inks (SHIPPED. / SOLD IRL. / FOR SALE.) whose Anybody wdth axis snaps from 50 to 150 on each impact.
scrollBeats: 0–8%: Arrival. The receipt-shaped portal match-cuts into the real paper rising from the slot on a day-glo orange field. The header prints in Doto: *** THE RECEIPTS *** / THEN I STARTED BUILDING. / AGE 17 · 2025–2026 · CASHIER: JOSH. Overprint behind it: 'YOU WANTED RECEIPTS?'
8–32%: STARSCALE · 2025 prints (high-end animated websites / 3 CLIENTS ……… ₹70K). The SHIPPED stamp slams, a blue star-halftone shockwave floods the world, and 'SHIPPED.' stretches behind the paper.

32–58%: FRAGS N FLAVS · JAN–MAR 2026 prints (premium instant gifting / 3 MONTHS ……… ₹42K). A ribbon wraps it and ties a bow, turning it into a GIFT RECEIPT. The price bar hides the amount, then slides off ('kidding'). The LIVE + SOLD IRL stamp lands and a pink bow-halftone flood follows.
58–80%: LAZYBULL · 2026 prints in TURBO (AI-simplified trading / BUILD TIME ……… 2 DAYS). The paper whips, the FOR SALE swing tag drops and swings, and a lime up-arrow flood follows.
80–92%: The footer prints (ITEMS: 3 · THANK YOU. VISIT AGAIN.), then the barcode. A red laser sweeps it: 'BEEP.'
92–100%: The tear. A jagged rip at the slot, the receipt flips toward the camera and fills the screen white, the next world's portal is punched through the paper, and you dive.
concepts.portalIcon: A receipt slip drawn as one closed path: a tall rectangle with softly rounded top corners and a bold 5-tooth sawtooth tear along the bottom edge, like the 🧾 glyph. No inner holes. It match-cuts straight into the real paper rising from the slot.
concepts.titleCard: A day-glo orange riso field with a fat glowing printer slot across the bottom edge. A strip of thermal paper rises out of it, the print head mid-sweep on '*** THE RECEIPTS ***' and then 'THEN I STARTED BUILDING.' Behind it, a 40vw misregistered overprint: 'YOU WANTED RECEIPTS?'

concepts.tech: Level 2–3: mostly DOM, with exactly one shader. One pinned ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container', pinType 'transform', scrub 0.6, about 3.5vh) owns a master GSAP timeline (M2). Paper feed, per-row print sweeps and the stamp, flood and ribbon cues are all labels on it, so everything scrubs and reverses. Lenis velocity drives the spring chain and the swing-tag pendulum on the same shared RAF (M14). The receipt is semantic DOM: an <ol> of rows plus a visually hidden summary, with about 44 per-row transforms on desktop. Mobile pairs the rows (22 transforms) and halves the amplitude. The floods are one full-screen fragment shader on a raw WebGL2 quad of about 60 lines, so three.js is not needed. It runs at 0.5–0.75 DPR, renders only during each flood of about 900ms, then freezes; without WebGL it falls back to a CSS radial-gradient halftone swap. Stamps, ribbon, tag and barcode are SVG + GSAP; the barcode is decorative bars generated from a hash. Stickers are capped at 24. The price gun appears only on (pointer: fine); touch gets tap-to-sticker with a movement threshold so it never fights scrolling. prefers-reduced-motion: no pin, billow or floods. The full receipt renders already printed, stamped, gift-wrapped and tagged on a static halftone field, and the portal becomes a crossfade. All decoration is aria-hidden, and an IntersectionObserver pauses everything offscreen.
concepts.risk: Paper can read as dull admin, or as a money flex. To counter that, the receipt is the only calm surface and every block sets off a full-screen colour flood. The voice stays self-aware ('You wanted receipts?', 'kidding', 'Thank you. Visit again.'). Amounts print exactly as given, with NO computed total; the only total is ITEMS: 3. Across worlds: if JEE goes for an exam-paper look, keep this one on thermal dot-matrix and riso ink floods (no ruled sheets, no pencils) so the two never echo each other. Legibility: the billow settles flat whenever a block is on screen.

why: The Receipts is the less expected idea and the one only Josh could own: it pays off the page's own promise ('Not a résumé. Just the receipts.'), turns the facts themselves into the hero object, and is built mostly in DOM and suits phones. Stage Separation is a great spectacle, but it rests on the most overused symbol in startups.

world: #6 MOVING (age 15): 5 homes in 3 years. The quiet, melancholic, warm chapter between MUN (#5) and Minecraft (#7).

concepts.name: One Box, Five Windows
concepts.oneLiner: Drop the map and the van: one cardboard box IS the room. Every home cuts a new window into it and tapes the last one shut, until, in the dark, the box becomes a stained-glass lantern of colored tape that throws all five homes across the walls.

palette.role: Kraft: the box and every surface (the room at night drops to umber #17110B)
Bulb amber: the lamp, Home 05's open window, the gloss on packing tape
Tomato tape: Home 01 (its dot sticker, light grade, window patch and projection)
Painter's-tape blue: Home 02
Mint tape: Home 03
Hot-pink tape: Home 04

concepts.typography: Big Shoulders Stencil Display, Black (fallback: Saira Stencil One), is for the giant words and numbers ('5 HOMES', '3 YEARS', 'HOME 03'). They are spray-painted into the back wall's texture through a stencil: a noise-threshold reveal with overspray speckle and a sputter as each letter starts. Permanent Marker is the Sharpie on the box. It writes on with a clip reveal that follows a marker-nib dot, and each old line is struck through with a wobbly hand-drawn SVG scribble (stroke-dashoffset) before the next line writes. Anton, in repeated caps, is printed along the tape ribbons and slides as the tape unspools. Space Mono is for the shipping label and the HUD ('HOME 03 / 05'). Ink is Sharpie black #141110, never pure black.
concepts.atmosphere: A warm, dark room (#17110B): a pale floorboard plane fading to black, a plain back wall, and the box as the only lit object, so the plain room frames the spectacle. The kraft is generated in code: a CanvasTexture built at runtime from layered noise, fiber specks and soft dents, and every cut edge shows the corrugated flutes. Tape is see-through, with generated wrinkles and a shiny streak. Each home gets its own light through its new window, with a per-home color grade (M24): 01 warm tomato morning, 02 blue noon, 03 mint-grey rain, 04 pink dusk, 05 amber night. A fake light shaft with dust motes sits in each beam. The camera has a subtle handheld breathing motion (M23), headlight sweeps cross the walls during moves, and there is film grain and a vignette.
concepts.heroMoment: THE TAPE LANTERN. Night falls. A bare bulb on a cord drops in through the flaps and clicks on. The box now has five windows: Homes 01–04 are taped over in tomato, blue, mint and pink, each with its number written in Sharpie on the tape, and Home 05 is still open and faces the back wall. Every window throws its own colored light shape, in correct perspective, across the floor and back wall, and the Sharpie numbers show up as shadow letters inside the beams. The bulb is a live damped pendulum, pushed by pointer speed on desktop and by dragging the cord or by scroll speed on phones, so all five projections swing, stretch and skew together like a real lantern. Build: every frame, project each window polygon from the bulb's world position onto the floor plane and the back-wall plane (ray-plane intersection, then a Sutherland–Hodgman clip where floor meets wall). Fill each result with an 8×8 subdivided grid mesh whose UVs come from window-local coordinates, so the projected texture (window bars, tape wrinkles, Sharpie number) stays in correct perspective. Use additive blending, a soft-edge falloff and bloom. The room is lit ONLY by these five meshes, which keeps the colors pure. The quote is real DOM text sitting inside the amber Home 05 patch: each frame, a CSS matrix3d homography is solved from that patch's four screen-space corners. It reads as projected light but can still be selected and read by screen readers.
supporting: Sharpie palimpsest: the box's label is rewritten once per home: 'JOSH — ROOM' → 'JOSH — ROOM (AGAIN)' → 'STILL JOSH — ROOM' → 'JOSH — ROOM v4' → 'JOSH — ROOM (FINAL) (FINAL)'. Each old line is scribbled out live before the next one writes on.

Every move uses a different fold, so the loop never repeats. 01→02: hop and tumble. 02→03: the box flattens into its cross-shaped unfolded template (the dieline), glides across the floor like a sheet of paper, then folds back up. 03→04: it lands upside down with its 'THIS SIDE UP ↑' arrows pointing at the floor, holds a beat, then grumpily hops itself upright. 04→05: the camera pulls back to show it as one box in a tower of identical boxes.

Packing-tape ribbons: full-width diagonal strips of see-through printed tape ('FRAGILE • THIS SIDE UP • HANDLE WITH CARE') whip across the screen every time the box is sealed, crinkled by an SVG displacement filter and finished with a jagged torn end.

The cut: in this world the cursor turns into a snap-off blade. Each new window is traced as a dashed line and then sliced, and the cardboard cutout punches inward and falls. That home's light floods in along with a burst of foam packing peanuts (instanced meshes, simple physics).
Dot-sticker HUD: movers' color-code stickers slap onto the box with squash-and-stretch, one per home in that home's color. A 5-dot progress rail in the frame's corner mirrors them.
Pop-up furniture: flat cardboard cut-outs of a bed, a desk and a lamp hinge up from the box floor like a pop-up book on every unpack and fold flat on every pack.
scrollBeats: 0–6%: The portal drops us straight down INTO the open box. Kraft walls rush past, and the box floor is the title card.

6–16%: HOME 01. The camera rises out through the flaps to a low 3/4 view. The blade cuts the first window and tomato morning light floods in. Pop-up furniture hinges up, '5 HOMES' and then '3 YEARS' are spray-stenciled onto the back wall, and the label writes 'JOSH — ROOM'.

16–28%: → HOME 02. The flaps snap shut (short pair, then long pair, with back.out overshoot). The tape gun zips the seam while tape ribbons whip across the screen, and window 01 gets a tomato tape patch. The box hops and tumbles through headlight streaks and lands. The tape is sliced, a blue noon window is cut, peanuts burst, the label adds '(AGAIN)' and sticker 02 goes on.
28–40%: → HOME 03. The flatten-and-glide fold: unfold to the template, glide, fold back up. Mint rain-light window; 'STILL JOSH — ROOM'.
40–52%: → HOME 04. It lands upside down, holds a beat, then rights itself. Pink dusk window; 'JOSH — ROOM v4'.
52–62%: → HOME 05. Pull back to the box tower, then push back in. Amber window; 'JOSH — ROOM (FINAL) (FINAL)'. Each cycle runs shorter than the one before.

62–88%: HERO, the Tape Lantern. Lights out, the bulb drops, and five colored projections bloom across the floor and wall. The quote is projected inside the amber patch, one line at a time: 'Some years weren't about winning anything.' then 'Some years were just about adjusting.' The swing is free to play with here.

88–100%: Exit. The blade comes back and cuts one last shape into the front wall: World 7's icon (for example, a chunky voxel cube). The cutout falls inward, World 7's light blasts out through the hole, and we dive through it.

concepts.titleCard: Looking straight down into the box: four kraft walls lead down to the floor, where 'MOVING' is stenciled huge, 'age 15' is scrawled in Sharpie, a tomato dot sticker reads '01', and a strip of tape says 'THIS SIDE UP ↑' with the arrow pointing right at you.

concepts.tech: Craziness level L5a: one live object. A single lazy-loaded R3F <Canvas> (next/dynamic, ssr:false) mounts when the world is within one viewport, renders only while visible, and unmounts after the exit. The box is built in code, no GLB: a floor, 4 hinged walls and 4 hinged flaps. Walls are ExtrudeGeometry (3mm of corrugated thickness) from a THREE.Shape with all five window holes already cut; 'plug' meshes fill the windows that haven't been cut yet and animate out when they are. Tape patches are thin see-through planes. All textures are CanvasTextures drawn at runtime: kraft noise, the Sharpie label (redrawn per home with the loaded font after document.fonts.ready), and the stencil spray on the back wall. One GSAP master timeline, with a label per home, is pinned and scrubbed by ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container', lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)). On a single gsap.ticker it drives the wall and flap hinges, the camera, the per-home light grade AND the DOM layer (tape ribbons, HUD, quote) (M2/M14). In the lantern scene, a short-range PointLight makes the inside of the box glow, and the room is lit only by the projection meshes. The pendulum is a damped spring updated on the same ticker. Performance: device pixel ratio capped at [1, 1.5] on desktop and [1, 1.25] on phones. An EffectComposer (bloom, vignette, grain) runs on desktop only; phones get a CSS radial glow instead. Peanuts are capped at 60 (20 on mobile) and dust motes at 150 (40 on mobile). At 375px the box sits at about 70vw, the back wall above it holds the amber patch and the quote, and projections are kept inside the frame. Reduced motion: no pinning, scrubbing or swing. The finished lantern renders once, the quote stays as plain DOM, and a static list of five color swatches, 'HOME 01–05', replaces the sequence. The canvas is aria-hidden, with a parallel semantic DOM (h2, ordered list of homes, blockquote) (M20).
concepts.risk: Biggest risk: it is still 'a moving box', the expected metaphor. Four seal-tumble-cut loops can start to feel like a screensaver, and a cube-shaped hero shares the page with the Rubik's and voxel worlds. Mitigation: every move uses a different fold, each cycle runs shorter than the one before, and the camera stays low and cinematic at human scale (never isometric), with soft tape and kraft materials in warm light. All the payoff is saved for the lantern so the box earns its ending. Also stay well away from the cozy pixel-art look of games about unpacking.

concepts.name: Repotted
concepts.oneLiner: Moving homes as being uprooted: a sprout is lifted out of five house-shaped pots, droops from transplant shock every time, and regrows to fill each new shape. When the soil finally falls away, its root ball holds all five homes nested inside it like tree rings.

palette.role: Loam: the soil cross-section and background
Terracotta: Home 01 roots and pot, warm UI
Orchid: Home 02 roots and glaze
Majolica cobalt: Home 03 roots and glaze
Jade: Home 04 roots and glaze, plus the leaves
Root glow: Home 05, live root tips, all type

concepts.typography: Fraunces is the display voice: a variable font with wght, SOFT, WONK and opsz axes, loaded via next/font. It is set at 900 weight, SOFT 100, opsz 144, so it reads chubby and warm. The quote is in Fraunces Italic. The type gets transplant shock too. After every uproot the headline slumps: wght eases from 900 to 350, SOFT rises, and each letter sags and tilts along a drooping baseline. Letters sit in fixed-width spans, so animating the weight never reflows the line. The headline recovers and stands upright as the new roots take hold, on the same clock as the leaves. When it first appears, the headline is grown: roots fill the letter shapes before the solid fill fades in. DM Mono is for the plant-tag print and the HUD ('HOME 03 / 05'). Caveat is for the handwritten marker notes added to the tag.
concepts.atmosphere: A full-screen cross-section of soil, like a terrarium sliced open. Deep loam with soil layers and perlite and pebble specks generated from canvas noise, re-tinted for each home. Above it, a thin strip of sky changes with each home: coral dawn, cobalt noon, grey-blue rain, orchid dusk, night. The pots are glossy glazed ceramics shown in cutaway (SVG with layered gradients and a highlight streak), filled with soil up to the roof, with the stem coming out through the chimney. The roots are the light source: filament-bright tips with an additive glow that slowly breathes, while older roots are thicker and dimmer, like heartwood. Ambient motion: drifting soil specks, a slow 1–2px parallax between soil layers, leaves swaying, film grain. The camera eases out as the pots get bigger.
concepts.heroMoment: THE ROOT RINGS. After Home 05 the pot splits along a vertical seam, both glazed halves fall away, and the soil crumbles off in a slow cascade. What's left floating in the dark is the root ball. Inside it, traced by the roots that ran around each pot's walls, five nested house shapes light up from the center outward: terracotta (01), orchid (02), cobalt (03), jade (04), cream (05), like tree rings made of houses. The quote sets in the middle, one line at a time. Hover or tap a ring to isolate it with the label 'HOME 0N'. Build: one root-growth engine using space colonization, run per pot at build time with a fixed random seed. Attractor points are Poisson-sampled inside the new area (pot N minus pot N−1), plus a dense band just inside pot N's walls. That band makes roots run along the wall, and it is what becomes the ring. Growth starts from the root tips on the edge of the previous root ball. Settings: influence radius about 50, kill distance about 7, step about 5, with a downward bias. Each node stores x, y, parent, birthT, homeIndex, a wall flag and a pipe-model radius (so roots taper naturally). Scroll position sets a time t, and every segment with birthT ≤ t is drawn, so growth scrubs perfectly forwards and backwards. Each finished home is drawn once to its own offscreen layer, which keeps per-frame cost low and means isolating a ring is just a layer's opacity. The reveal brightens the wall-flagged segments one home at a time.
supporting: Root-grown headline: '5 homes in 3 years.' takes root. After document.fonts.ready, the Fraunces letters are drawn to an offscreen canvas on the main thread, attractor points are sampled from them, and a Web Worker runs the same growth engine on those points. Roots fill the letters, then the solid type fades in underneath.

Transplant shock you can see: every uproot makes the leaves droop and turn grey AND makes the headline slump. Both perk back up in exact proportion to how much new root has grown, which turns 'adjusting' into an animation you scrub.

The uproot: the pot drops away beneath the plant, and the house-shaped root ball is left hanging intact. Soil rains off as particles and a few fine root tips snap and spin away. Each pot leaves differently: one falls into the dark, one shatters into glazed shards, one slides out sideways like a drawer.

Plant-tag HUD: a plastic plant tag pushed into the soil carries the world's info: 'JOSHMANN SINGH · AGE 15 · Hardy. Tolerates relocation.' plus 'HOME 03 / 05'. Handwritten Caveat notes are added for each home ('Drooped. Adjusted.'). The tag wobbles after the pointer with a soft lag (M1).

Five house-shaped glazed pots: gable, tall and narrow, wide, flat roof, double gable. They are generic house shapes, not portraits of the real homes. Each is bigger than the last so the old root ball always fits inside, and each new pot rises from below to catch the hanging plant.

Exit: the camera sinks beneath the root ball and the soil grain pixelates into chunky loam-colored cubes (an original look, not any game's dirt texture). The cubes stack into World 7's icon, which becomes the portal mask.
scrollBeats: 0–7%: The house-and-sprout portal opens onto the soil cross-section. The title card holds, and the plant tag springs up out of the dirt with a back.out overshoot.

7–18%: HOME 01, the terracotta gable pot. The sprout unfurls, and roots grow down, branch, hit the walls and run around them. '5 homes in 3 years.' grows out of roots in the soil behind the pot, then fills in solid.

18–26%: First uproot. The pot drops away and the root ball hangs there: a perfect little terracotta house. Soil cascades, root tips snap, the leaves droop and the headline slumps. Caption: 'Roots remember the shape of every pot.'

26–38%: HOME 02. The orchid pot rises to catch the plant, soil pours in, and orchid roots push out from the terracotta house to the new walls. The leaves and the type recover, and the tag gets 'Drooped. Adjusted.'
38–50%: HOME 03, cobalt. This time the old pot shatters, the sky strip turns to rain, and the roots grow faster.
50–60%: HOME 04, jade. The plant hangs over an empty frame at dusk for a held beat (the in-between), then gets planted.
60–70%: HOME 05, cream glaze, the biggest pot. Roots fill it completely and the leaves come all the way up.

70–90%: HERO, the Root Rings. The pot splits and falls, the soil falls away, and five nested house rings light up from the center outward. The quote sets in the middle one line at a time: 'Some years weren't about winning anything.' then 'Some years were just about adjusting.'
90–100%: Exit. Sink into the soil; the grains pixelate into cubes that build World 7's icon; dive through it.

concepts.titleCard: A sliced-open soil cross-section in deep loam. Huge, soft Fraunces letters reading 'MOVING HOMES' in root-cream sit behind a small terracotta house-pot shown in cutaway, with a single sprout coming out of its chimney. The plant tag pokes up beside it: 'JOSHMANN SINGH · AGE 15'.
