concepts.tech: Craziness level L4, deliberately with no three.js: this is the quiet world, so it uses the lightest technique that does the job. Layers: DOM type (Fraunces variable font via next/font with axes ['SOFT','WONK','opsz']), SVG for the pots, plant and tag, and two Canvas 2D layers for roots and particles. One GSAP master timeline drives all of it, pinned and scrubbed by ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container' with Lenis) and read in a single gsap.ticker callback (M2/M14). Root data is precomputed by a Node build script: about 5k nodes on desktop and 2k on mobile, stored as binary Float32 arrays (about 100KB gzipped) and fetched only as the world approaches. Rendering: each finished home is drawn once to its own offscreen layer, and only the growing home's segments are drawn each frame, batched into Path2D by color and width. Tip glow is capped at 120 additive radial sprites. The uproot only moves the cached images, with no redrawing. Particles are capped at 150 on desktop and 50 on mobile; device pixel ratio is capped at 2 and 1.5. An IntersectionObserver pauses everything offscreen. At 375px the final pot is about 80vw wide, the headline stacks into three lines (with its own glyph sample points), tip glow is simplified, and the rings scale to fit. Reduced motion: no pinning or scrubbing. The finished state renders once: the five labeled nested root rings, the solid headline, the tag at 'HOME 05 / 05', and the quote. The canvas is aria-hidden, and the rings are focusable buttons in a parallel DOM list (M20).
concepts.risk: Biggest risk: a plant metaphor can slide into soft, cheesy 'growth journey' territory and feel less CRAZY than the worlds around it. Mitigation: make it literal and loud. Glossy house-shaped pots make 'home' read in under two seconds, roots glow like filament in saturated colors, the type physically slumps and recovers, pots shatter, and the plant-tag copy is funny. Also tune the generator (downward bias, the wall-following band, natural taper, a color per home) so the roots look grown rather than like a stock lightning or vein effect.

why: Repotted turns the chapter's own line, 'just about adjusting', into something you watch happen (transplant shock, then recovery), and it ends on an image nobody has seen before: five homes nested inside one root ball. It does this with a light 2D engine and gives the page a glowing, organic breather between the formal MUN world and the hard-edged voxel world, where a cardboard box would be the page's third cube, landing right before the voxel one.

concepts.name: Face Value
concepts.oneLiner: The page itself is the puzzle. What looks like a flat Swiss poster is really the top face of a building-sized picture cube, and its stickers carry this world's copy. Scroll shreds the words into a three-letter ransom note, then solves them back layer by layer, in reading order.

palette.role: Sticker white (grid-paper pattern): the opening poster and its flood
Sticker yellow (halftone dots): the first flood after the screen turns
Sticker red (zigzag pattern)
Sticker orange (grain-gradient pattern)
Sticker blue (pinstripe pattern)
Sticker green (checker pattern)

concepts.typography: Rubik Mono One for everything printed on the cube. It is a heavy monowidth caps face, set at exactly three characters per sticker, so every face is a 9-character x 3-line grid that slices cleanly into stickers. It is also a quiet in-joke: the Rubik family was first drawn for Google's Chrome Cube Lab. Tilt Warp for DOM labels and the move-notation ticker. Its XROT/YROT axes are scrubbed by the live turn angle, so the letters tilt along with the turning layer. The competition timer is a code-built SVG 16-segment LCD with no font, so it can spell words as well as digits. The DOM captions that mirror each locked band reveal three characters at a time, echoing the sticker grid. Geist Mono stays for tiny site-chrome meta.
concepts.atmosphere: There is no black void. The background is a full-bleed flood of whichever face points most toward the camera, so the whole room changes color with every turn. A giant halftone dot screen sits over the flood and swells with turn velocity. The cube body is glossy clearcoat plastic in #0C0C10, the world's only neutral and the color of all sticker type. It reflects a studio of light panels built in code and casts a hard contact shadow on the flood. The sticker gaps double as the page's layout grid. Each sticker color carries its own procedural pattern, light film grain covers everything, and each band lock sets off a halftone shockwave in that face's color.
concepts.heroMoment: THE GRID WAS A CUBE. You land straight above what reads as a flat Swiss poster: “SCRAMBLED / AT AGE 14 / WORLD 03.” on a 3x3 grid. It is really the top face of a building-sized picture cube, built from 27 RoundedBox cubies plus 54 instanced sticker quads mapped to a 54-tile CanvasTexture atlas. The camera looks straight down at FOV 8°, so it reads as flat. On the first scroll tick, the right third of your screen swings 90° away in true perspective (an R turn). At the same time a dolly-zoom (FOV 8°→35°, with camera distance re-solved each frame to hold the face size) bends the 'page' into an object, and the word SCRAMBLED is the first thing to get scrambled. About 30 scrubbed quarter turns then shred every face into a three-letter ransom note (“AMB TOO CUB DEE SCR BIT”). Next, scroll plays the exact inverse of that scramble. It is written as a real layer-by-layer solve, and the cube revolves like a billboard while it runs, so the copy reassembles in reading order. First the top face and band 1 lock (“7+ CUBES. DIFFERENT PUZZLE TYPES.”). Then band 2 locks (“TIME SPENT: WAY TOO MUCH.”), then band 3 (“GOING TOO DEEP INTO THINGS? YEAH.”). Each lock fires a halftone shockwave in that face's color. A final x2 flip shows the bottom face: “IT'S A / HABIT.”
supporting: Patterned stickers: each color has its own procedural pattern (white grid paper, yellow halftone, red zigzag, orange grain, blue pinstripe, green checker). This brings maximal Memphis-style energy, stays readable for color-blind viewers, and makes it clearly an original cube rather than a branded one.
Chromatic flood: the backdrop recolors to the face nearest the camera on every turn, so the cube literally paints the room.

SVG 16-segment 'competition timer': INSPECTION counts 15 → 14, freezes, and flips to “AGE 14”. During the solve the digits speed up past readability, so no time is ever legible and nothing looks like a claimed record, then they overflow into “WAY TOO MUCH”.
Notation ticker: every turn prints its move (R, U′, F2…) in Tilt Warp, with the letters tilting along with the layer. The scramble prints forward, and the solve prints its exact inverse.
The 7+ orbit: seven small abstract puzzle-moons circle the cube, plus one '+' that keeps drifting out of formation. The moons are deliberately not models of real puzzles.
Free-play: after the solve, you can swipe or drag any layer to twist it, and the cursor becomes a curved twist-arrow. 'Solve it' replays your exact moves backwards: “Go on, scramble it. I'll wait.”
scrollBeats: 0–8% POSTER: the portal lands you straight above a flat white Swiss-grid poster reading “SCRAMBLED / AT AGE 14 / WORLD 03.” The corner LCD counts INSPECTION 15 → 14, freezes, and flips to “AGE 14”.
8–18% THE TURN: the right third of the screen swings 90° away in real perspective (R). The dolly-zoom (FOV 8°→35°) bends the page into an object, and yellow floods in behind it.

18–32% SCRAMBLE FRENZY: about 30 scrubbed quarter turns shred the copy into a three-letter ransom note. The camera arcs up and out to a 3/4 view of a building-sized cube. The seven puzzle-moons and the stray '+' start orbiting, the flood follows the nearest face, and the ticker spews notation.

32–75% THE SOLVE (hero): scroll plays the exact inverse as a layer-by-layer solve while the cube revolves like a billboard. First the top face and band 1 lock (7+ CUBES. DIFFERENT PUZZLE TYPES.), then band 2 (TIME SPENT: WAY TOO MUCH.), then band 3 (GOING TOO DEEP INTO THINGS? YEAH.). Each lock fires a halftone shockwave and adds a DOM caption, and the LCD digits speed up past readability.

75–88% PUNCHLINE + PLAY: the final click leaves the cube solved, and an x2 flip shows the bottom face, “IT'S A / HABIT.” The LCD overflows into “WAY TOO MUCH”, and free-play unlocks (“Go on, scramble it. I'll wait.”).

88–100% TOO DEEP: any scramble the visitor made reverses automatically. The middle slice then turns 45° to crack the cube open, and the camera dives into the glossy black core, where World 04's portal opens.
concepts.portalIcon: Isometric cube silhouette: a regular hexagon split into three rhombus faces, each cut into a 3x3 grid of rounded-rhombus stickers with gaps about 7% of the face width, for 27 windows in total. In the SVG mask only the stickers are open, so the Rubik's world first shows through 27 sticker-shaped windows. The dive aims at the center sticker of the top face. The gaps sweep past like a grid flying by, and you land looking straight down at the cube's top face.
concepts.titleCard: You look straight down onto a flat white Swiss-grid poster that fills the screen. It reads “SCRAMBLED / AT AGE 14 / WORLD 03.” in Rubik Mono One, three characters per grid cell, with crisp black gutters. A tiny 16-segment LCD in the corner counts INSPECTION 15 → 14 → “AGE 14”. It reads as page layout, and nothing hints that it is the top of a cube until the first scroll tick.

copy.headline: Scrambled at 14.
lines: 7+ cubes. Different puzzle types.
Time spent: way too much.
Going too deep into things? Yeah. It's a habit.
Go on, scramble it. I'll wait.

concepts.tech: One R3F canvas, loaded with next/dynamic (ssr:false). It mounts when the world is about 1.5 viewports away and pauses offscreen. One pinned ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container', updated from Lenis on the shared gsap.ticker) owns a master timeline that drives the camera, cube, flood, LCD and labels, so everything runs on one clock. Cube: 27 cubies as an InstancedMesh of a drei RoundedBox geometry, using MeshPhysicalMaterial clearcoat. Reflections come from a drei <Environment> built from <Lightformer>s, with no HDR file. The 54 stickers are one InstancedMesh whose per-instance UV offset points into a 54-tile CanvasTexture atlas. Each tile holds a pattern plus three Rubik Mono One characters, drawn after document.fonts.load, at 2048² on desktop and 1024² on mobile. Move engine: precompute the cubie transforms at every integer step k = 0…N (N ≈ 60) and map scroll to m in [0, N]. Each frame, render state[floor m] plus the next layer rotated by snapEase(frac m)·90°. That is O(1) per frame and reverses exactly when scrolling back up. Write the solve as three layer-preserving phases: first the layer at the top face, then middle-layer inserts that keep it, then last-layer algorithms that keep the first two. Choose algorithms whose per-face quarter-turn sums are ≡ 0 mod 4, so the printed centers stay upright. Generate the scramble as the exact inverse, and check it with a 54-facelet state checker in a unit test. Dolly-zoom: each frame, distance = halfFace / tan(fov/2). The flood and the halftone shockwave are DOM/CSS layers behind a transparent canvas. The LCD is inline SVG 16-segment glyphs, and Tilt Warp's XROT/YROT axes are bound to the turn angle. Perf: about 5 draw calls, since a turn only updates 9 cubie and 21 sticker instance matrices. DPR is clamped to 1–1.75 (1–1.25 on mobile), with no postprocessing on mobile. Mobile: on portrait phones the poster is fitted to the width over a matching white flood, so the face edges disappear. The 3/4 framing keeps each sticker at 56px or more on a 375px screen, and DOM captions mirror every locked band. Free-play uses swipes, with touch-action: pan-y outside the cube so page scroll is never taken over. Reduced motion: no pin or scrub. Show one static render of the solved cube with every band readable, all copy as DOM, and the LCD frozen on 'WAY TOO MUCH'; free-play turns snap without animation. The canvas is aria-hidden, with a parallel <ol> of the copy, keyboard Scramble/Solve buttons, and aria-live announcements when a band locks.
concepts.risk: At heart this is still 'a cube that solves on scroll', the most predictable idea for this world. The fake-out fails if any depth shows before the first turn, or if the three-letter stickers can't be read on a phone. Mitigation: hold a near-orthographic top-down opening, size the type so each sticker is 56px or more at 375px, mirror every locked band in DOM captions, and unit-test the layer-by-layer solve so the lines really do lock in reading order. Keep the object original: patterned stickers, our own hex values, and no Rubik's logo or wordmark anywhere.

concepts.name: 7+ Cubes Deep
concepts.oneLiner: The habit of going too deep, taken literally. A cube sinks off a sunny waterline and pulls you down through a glowing deep-sea world where every creature is built from cube parts. A dive computer logs depth in cubes and dive time as 'way too much'. At the bottom, the cube's own stickers swim back together into a solved cube.

palette.role: Surface sky and sticker-yellow glow
Sunlit shallows and caustics
Twilight cobalt mid-water
Abyssal ultraviolet floor (never pure black)
Red glow, warnings and pressure cracks
Dive-computer phosphor and sticker-green glow

concepts.typography: Anybody (variable width) for the headline. “7+ CUBES DEEP” starts ultra-expanded (wdth 150) just under the waterline with an SVG displacement wobble. As depth increases it is crushed toward wdth 50 / wght 900, so you can see the pressure in the type. Fraunces italic (SOFT 100, WONK 1) for field-guide specimen captions with hairline leader lines (“Specimen 03 of 7+”). Doto (dot-matrix) for the dive-computer HUD, in phosphor green on smoked glass.
concepts.atmosphere: The whole water column is one vertical gradient: sun-yellow sky, then turquoise shallows, cobalt twilight, and an ultraviolet abyss that is never pure black. Caustic light nets crawl over everything near the surface, and light shafts thin out and die with depth. Marine snow made of tiny confetti stickers streams upward past the camera, and a vignette tightens like pressure. Everything alive glows in a neon remix of the six sticker colors (white #F2FFF9, yellow #FFE45C, red #FF3355, orange #FF8A1F, blue #39A0FF, green #3DFF8C) with bloom, against glossy black-plastic bodies. Motion language: every creature moves in quarter-turns with a click-snap ease (fast attack, tiny overshoot, long settle). Only the shoal flows, until it clicks into a cube.
concepts.heroMoment: THE STICKER SHOAL. In the midnight zone, the cube you followed down gives way under pressure. Its 54 stickers peel off the black plastic body and become fish: glowing rounded-square stickers whose trailing edge flutters as a tail. They are one InstancedMesh of 54, with the tail bend done in the vertex shader. First they swirl as a bait ball (CPU boids: separation, alignment, cohesion). Then scroll takes over in three phases. (1) The fish sort by color into six schools. (2) Each school flattens into a 3x3 face. (3) The six faces lay out as a cross-shaped net and fold up, hinge by hinge, around the returning plastic body (click, click, click). The result is a solved cube that pulses like a heartbeat and floods the abyss with six colors. Meanwhile the dive computer's DIVE TIME digits blur and lock on “WAY TOO MUCH”. Each phase is a fixed target pose blended with boid noise whose strength falls to zero, so scrolling back un-solves it cleanly. The cursor (or a tap on phones) acts as a predator: nearby fish scatter, the cube tears open, then heals itself.
supporting: Specimens built from cube parts, counted on the way down with field-guide captions (“Specimen 01 of 7+”). A cube-jelly swims by twisting its top layer, so every pulse is a quarter-turn, and trails tentacles made of chains of small cubes. A face-manta is a single 3x3 face flapping its outer columns. A cube-eel moves only in 90° snaps. A lantern-cube dangles one glowing sticker as a lure. A siphonophore is a long string of tiny cubes rippling with color. An urchin-cube's sticker spines bristle when the cursor comes near. The shapes stay abstract, with no models of real puzzles.
The '+': after Specimen 07, a lone glowing plus-shaped creature swims off into the dark. It is the plus in 7+.

Dive-computer HUD (Doto): 'DIVER: AGE 14' and 'DEPTH: 1 CUBE … 7+ CUBES'. 'DIVE TIME' rolls without ever showing a readable number, then overflows into 'WAY TOO MUCH'. An 'ASCEND' warning gets struck through with 'nah.' Each counted specimen sends out a six-color sonar ping ring.
Pressure type: the headline compresses from wdth 150 to wdth 50 with depth, and its letter spacing tightens as if the water is squeezing it.

Pressure cracks: at the floor, glowing hairline cracks draw themselves across the viewport 'glass' (SVG stroke-dashoffset) next to the HUD warning. They retract as the seabed opens, so they read as a gag and never as a broken page.
Seabed exit: the floor of dim sticker tiles splits, light pours up, and World 04's icon-portal opens in the crack: “There's no bottom. Just the next thing.”
scrollBeats: 0–10% SURFACE: the portal opens on a split-level waterline: sun-yellow sky, 'WORLD 03 · AGE 14', a lone glowing cube bobbing at the surface, and '7+ CUBES DEEP' refracting just under the surface at full width.

10–25% DROP: the cube's top layer gives one last quarter-turn, then the cube tips and sinks in a burst of bubbles. The waterline slides off the top of the screen, and the dive computer boots ('DIVER: AGE 14 / DEPTH: 1 CUBE'). Specimen 01, a cube-jelly, pulses past by twisting its top layer.

25–45% TWILIGHT: cobalt water and thinning light shafts. Specimen 02, a face-manta, flaps its columns, and Specimen 03, a cube-eel, snaps along in 90° steps. Sticker-confetti marine snow streams upward, and the headline is visibly squeezed narrower.

45–75% MIDNIGHT, STICKER SHOAL (hero): in ultraviolet dark, the sinking cube's 54 stickers peel off and become Specimen 04, a glowing shoal. Scroll sorts them by color, flattens the six schools into faces, and folds the net into a solved cube that pulses and floods the abyss with color. DIVE TIME locks on 'WAY TOO MUCH', and the pointer or a tap scatters the shoal before it heals.

75–92% FLOOR: Specimens 05–07 (lantern, siphonophore, urchin) light up the cube. DEPTH reads '7+ CUBES' as the lone '+' swims off into the dark. The 'ASCEND' warning gets struck through ('nah.') and hairline pressure cracks draw across the glass. “Going too deep into things. (Yes, it's a habit.)” appears, squeezed to wdth 50.
92–100% EXIT: the seabed splits, light pours up, and World 04's icon-portal opens in the crack. The cube drops through: “There's no bottom. Just the next thing.”
concepts.portalIcon: The isometric cube silhouette: a hexagon of three rhombus faces with 3x3 rounded-rhombus stickers per face, 27 windows in total, plus three rising bubble circles above its top corner. Cube plus bubbles reads as 'sunken cube'. In the SVG mask, the stickers and bubbles are open windows showing turquoise water. The dive aims at the front-right face, so it feels like plunging into a cube-shaped aquarium.
concepts.titleCard: A split-level waterline. Above it is flat sun-yellow sky with 'WORLD 03 · AGE 14' in Doto. A lone glowing cube bobs on a wobbling SVG waterline, with caustics crawling over it. Just below the surface, '7+ CUBES DEEP' is set in ultra-expanded Anybody, refracting and swaying.

copy.headline: 7+ cubes deep.
lines: Age 14. Dropped in. Kept sinking.
Depth: 7+ cubes. Different puzzle types.
Dive time: way too much.
Warning: going too deep into things. (Yes, it's a habit.)
There's no bottom. Just the next thing.

concepts.tech: One R3F canvas for the whole water column, loaded with next/dynamic (ssr:false). It mounts about 1.5 viewports early and pauses offscreen. DOM overlays sit on top for the HUD, captions, crack SVG and waterline/sky SVG. A pinned ScrollTrigger on '#scroll-container' scrubs one master GSAP timeline that drives camera.y, fog color and density, the background-gradient uniform, light-shaft opacity, the headline's wdth axis and the HUD states. It runs on the shared gsap.ticker, which also drives Lenis and invalidates R3F (frameloop='demand'). Water: a full-screen gradient shader keyed to depth, with procedural sine/Voronoi caustics near the surface that are also sampled into the sinking cube's emissive. Every creature is built from three primitives (rounded box, rounded-square sticker quad, chain of small cubes) and two vertex shaders (undulate, and pulse-twist). The chains are follow-the-leader InstancedMeshes, hidden when outside a depth window. Shoal: one InstancedMesh of 54 with CPU boids (about 2.9k neighbor checks per frame). Fixed target poses for the sorted, net and folded-cube phases are blended by weights derived from scroll, so the formation scrubs backward cleanly. The predator is a pointer or tap raycast onto a plane. Glow: on desktop, Bloom (mipmapBlur, half resolution) plus Noise and Vignette in a single EffectComposer. Mobile skips postprocessing and fakes the glow with additive halo sprites. Marine snow is shader-animated instanced quads, 1,200 on desktop and 300 on mobile. Perf: about 25 draw calls, with DPR clamped to 1–1.75 (1–1.25 on mobile). Mobile keeps the same story; the HUD collapses into one top strip, and 'tap to scatter' replaces hover. Reduced motion: no pin and no camera travel. Show one static frame of the formed, glowing cube among three specimens over a CSS water gradient, with the HUD frozen at 'DEPTH: 7+ CUBES / DIVE TIME: WAY TOO MUCH' and all copy as DOM. The canvas is aria-hidden, with semantic text in parallel.
concepts.risk: The leap to an ocean could bury the cube read, and a deep descent on a near-black site could feel dark rather than colorful. Mitigation: open on the cube itself at a sun-yellow waterline, build every creature from stickers and black plastic, and move everything in quarter-turns. Keep the abyss ultraviolet (#160A3A, never #000) and let the six-color glow carry each frame. Cap the creature work at three primitives and two shaders. Keep specimen shapes abstract, with no real puzzle names, unless Josh confirms the puzzles he actually owned. Coordinate with World 07 (Minecraft) so it doesn't also use a vertical dig-down.

why: 7+ Cubes Deep is the stronger concept because it turns the one personality trait in this chapter's facts, going too deep, into the world itself and lets every other fact land as a dive-computer joke. It pays off with a shoal of stickers that solves itself into a cube, a 'how did they build that' moment that a cube solving on scroll can't match, and it keeps the Rubik's world visually unlike the other cube-heavy chapters (Moving homes, Minecraft) while handing off naturally as the seabed cracks open into the next obsession.

concepts.name: Spin Room
concepts.oneLiner: Josh's MUN position paper types itself out weak and mostly blacked out. Then scroll swings the camera 90° around the page, and the very same redaction bars, seen side-on, lock into a blazing fluoro 'ARGUMENT: WON.' Nothing is peeled back and nothing new is added: the win comes purely from where you stand.

palette.role: Position-paper cream: the page and the quiet analog first act
Redaction ink: lacquer front faces of the bars and the void behind the page
Fluoro yellow: bar side faces / headline letters
Fluoro pink: bar side faces / headline letters
Fluoro cyan: bar side faces, rim light, protractor HUD
Seal red: the award seal, ink splats, the 'POSITION PAPER' header stamp and the second ribbon colour for field labels

concepts.typography: Courier Prime (Regular/Bold) for the position paper on a strict monospace grid. That grid IS the redaction geometry. It is typed character by character on scroll, with per-glyph ink jitter (±0.5px offset, 75–100% opacity) and a two-colour ribbon (ink for body, seal red for field labels). Anton for the payoff: it is rasterized at runtime into horizontal stripe runs, so the typeface literally becomes the 3D bars (the DOM twin uses Anton with a CSS stripe fill). Saira Stencil One for stamps and for the seal's circular text on an SVG textPath, with a slight rubber wobble. Geist Mono (the site's own font) appears only on the protractor HUD as the degrees tick 00°→90°, which ties the world back to the site frame.
concepts.atmosphere: Act A is analog and nearly monochrome on purpose: warm cream stock with procedural fibre grain (SVG feTurbulence), ink-density jitter on every glyph, and a soft top-light falloff and vignette. Its motion is staccato: typewriter ticks, carriage slams, hard redaction thunks. Act B is the void behind the page: redaction-ink black with a slow-drifting cream halftone field (CSS radial-gradient pattern at ~4%), one diagonal light shaft and ~40 paper-dust motes. The fluoro faces bloom, and a faint chromatic fringe peaks at 45° then clears. The motion becomes one long, heavy, inevitable orbit (expo.inOut) that ends in a magnetic click. At the lock everything goes dead still, so the stamp that follows hits like a hammer.
concepts.heroMoment: THE TURN. A pinned stage holds an R3F scene shot through an OrthographicCamera: the paper plane sits at the back with ~220 instanced lacquer bars (~140 on phones) in front of it. Each bar is a box whose +z face is redaction ink and whose +x face is fluoro. At azimuth 0° the +z faces are exactly the redaction bars of the typed position paper. At 90° the paper is edge-on (a vanishing hairline), and the +x faces are exactly the stripes of 'ARGUMENT: / WON.' set in Anton. Same objects, two readings. The geometry is solved at mount: (1) rasterize the headline offscreen into N horizontal stripe rows whose pitch equals the page's line pitch, and scan each row for ink runs to get z-intervals; (2) take each page line's redaction runs from the monospace grid to get x-intervals; (3) per row, split the shorter list into contiguous pieces so every box gets exactly one x-run and one z-run. Contiguous pieces read as one bar from either side, and boxes within a row never overlap. Scroll maps p∈[0,1] to azimuth θ = 90°·easeInOut(p), elevation φ = 18°·sin(πp), and a per-bar chaos offset = seed_i·sin²(πp). Mid-turn, the bars scatter into a black-and-neon skyline; both endpoints stay mathematically exact. Past p = 0.92 a magnet lock tweens θ to exactly π/2, and φ and chaos to 0 (expo.out, 350ms), with a trauma kick as 'WON.' clicks into legibility.
supporting: Redaction slams that bleed: the scroll-scrubbed typewriter blacks out COMMITTEE, COUNTRY and TOPIC (honest and funny, because those details are never invented) plus most body lines. Each bar bleeds wet ink for ~120ms (SVG displacement), then hardens into a lacquer object with a 2px carriage nudge.
The tell: at 7° every black bar shows a razor-thin fluoro edge, neon hiding inside the black, before the viewer understands why.
Protractor HUD: a hairline protractor arc whose needle tracks the real camera azimuth in Geist Mono degrees. Ticks light up fluoro as you pass them, and it flips to 'ANGLE FOUND · 90°' at the lock.

The seal: a red rubber stamp, '2ND BEST DELEGATE · MODEL UNITED NATIONS ·' (SVG textPath, rubber texture via feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap), drops and slams with a decaying trauma shake. The 3D bars shiver under the impact and re-lock.
Uncountable stamp-burst: 'MULTIPLE CONFERENCES' machine-guns the same stamp into an overlapping pile, so no number is ever implied.
Mid-turn debate chaos: ~60 blank folded chits (instanced; ~20 on phones) whip through the gaps between bars on curved paths, then clear out before the lock.
scrollBeats: 0–8% ARRIVAL: the lectern-shaped portal from the Social/Content world expands (optionally rolling a quarter-turn as you pass through, to foreshadow the hero). We drop onto the sheet on the lectern until the cream page fills the screen, and 'POSITION PAPER' thunks in as a red stencil stamp over 'MODEL UNITED NATIONS'.

8–28% THE CASE FILE: scroll drives the typewriter. 'Delegate: Joshmann Singh, 15.' types out, then COMMITTEE / COUNTRY / TOPIC, each slammed black. Body lines type and get redacted until the page is mostly ink. The one clean line sits dead centre: 'POSITION: WEAK.'

28–36% THE TELL: azimuth creeps from 0° to 7°. The bars betray their thickness, depth offsets and thin fluoro edges (they were objects all along). The protractor HUD fades in at 07°, with the margin note 'Same facts.'

36–78% THE TURN (hero), 7° to 90°: the paper swings edge-on and vanishes, and the bars scatter into a black-lacquer skyline with fluoro flanks. The camera tilts up and back, bloom climbs, and the halftone void and paper dust appear. The magnet lock clicks at exactly 90°: 'ARGUMENT: WON.' The HUD reads 'ANGLE FOUND · 90°', with the line 'Better angle.'

78–90% THE SEAL: the red '2ND BEST DELEGATE' seal slams down (screen thump, ink splat, bars shiver and re-lock). The uncountable 'MULTIPLE CONFERENCES' burst rattles in. 'Learned to argue before I learned to code.' gets a scroll-drawn fluoro highlighter swipe, with the aside 'Not spin. Perspective.'
90–100% EXIT: the counter of the O in 'WON.' heats to white, the next world's icon-shaped portal grows out of it, and the dive begins.
concepts.portalIcon: Lectern with gooseneck mic: a tapered trapezoid podium with a slanted reading ledge, and a thick curved mic stem ending in a bulb. Keep the stem at least 6% of the icon width so it survives as a mask. As it scales past the viewport, the reading ledge becomes the page.
concepts.titleCard: The sheet on the lectern fills the frame. 'POSITION PAPER' thunks in as a red stencil stamp over 'MODEL UNITED NATIONS', then the carriage types 'Delegate: Joshmann Singh, 15.' Nothing in this first frame hints that the page is 3D.

copy.headline: Same facts. Better angle.
lines: POSITION PAPER · Model United Nations
Delegate: Joshmann Singh, 15.
Committee: ██████ · Country: ██████ · Topic: ██████
POSITION: WEAK.
ARGUMENT: WON.
Even when my opening position was weak, I found a way to win the argument.
Learned to argue before I learned to code.
2nd Best Delegate. Multiple conferences.
Not spin. Perspective.

concepts.tech: R3F, lazy-loaded with next/dynamic (ssr:false) and mounted by an IntersectionObserver about one viewport early; it shares the three.js chunk with the other 3D worlds. It uses an OrthographicCamera, because the trick needs parallel projection. Draw calls: ONE InstancedMesh of unit boxes (~220 desktop / ~140 phone), scaled per instance. A tiny shader colours each face by its object-space normal: +z gets lacquer ink with a specular streak, +x gets the instanceColor fluoro, and the other faces are near-black. Chaos offsets are computed in the vertex shader from a per-instance seed times one uniform, so there are no per-frame matrix uploads. Add one paper plane (a CanvasTexture of the typed page at 2× DPR; alternatively keep the typing phase as crisp DOM and swap to the pixel-identical plane on the turn's first frame) and one instanced draw call for the chits. The bars are long, thin lacquer slabs, never cubes, so they don't echo the Rubik's or Minecraft worlds. Layout solver (pure function, unit-tested): after document.fonts.load for Anton, rasterize the headline onto an offscreen canvas and scan the stripe rows for ink runs to get z-intervals. The row pitch equals the Courier Prime line pitch, and bars are about 80% of that pitch. Redaction runs come from the monospace grid as x-intervals, and the two are paired per row by splitting. The page layout enforces two rules: redactions appear only on stripe rows, and every stripe row has at least one. On 375px phones, only 'WON.' is striped (7 rows at a 20px pitch fills the 343px column), and 'ARGUMENT:' drops in as solid DOM Anton at the lock. Choreography: a pinned 100vh stage in a ~340vh section, using the page's existing pin inside #scroll-container. ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container', updated from Lenis's scroll event) scrubs ONE GSAP timeline covering the typing index, θ, φ, chaos, bloom, the HUD needle and the seal. That timeline runs on gsap.ticker, which also ticks Lenis and calls R3F invalidate() (frameloop='demand'). Optional sound effects (typewriter ticks, the lock click, the stamp thud) fire from the same timeline and are off by default. Desktop uses @react-three/postprocessing Bloom (mipmapBlur) plus light Noise. Phones skip the composer: the fluoro faces are unlit, with a CSS radial glow behind them. DPR is capped at 1.75 on desktop and 1.5 on phones, and rendering pauses offscreen. Reduced motion: no pin, orbit or typing. Instead the section is a static two-panel spread: the fully redacted paper in DOM, then 'ARGUMENT: WON.' in Anton with a repeating-linear-gradient stripe fill (background-clip:text). The seal is printed flat, and fades are opacity-only. The canvas is aria-hidden, and a semantic DOM twin carries every line.
concepts.risk: The illusion is all-or-nothing. A perspective camera, a lock that stops at 88°, or a font that loads after the solver runs will smear 'WON.' into noise. And if viewers don't notice the bars are the same objects, the moment reads as an ordinary morph. Mitigations: use an OrthographicCamera plus a hard lock to exactly π/2 and 0. Solve the layout only after the fonts load, and re-solve on resize. A headless test renders both endpoint views and pixel-diffs them against the target rasters. The 7° tell and the mid-turn tilt make it obvious the bars are physical objects, and the HUD says it outright. If WebGL is unavailable, fall back to the DOM two-panel layout.

concepts.name: Turning the Room
concepts.oneLiner: A top-down ultramarine assembly hall where every delegate's gaze is a glowing coloured thread locked on the opponent's podium. Three scroll-driven speeches then ripple the whole room around to Josh's seat at the edge, in a moiré storm that ends in a white-hot starburst.

palette.role: Assembly ultramarine: the hall floor and the world's ground
Tomato: the opponent's podium and the 'against' backs of placards
Saffron: gaze threads and placards
Mint: gaze threads and placards
Bubblegum: gaze threads and placards
Bone white: type, delegate heads, the starburst core

concepts.typography: Fraunces (variable, with the wght, SOFT, WONK and opsz axes loaded through next/font) for the speeches and the 'ORDER.' title card. Its weight is scrubbed 100→300→600→900 across the three waves, and WONK switches on at the climax, so the argument literally gains weight as the room turns. Archivo (variable width 62–125) for the placards and Josh's name card, which widens as he wins the room. Martian Mono for the chair's micro-labels ('THE CHAIR RECOGNIZES', 'OPENING POSITION').
concepts.atmosphere: A top-down ultramarine floor with procedurally drawn concentric carpet arcs and aisle wedges, a soft radial vignette and fine film grain. Delegates are flat geometric pills (bone-white heads with a single eye-dot) casting tiny offset shadows. The opponent's podium glows tomato, and the threads glow additively over the blue. Every delegate has an idle breathing bob, and the carpet pattern drifts slowly. Motion language: springy back.out head-turns rippling outward, long sweeping strands, and an elastic twang. At the climax a bone-white bloom floods out from Josh's placard.
concepts.heroMoment: THE ROOM TURNS. A Canvas 2D hemicycle seats 168 delegates on 7 arcs (72 on 4 arcs on phones). From each head, a 1–1.5px gaze thread in that delegate's colour runs to a target. At the start they all converge on the opponent's tomato podium in a dense fan, while Josh's tiny placard pulses at the outer edge. Three scroll waves re-aim the threads at Josh: target_i = mix(podium, josh, backOut(clamp((wave − delay_i)/0.25, 0, 1))), with delay_i = 0.65·dist(seat_i, josh)/maxDist + 0.08·hash(i). Heads therefore turn in a ripple spreading outward from him. Threads composite with 'lighter' at ~0.3 alpha, so the crossing, sweeping strands throw off live moiré interference for free. When all 168 lock on, they stack into a white-hot starburst (a half-res blurred copy composited for bloom). Then the virtual camera drops from overhead to just behind Josh's placard, using a ~40-line perspective projection in the same canvas. The strands from the whole hall now fan across the room into the 'JOSH' card in the foreground.
supporting: Variable-weight oratory: each speech line is set in Fraunces, with wght scrubbed 100→900 and WONK switching on at the climax, on the same timeline as the threads.

Flip-placards: every delegate holds an abstract flag-geometry card generated from a seed (stripes, discs, chevrons, crosses; no real flags, no invented countries). It flips through scaleX 0 from its tomato 'against' back to its own colour the instant its owner turns.
Eye-dot comedy: each delegate's single pupil slides toward the new target a beat before its thread follows, so a ripple of 168 tiny glances visibly sweeps the hall.
Over-the-shoulder drop: after the third wave, the camera falls from overhead to just behind Josh's placard, and every strand fans across the hall into his name card.
Gavel twang: the strike plucks the whole web, sending a damped sine displacement rolling outward arc by arc.
String-art exit: the strands re-aim to points sampled along the next world's icon outline and stitch the portal together before it opens.
scrollBeats: 0–8% ARRIVAL: the gavel-shaped portal opens onto 'ORDER.' set huge in bone-white Fraunces 900 on ultramarine, with the gavel head landing as the period. The letters crumble into 168 delegates scurrying to their seats as the camera rises to a top-down view.

8–22% THE ROOM AS IT IS: every strand converges on the tomato podium, and the placards show their tomato backs. Josh's placard pulses at the edge, labelled in Fraunces wght 100: 'Opening position: weak.'
22–38% WAVE 1: '“Honourable Chair, fellow delegates—”' (wght 300) unspools from Josh's seat. The nearest arcs turn, and the first strands peel off the podium.
38–55% WAVE 2: '“Point of information.”' (wght 600). Half the room turns, the sweeping field throws off moiré storms, and placards flip to their own colours.

55–72% WAVE 3: '“Right of reply.”' (wght 900, WONK on). The last arcs turn, every strand locks into the starburst on Josh, and the podium dims. The camera drops over his shoulder so the whole hall fans into his placard.
72–86% THE GAVEL: the strike twangs the entire web. Josh's placard balloons into '2ND BEST DELEGATE', followed by 'Learned to argue before I learned to code.' and 'Multiple conferences.'
86–100% EXIT: the strands re-aim to the next world's icon outline and stitch it in string art. Its interior opens, and the dive begins.
concepts.portalIcon: Chair's gavel: a barrel-shaped mallet head with two raised bands on a short angled handle, striking a small round sound block. One bold compound path, legible from 40px to full-bleed.
concepts.titleCard: 'ORDER.' set enormous in bone-white Fraunces 900 on the ultramarine floor, its period being the gavel's strike point, with 'MODEL UNITED NATIONS · AGE 15' beneath it in Martian Mono. Then the letters crumble into the delegates taking their seats.

copy.headline: The room turns.
lines: ORDER. Model United Nations, age 15.
Opening position: weak.
“Honourable Chair, fellow delegates—”
“Point of information.”
“Right of reply.”
Found a way to win the argument anyway.
Learned to argue before I learned to code.
2nd Best Delegate. Multiple conferences.

concepts.tech: No three.js needed: one Canvas 2D (DPR capped at 2 on desktop and 1.5 on phones) sits under DOM type. Seats are precomputed in polar coordinates: 7 arcs × 24 on desktop, and 4 × 18 on phones, with the hemicycle fitted to the 343px column and type above and below. Threads are drawn with globalCompositeOperation='lighter' at ~0.3 alpha and 1–1.5 CSS px, which produces the moiré naturally. Cheap bloom, used only at the climax: redraw the thread layer into a half-res offscreen canvas with ctx.filter='blur(6px)' and composite it with 'lighter'. The over-the-shoulder drop is a ~40-line hand-rolled perspective projection in the same canvas (pitch lerps 90°→10°, x' = f·x/z). For the twang, threads become quadratic curves whose control point is offset by A·e^(−4t)·sin(22t + arcIndex·0.6). The string-art exit re-aims threads to points from getPointAtLength along the next world's icon path. Placards are generated once from seeds and cached to a sprite atlas. The pinned stage sits in a ~300vh section inside #scroll-container. ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container', updated from Lenis) scrubs one GSAP timeline that also drives CSS font-variation-settings (Fraunces wght/WONK, Archivo wdth), all on gsap.ticker. An IntersectionObserver pauses drawing offscreen. Reduced motion: no pin. Instead, one static canvas frame shows the final converged web with full-colour placards, the speeches are stacked as text, and every fact is in the DOM. The canvas is aria-hidden, with a semantic DOM twin.
concepts.risk: Moiré can tip from mesmerising into shimmer or aliasing on low-DPR screens. And 'the whole room turns to look at Josh' can blur into the Social/Content world's attention theme right before it. Mitigations: tune line width and alpha per DPR, and allow moiré only during sweeps (locked states are clean single-direction fans). Keep the language strictly procedural (podium, placards, gavel, 'Point of information') so it reads as persuasion, not followers. Cap phones at 72 delegates, and test the over-the-shoulder drop at 375px early.

why: Spin Room is stronger because its hero doesn't decorate the fact, it performs it. The exact same bars read as a weak, blacked-out case at 0° and as 'ARGUMENT: WON.' at 90°, a perspective trick nobody has seen in a portfolio, and it lands 'won even from a weak position' in one gesture for a single instanced draw call. Turning the Room is lovely and cheaper, but 'everyone turns to look at Josh' sits too close to the attention theme of the Social/Content world right before it, and it leans on more familiar string-art effects.

world: #9 Fitness (age 18). Built the body too: discipline, training, nutrition, consistency.

concepts.name: Progressive Overload
concepts.oneLiner: In this world the website itself carries the weight: each set fills the screen with a pillar plate and makes the type, the frame, the cursor and the actual scroll heavier, until you press the whole thing to lockout and drop it.

palette.role: Rubber-floor black: ground and background
Chalk white: type, ECG line, dust. The only non-plate color
Vermilion plate: DISCIPLINE
Ultraviolet plate: TRAINING
Electric cyan plate: NUTRITION
Hot-pink plate: CONSISTENCY, and the base of the final pigment-chalk blast

concepts.typography: Anybody (Google Fonts variable font, wdth 50–150, wght 100–900) carries the whole arc. The headline starts skinny (wdth 50 / wght 100) and bulks up one step per set until it reaches wdth 150 / wght 900 ('bulking season'). Past that it goes 'over max' with three stacked offset text-strokes and a squash-and-stretch on every slam. The same face is wrapped around each plate rim as circular type. Big Shoulders Stencil Display sets the 'AGAIN.' stamps and set numbers, like paint sprayed through a gym-wall stencil. JetBrains Mono, tiny and chalk-white, sets the labels (SET 01, LOAD, HOLD).
concepts.atmosphere: A pitch-black EPDM rubber gym floor with procedural confetti speckle (flecks in the four plate colors at about 6% density). One hard overhead key light pools a cone of chalk haze mid-screen, chalk motes drift in the beam, faint stenciled floor marks sit at the edges, and fine film grain covers everything. Restraint rule: color appears only on the plates and in the final chalk blast; everything else is black and chalk. Ambient motion: the bar is never perfectly still (a micro-oscillation), the light cone breathes, and every slam fires a decaying trauma shake (shake proportional to trauma squared) that makes the floor flecks hop.
concepts.heroMoment: THE LOCKOUT. A full-bleed barbell loaded with the four pillar plates, which YOU press from the floor to overhead with your own scroll while the website buckles under the load. During the lift, the Lenis virtualScroll hook multiplies wheel/touch delta by a load factor that ramps from 1.0 to 0.55 (with lerp going from 0.1 to 0.05), so the page physically resists. A 16-node Verlet spring chain makes the bar sag in the middle and whip on every scroll burst. The stage tilts a few degrees under the strain. The site's thin rounded frame has already thickened, and its bottom edge bows in sync with the bar's sag. The headline sits at over-max bulk. At the top, everything freezes for 600 ms on 'HOLD.' Then the release: the load factor snaps back (briefly 1.25x, settling to 1.0) so the scroll feels weightless, the bar drops, the plates bounce on the rubber with an elastic settle, the frame springs back straight, and a blast of pigment chalk in all four plate colors fills the screen.
supporting: Plate eclipses: each pillar plate rolls in face-on and fills the viewport with solid color, its word wrapped around the rim. It spins like a record with scroll velocity, then turns edge-on and slams onto the sleeve (expo.in attack, elastic settle).

ECG becomes the barbell: the title card's chalk flatline thickens and hardens into the knurled bar. Your scroll speed draws heartbeat spikes that travel along the shaft as whip, and when you stop scrolling it flatlines with the caption 'Don't flatline now.'
Bulking type: a skinny-to-swole variable headline that grows in both width and weight, then goes over max with stacked strokes and squashes on every impact.
The site gets heavy: the global frame border thickens set by set and its bottom edge bows with the bar. The custom cursor becomes a chalked mini-plate with mass and lag.
Rubber-floor confetti: procedural EPDM speckle in the four plate colors; the flecks hop on every slam.
'AGAIN.' stencil stamps slapped on in rhythm during Set 04, each one slightly misregistered like real spray paint.
scrollBeats: 0–8%: Portal lands through the kettlebell. Black rubber floor, one chalk-white ECG flatline across the screen, and a tiny, skinny 'BUILT THE BODY TOO.' (wdth 50 / wght 100). Caption: 'Light. For now.'

8–24%: SET 01 · DISCIPLINE. The flatline blips once, then thickens into a knurled steel bar running edge to edge. A vermilion plate rolls in face-on and eclipses the whole screen with DISCIPLINE around its rim, then turns edge-on and slams onto the left sleeve: trauma shake, chalk puff, floor flecks hop. The type bulks one step and the site frame thickens from 1px to 3px.

24–40%: SET 02 · TRAINING. Ultraviolet eclipse, then onto the right sleeve. The bar sags and whips, and heartbeat spikes ride along the shaft at your scroll speed. The cursor turns into a chalked mini-plate with mass.
40–54%: SET 03 · NUTRITION. Cyan eclipse. The scroll starts to resist (0.8x) and the copy owns it: 'Yes, the scroll got heavier. That's the point.' The frame's bottom edge starts to bow with the bar.
54–66%: SET 04 · CONSISTENCY. Hot-pink eclipse. 'AGAIN.' stamps slap on in rhythm, the type hits max bulk and goes over max, and the bar sags deep.
66–86%: HERO · THE LOCKOUT. Your scroll presses the bar from the floor to overhead at 0.55x resistance. It whips on every scroll burst, the stage tilts under strain, and the heartbeat trace races.

86–93%: HOLD, then DROP. A 600 ms freeze on 'HOLD.' Then the release: the scroll goes weightless, the bar drops, the plates bounce, the frame snaps straight, and pigment chalk in all four plate colors blasts the screen.
93–100%: EXIT. The chalk settles everywhere except a clean cut-out in the shape of World 10's (JEE) icon. Scroll dives through it.
concepts.portalIcon: Kettlebell: a fat round bell on a flat base with a thick arched handle and an open rounded-rectangle window (even-odd fill keeps the window see-through). Compact, about 1:1.1 aspect, readable at 40px, and it scales cleanly to full screen.
concepts.titleCard: Through the kettlebell: a pitch-black speckled rubber floor and one hairline chalk-white ECG flatline across the screen. Centered and almost weightless, 'BUILT THE BODY TOO.' in Anybody at wdth 50 / wght 100 sits over 'WORLD 09 · AGE 18', captioned 'Light. For now.' This is the lightest the type will ever be.

copy.headline: Built the body too.
lines: Light. For now.
Set 01 · Discipline.
Set 02 · Training.
Set 03 · Nutrition.
Set 04 · Consistency.
Yes, the scroll got heavier. That's the point.
Again. Again. Again.
Hold. … Drop it.

concepts.tech: No WebGL. The lift is a side view by design, so it stays light and robust on phones. Sticky stage inside a 350vh section (280vh on phones). One GSAP master timeline scrubbed by ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container'), with lenis.raf driven from gsap.ticker so DOM, SVG and canvas share one clock. Plates: CSS-3D discs (5 stacked translateZ layers fake the rubber thickness; radial-gradient sheen; SVG textPath rim word) tweened from camera-facing and full-bleed to rotateY(90deg) edge-on on the sleeve. Bar: an SVG path rebuilt each tick from a 16-node Verlet spring chain (sag proportional to plate load, whip proportional to scroll velocity) with a knurl pattern fill. It starts as the ECG polyline and morphs its stroke width and pattern. Chalk: one Canvas2D layer with pooled particles (600 max on desktop, 180 on mobile); pigment colors appear only in the final blast. Type: headline font-variation-settings bound to CSS vars from timeline progress; over-max uses 3 stacked text-stroke copies; the 'AGAIN.' stamps use Framer Motion. Heavy interface: a CSS var on the site frame controls thickness, and an in-world SVG frame overlay's bottom edge follows the bar's sag. The cursor switches to a 'plate' mode with heavier lerp via context. Scroll weight goes through the Lenis provider's virtualScroll hook (deltaY multiplied by a shared load ref) only during the lift. It is always restored on leave, unmount and visibilitychange, and keyboard and scrollbar input are never touched. Mobile: the bar bleeds off both edges (plates half-cropped) and the lift uses the tall portrait viewport. Touch resistance is capped at 0.7x and the chain drops to 12 nodes. Reduced motion: no resistance, no shake, no scrub. Instead a static SVG of the loaded bar locked out overhead, with four labeled plates and the headline at full bulk, about 1.2vh. A11y: decorative layers are aria-hidden and all copy is real DOM text.
concepts.risk: Deliberately heavier scrolling can feel like lag or a broken page, especially on trackpads and touch. Mitigation: announce it in the copy before it starts, ramp it smoothly, cap it (0.55x wheel, 0.7x touch), and confine it to the roughly 0.7vh lift. Release it with a satisfying weightless rebound, never affect keyboard or scrollbar input, and disable it for reduced motion and low-power devices. If playtests still feel bad, keep the visual buckling (frame bow, bar whip, bulked type) and drop only the real resistance; the world still works.

concepts.name: Heat Signature
concepts.oneLiner: Josh's training seen through a thermal camera: a glowing blob body lifts an ice-cold barbell as you scroll, and every rep leaves heat behind until the body burns white-hot and the scale reads BUILT.

palette.role: Cold field: background, the coldest reading
Cool indigo: resting body, cold edges, food and barbell outlines
Magenta: warming up
Furnace orange: working muscle
Amber: near max
White-hot: peak heat, HUD text

concepts.typography: Unbounded (Google Fonts variable, 200–900) for the heat-type. Its wide, rounded forms survive blur and diffusion, so the pillar words stay legible while they glow, bleed and cool. The words are rendered into the heat buffer, never as plain colored DOM; a real DOM copy mirrors them for accessibility. Share Tech Mono for the thermal HUD (SUBJECT, SET, mode and scale labels), set in white-hot with a 1px sensor jitter. Geist Sans for small captions, for continuity with the site chrome.
concepts.atmosphere: An infrared sensor field: near-black cold indigo with animated sensor grain, faint horizontal scan bands and a lens vignette. There is no visible room; space is implied only by temperature (a cold floor line, a lukewarm wall gradient, a near-black barbell). Restraint rule: the world starts almost monochrome-cold and every color on screen is earned by a rep. Ambient motion: heat diffuses and breathes every frame, handprints cool off, sweat specks drift up as cool flecks, and a NUC recalibration 'click' (a 120 ms freeze plus a small exposure jump, like a real thermal camera's shutter) marks each set change.
concepts.heroMoment: THE HEAT BUILD. A full-screen shader renders Josh as a blobby thermal body: 12 capsule SDFs on a 2D side-view rig, smooth-min unioned so the limbs melt together like a real thermal silhouette. He holds a barbell that reads near-black, because metal reads cold. Scroll scrubs the reps, with rep speed following scroll velocity on the same clock: squats in Set 1, presses in Set 2, fuel absorption in Set 3, thrusters in Set 4. Each rep deposits heat into a persistent quarter-res ping-pong heat buffer, weighted toward the muscles that movement uses (quads and glutes on the squat, delts and triceps on the press). The buffer diffuses and decays every frame. Decay slows set by set (0.96 to 0.995 per frame), so heat stacks instead of fading. The ironbow LUT climbs from indigo through magenta and orange to white-hot, the earlier pillar words resurface as warm residue, and the HUD needle travels from COUCH to BUILT. Final frame: a white-hot body holding a still-cold bar overhead.
supporting: Heat handprints: the cursor or a finger stamps a procedurally drawn hand into the heat buffer, leaving glowing palm and finger prints that cool and fade over about 4 seconds, exactly like a hand pressed on a wall under a thermal camera. It is the best toy on phones.
Cold metal truth: the barbell renders as negative heat (near-black violet), with warm smears only where the hands grip. It is physically true and makes the gym read instantly.

Heat-type: each pillar word is branded into the field as its set begins. It blooms, bleeds into a soft glow, and leaves faint warm residue, so by the end all four words are present as ghosts (consistency is heat that never fully leaves).

Physics-true jokes: sweat specks fly off as cool flecks (evaporation reads cold), and in Set 3 cold, dark food silhouettes (a bowl, an egg, a shaker) drift in and flare into heat once absorbed into the core.

Word-only HUD (live HUD overlay): corner brackets, a reticle that tracks the chest joint, the COUCH to BUILT scale bar, SET 01–04, and the NUC freeze-click. Zero invented stats; every readout is a word.

Mode switch easter egg: tapping the HUD cycles IRONBOW / RAINBOW / LAVA / ARCTIC, recoloring the whole world instantly. The last mode, VISIBLE, shows the boring truth in flat grey: 'Visible light: a guy and a barbell. Thermal: everything else.'
scrollBeats: 0–8%: Portal lands through the flexed bicep, its peak already white-hot. A cold indigo viewfinder boots: corner brackets, reticle, the COUCH to BUILT scale bar, 'SUBJECT: JOSH · AGE 18'. 'BUILT THE BODY TOO.' flickers as a lukewarm heat signature. 'Touch anything.' The cursor and fingers start leaving glowing handprints.

8–28%: SET 01 · DISCIPLINE. Cold start: the body is dim violet and the bar near-black. Squats are scrubbed by scroll, and the first rep detonates color in the legs. DISCIPLINE is branded into the heat field, then slowly diffuses. 'Starting cold anyway.'
28–46%: SET 02 · TRAINING. Presses join in, and heat climbs the back, shoulders and arms. Sweat specks fly off as cool flecks. 'Effort, rendered as heat.'
46–60%: SET 03 · NUTRITION. Cold, dark food silhouettes drift in; on contact they are absorbed and flare into the core. 'Fuel in. Heat out.'

60–84%: SET 04 · CONSISTENCY, the hero. Thrusters on scroll. Decay slows, so heat stacks rep over rep and the earlier words resurface as warm residue. The LUT climbs to white-hot and the needle slams to BUILT. 'Again. Again. Again.' A NUC freeze-click lands on the last rep.
84–93%: LOCKOUT GLOW. The white-hot body holds the still-cold bar overhead; auto-range re-normalizes and the whole field blooms. 'No before-and-after pics. Just the heat signature.'
93–100%: EXIT. World 10's (JEE) icon appears as the only cold, dark shape left in the hot field, then opens as the portal.
concepts.portalIcon: Flexed bicep: a side-view arm curled up with a tall bicep peak and a closed fist. One solid, bold path with no interior holes, so it is mask-friendly and reads at 40px. Inside the mask the bicep peak is already glowing white-hot, so the very first glimpse of this world is pure heat.
concepts.titleCard: A thermal viewfinder booting in cold indigo: corner brackets, a crosshair, the COUCH to BUILT scale bar, 'SUBJECT: JOSH · AGE 18', and 'BUILT THE BODY TOO.' as a lukewarm magenta heat signature crawling with sensor noise. Below it, a dim, cold figure stands at an even colder barbell, waiting for the first rep.

copy.headline: Built the body too.
lines: Subject: Josh · Age 18.
Touch anything. You'll leave a mark.
Discipline: starting cold anyway.
Training: effort, rendered as heat.
Nutrition: fuel in, heat out.
Consistency: the heat never fully leaves.
COUCH ←→ BUILT
Visible light: a guy and a barbell. Thermal: everything else.
No before-and-after pics. Just the heat signature.

concepts.tech: Lazy-load one R3F <Canvas> (next/dynamic, ssr:false, mounted about 1vh before entry) as a thin host for a two-pass 2D shader; no 3D scene is needed. It uses frameloop='never' and advance() from gsap.ticker, the same ticker that drives lenis.raf, so the rig, heat sim, HUD and copy share one clock. Sticky stage inside a 350vh section (280vh on phones; the side-view figure suits portrait screens). ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container') maps progress to set index and rep phase. Pipeline: (1) JS rig: a 2D skeleton with 3 eased key-pose loops (squat, press, thruster); rep phase is progress plus smoothed scroll velocity; joint positions go to a uniform vec2[12]. (2) Heat pass: drei useFBO ping-pong at quarter resolution (about 256x512 on phones). Each frame, heat = blur(previous) × decay + bodySDF × (base + activation × effort) − barSDF × cold + stamps. The stamps are a procedural handprint texture, word textures drawn on an offscreen canvas in Unbounded 900, and food SDFs. (3) Composite: a 256x1 DataTexture LUT (ironbow / rainbow / lava / arctic / visible-grey), plus grain, scan bands and vignette. HUD and copy are DOM/SVG with Framer Motion; the needle is driven from a JS heat estimate, with no GPU readback. Performance: dpr capped at 1.5, two cheap full-screen passes, no postprocessing library (the white-hot end of the LUT fakes bloom), drei PerformanceMonitor lowers buffer resolution under load, and an IntersectionObserver pauses the sim offscreen. A11y: the canvas is aria-hidden and all copy is real DOM text. Reduced motion: no scrub and no sim loop. Instead, one rendered frame of the final white-hot lockout with all four words as heat signatures and the needle at BUILT, about 1vh, with static text. Without WebGL2, the same composition is built in SVG with gradient fills.
concepts.risk: The metaball body is the whole show. If the rig moves stiffly or the silhouette reads as a blob, the world turns into a lava lamp, and thermal imagery can drift toward 'surveillance cam'. Mitigation: build and art-direct the rig first (side view, 3 clean key poses, generous smooth-min radii, the cold bar always in frame for an instant gym read) and test legibility at 375px before anything else. Keep the HUD copy funny (COUCH to BUILT, the VISIBLE joke) so it reads as playful, not military. Use adaptive resolution, and fall back to a static white-hot frame if FPS or WebGL2 fail.

why: Heat Signature is the more original idea and the safer build. Color here comes from heat, so the world gets more colorful as you train. A glowing body lifting a cold bar reads as a workout at a glance, and one mechanic covers all four facts: a cold start, heat going in, fuel burned, heat that never fully leaves. The touch handprints are a real treat on phones. Progressive Overload is a great meta-gag, but its signature move is deliberately making scrolling worse, and that can feel broken on trackpads and touch screens.

world: #11 HACKATHONS (age 18): 'BUILD. BREAK. PITCH. REPEAT.' The last world before the Outro. Josh dives into a new universe under a deadline, again and again (IIT Roorkee Productathon ~4th · Ashoka University Fashion Design Hackathon 2nd · Smart India Hackathon participated).

concepts.name: Literal Brainstorm
concepts.oneLiner: The hackathon war-room whiteboard gets a brainstorm in the most literal sense. When night flips the room to blacklight, every neon sticky note rips off the wall into a 3D hurricane around you. The storm spells out the results one at a time, and at dawn every note flies home for the next round.

palette.role: Whiteboard white (noon). The base surface, with procedural ghost-smudges of erased marker
Blacklight navy (3AM). The room's night/UV state and the storm's sky
Neon note yellow. Title-card note, hero notes, mosaic highlights
Neon note pink. BREAK accents, storm density, glow on the '2ND' mosaic
Neon note cyan. UV highlighter strokes and the PITCH spotlight tint
Neon note orange. Marker arrows, can stripes, dawn rim light

concepts.typography: Permanent Marker for every whiteboard scrawl (HACKATHONS, the four verbs, mosaic captions). It writes on through a jagged clip-path wipe led by a glowing marker-tip dot. Shantell Sans (variable; its Informality and Bounce axes INFM/BNCE loaded via next/font 'axes') for all sticky-note handwriting, scrubbed by the time of night: neat and upright at noon, bouncing and feral at 3AM, sobered up at dawn. The handwriting is literally sleep-deprived. JetBrains Mono only for tiny utilitarian tags (magnet label, 'AGE 18' stamp, can labels).
concepts.atmosphere: A life-size war-room wall: a whiteboard with ghost-smudge noise texture, round magnets, a metal marker tray, and a fluorescent tube strip along the top. The lighting is a scroll-scrubbed time-lapse driven by CSS variables. At noon a warm window-light parallelogram slides across the board. At dusk it stretches long and orange. Then the tube flickers on and the room drops to blacklight: the board turns navy, black marker nearly vanishes, and every neon note and highlighter stroke fluoresces. A peach-gold dawn ends it. Ambient motion: dust motes in the window beam, a slow camera breath, and note corners lifting in the AC draft that later becomes the storm.
concepts.heroMoment: THE STORM (about 40% into the world, under blacklight). An AC draft hits and every sticky note on the board (about 700 on desktop, about 200 on mobile) peels from its adhesive edge. The notes rip free in a staggered wave starting from the window side and spiral into a 3D hurricane that wraps around the camera. The viewer sits in the eye, with BUILD · BREAK · PITCH · REPEAT orbiting slowly inside it as the cycle wheel. Further scrolling condenses the hurricane into one giant, loose sticky-note mosaic spelling '~4TH' (marker caption: IIT Roorkee Productathon). It reshuffles mid-air into '2ND' (Ashoka University Fashion Design Hackathon), then into 'SIH' (Smart India Hackathon, participated). Build: ONE R3F InstancedMesh of 6x6-segment planes with a custom ShaderMaterial. Per-instance attributes hold board pose, vortex params (radius, height, phase, angular speed), three mosaic targets (sampled from text drawn onto a small offscreen canvas) and a seed. A single uProgress uniform from the scroll timeline blends board, vortex, mosaic A, B, C and back to board with per-note stagger, and uTime adds flutter and corner curl. It is one draw call and scrubs in both directions. The four orbiting verbs are a DOM ring with CSS 3D transforms, so they stay crisp and accessible.
supporting: Blacklight mode: the night beat flips the room to UV. Neon notes and highlighter strokes glow, black marker almost disappears, and hidden 'UV-ink' jokes surface on the board ('TODO: sleep', 'it works. don't touch it.').
Sleep-deprived handwriting: scroll drives Shantell Sans' INFM/BNCE axes, so every note's handwriting falls apart through the night and recovers at dawn.
Self-drawing marker diagrams (SVG stroke-dashoffset / DrawSVG): arrows, circled words, crossed-out ideas, and a gloriously bad architecture sketch ('frontend → backend → ??? → demo').
Can skyline: unbranded, color-blocked cans pile up on the marker tray into a spring-physics tower. It sways harder as the night deepens and topples into the storm at the BREAK beat.
Kanban as the verb wheel: columns BUILD | BREAK | PITCH | REPEAT with a round 'YOU ARE HERE' magnet that slides from column to column. At REPEAT a marker arrow loops it back to BUILD.
Squash-and-stretch note slaps during BUILD: each new note lands with a tiny overshoot and a puff of eraser dust.
scrollBeats: 0-8% ARRIVAL: the sticky-note portal finishes opening. The title-card note fills the screen, then the camera pulls back to show it's one of hundreds on a war-room whiteboard at noon.

8-30% BUILD (noon to dusk): notes slap on in bursts, marker arrows draw themselves, and the kanban headers write on. The three swimlanes get labeled IIT Roorkee Productathon / Ashoka University Fashion Design Hackathon / Smart India Hackathon. Cans start lining up and the window beam slides and warms.

30-55% BREAK (night): the tube flickers, then blacklight. Handwriting goes feral, the can tower wobbles and falls, and the draft hits. HERO: every note rips off and the 3D hurricane wraps the camera, with the four verbs orbiting in the eye.

concepts.tech: R3F is lazy-loaded (next/dynamic, ssr:false) and mounted only when an IntersectionObserver with root '#scroll-container' sees the world within about one viewport; it unmounts after. Canvas uses frameloop='never' and is advanced from gsap.ticker, so Lenis (lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)), the pinned ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container', pinType transform, scrub) and WebGL all run on one clock. The static board, marker scribbles, kanban, cans and all readable text are SVG/DOM behind a transparent canvas. Camera fov and distance are solved so board units map to CSS px, which lets the WebGL notes sit pixel-exact over the DOM board before the rip. Notes are one InstancedMesh: curl and flutter in the vertex shader; paper, adhesive-strip gradient, handwriting atlas and UV emissive in the fragment shader. The handwriting atlas is drawn at runtime on a 2D canvas after document.fonts.load: a neat day set plus a per-character-jittered night set. Mosaic targets come from text drawn onto a 64x24 offscreen canvas, with filled cells assigned to the nearest notes so paths don't cross. Perf: 600-800 notes on desktop, 160-220 on mobile (chosen by width and deviceMemory). DPR is clamped at 1.5 (1.25 on mobile). No shadows and no post-processing library; the glow is faked with an emissive boost plus additive halo quads. The fluorescent flicker never exceeds 3 flashes per second, at low contrast. Reduced motion: no canvas and no pin. A static dusk board shows the kanban, the three results as flat SVG sticky-note mosaics with captions, and real headings. The canvas is aria-hidden, and a parallel semantic list carries every fact.
concepts.risk: Biggest risk: the storm could read as a generic 'particles form text' effect, and the mosaics could echo the colored-square grids of the Rubik's and Minecraft worlds. Mitigation: make every note unmistakably paper (curl, adhesive-strip shading, handwriting, ±8° rotation jitter, overlaps), keep the mosaics loose and wobbly instead of grid-perfect, stick to the fluorescent-UV palette (no cube primaries), and hold each mosaic only briefly. Secondary risk: WebGL cost on low-end phones, handled by the adaptive note count and the static fallback.

concepts.name: Hot Reload
concepts.oneLiner: This world doesn't show a hackathon, it IS one. The section boots as raw unstyled HTML, styles itself into a maximal poster, then deletes one line of CSS and collapses into a heap. It hot-reloads into pitch mode and finally git-resets, all on the visitor's own screen.

palette.role: Unstyled paper. The v0.0.1 cold open
Default-link blue turned electric blue. Structure and the BUILD layer
Hotfix magenta. The world's signature color: headline blocks, flood fills
Build yellow. Highlights, toasts, starburst badges
Stack-trace red. The crash, diff deletions, the error sheet
Pitch-room indigo. Projector darkness for PITCH and the REPEAT rewind

concepts.typography: The cold open deliberately loads NO font: the browser's default serif and default-blue underlined links are the joke. When the CSS installs, headings swap to Anybody (Google Fonts variable; width 50-150, weight 100-900). The swap is visible letter by letter as the width axis jumps from ultra-condensed to ultra-expanded, and the width also follows scroll velocity. During BREAK, every letter of 'HACKATHONS' (split with GSAP SplitText) becomes its own falling piece. JetBrains Mono for everything machine-made: diff lines, toasts, inspector tags, the error sheet, the git terminal and the commit ticker.
concepts.atmosphere: The stage is framed as a generic, original app window ('localhost:3000/hackathons'); no real browser UI is copied. Cold open: a white page with a faint blueprint grid. Styled state: hackathon-poster maximalism with magenta/yellow/blue color blocks, checkerboard bands, halftone gradients, starburst badges and grain. BREAK: red vignette, rainbow outlines colored by nesting depth on every element, one decaying screen shake. PITCH: the room goes dark indigo, a projector light cone fills with drifting dust motes, and the slide sits keystoned on the wall. REPEAT: VHS rewind with RGB split, scanlines and tracking jitter. Ambient: a blinking caret, plus a bottom ticker of honest commit messages that speeds up with scroll velocity.
concepts.heroMoment: THE CRASH (about 45% into the world). A floating mini-editor types one red diff line: '- display: grid;'. The instant it executes, the whole styled world drops out of its layout and falls: each letter of the giant HACKATHONS heading, the three result cards, the four verb chips, badges, buttons and the fake nav (about 40 pieces on desktop, about 22 on mobile). Pieces tumble with spin, squash into the floor, bounce, and settle into a believable heap along the bottom of the stage. Each one wears a rainbow debug outline and an inspector tag, while an original red runtime-error sheet slams down from the top ('ReferenceError: sleep is not defined'). Build: on every ScrollTrigger refresh, a tiny deterministic 'skyline drop' packer computes each piece's resting spot: a seeded x position, the lowest free y on the current skyline, ±14° tilt, slight overlap allowed. A GSAP sub-timeline then tweens every piece from its measured grid rect to that spot (power2.in fall, CustomBounce settle, rotation) with a seeded stagger. Because it's an ordinary timeline, it scrubs both ways: scroll back up and the page un-crashes, with pieces flying back into the grid. A hot-reload flash then FLIPs every piece from the heap into its PITCH layout.
supporting: Cold-open gag: v0.0.1 unstyled HTML. A default-serif <h1>, a default-blue underlined list of the three events, and gray placeholder boxes with an X. Readable, deliberate, and over in under one screen.

The CSS installs itself in three visible layers, each announced by a toast ('✓ colors.css', '✓ type.css', '✓ motion.css'): paint-bucket flood fills (circle() clip-paths blooming from 'click points' in magenta, yellow and blue), the Anybody font swap, then a motion layer where everything starts breathing.
Rainbow debug mode during BREAK: outlines colored by nesting depth, inspector tags like <ResultCard place="2nd" />, and the site's custom cursor turns into an inspect crosshair.

Pitch mode: the whole stage tilts into a projected 16:9 slide (CSS 3D perspective keystone) and the custom cursor becomes a red laser dot. Each result gets its own slide look: blueprint for IIT Roorkee Productathon, a houndstooth/runway pattern for Ashoka University Fashion Design Hackathon, deadpan black-on-white for Smart India Hackathon: 'participated.'
Honest commit ticker along the bottom ('fix', 'fix again', 'it works don't touch it', 'final_final_v3', 'pls'). Its speed and the heading's width axis both follow scroll velocity.
REPEAT as a literal 'git reset --hard': a terminal line types itself, then the master timeline rewinds at 3x through pitch, heap, poster and raw HTML with VHS RGB split and scanlines.
scrollBeats: 0-8% COLD OPEN: the laptop-screen portal lands on the unstyled v0.0.1 page. The status bar reads 'localhost:3000/hackathons · age 18 · compiling…' with a blinking caret.

8-32% BUILD: three CSS sweeps install the world (flood fills, the Anybody font swap with width 50 to 150, then the motion layer). The three event cards turn into styled cards, toasts stack up, and the BUILD chip lights up.

32-58% BREAK: the diff line '- display: grid;' appears and runs. HERO: the whole layout collapses into a rainbow-outlined heap, the red error sheet slams down with 'relax, this one's on purpose' underneath, and the screen gives one decaying shake.

58-84% PITCH: a hot-reload flash, and the heap springs up into presentation mode (keystoned slide, projector cone, laser cursor). It steps through three slides: IIT Roorkee Productathon: ~4th · Ashoka University Fashion Design Hackathon: 2nd · Smart India Hackathon: participated.
