concepts.tech: No three.js and no physics engine. The medium is the page itself, so this is DOM + CSS + GSAP, the lightest technique that sells it. One pinned ScrollTrigger on '#scroll-container' (pinType transform; Lenis driven from gsap.ticker with lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)) runs a master timeline labeled build/break/pitch/repeat, which works as the state machine for the story. BUILD uses CSS custom properties, circle() clip-path floods, and font-variation-settings tweens on only a few big glyphs. BREAK uses GSAP SplitText, CustomBounce and the skyline-drop packer; function-based values with invalidateOnRefresh recompute the heap on resize or font load. The falling pieces are aria-hidden, absolutely positioned clones moved only with translate3d/rotate (no layout thrash), while the real semantic content (an h2 plus an ordered list of results) stays untouched underneath for screen readers. Toasts use Framer Motion AnimatePresence. PITCH uses a CSS 3D perspective keystone, Canvas 2D dust (up to 120 motes on desktop, 40 on mobile), and a context swap on the site's custom cursor to show the laser dot. The rewind uses tl.tweenFromTo at 3x plus CSS RGB-split and scanline overlays. The stage is overflow: clip with clamp() type, so the wide headings never cause horizontal scroll at 375px. Mobile: about 22 pieces (the heading splits into syllables, not letters), no shake, no dust, single-column slides. Reduced motion: no pin, no fall. The styled poster renders statically with one frozen debug-outline detail and a small static error card as the gag, then the three results as a plain list; every state change becomes a crossfade. No effect flashes more than 3 times per second.
concepts.risk: Biggest risk: visitors could mistake the staged crash or the unstyled cold open for a real bug, and the PITCH slides could drift into the Startups world's pitch-deck territory. Mitigation: frame everything as theatre with the window bar, the version tag, the visible diff line that 'causes' the crash, and the wink line under the error sheet. Keep the unstyled state under about 8% of the world and recover instantly with the hot reload. Keep PITCH as 'presentation mode of this same page' (keystone, laser, projector), never an investor-deck look. Recompute the heap on every refresh so pieces never land misaligned after a resize.

why: Hot Reload is stronger because the medium becomes the message. It is the one world where the visitor's own screen gets built, broken, pitched and reset, so all four verbs happen as real events instead of decoration, and the reversible page collapse is a genuine 'how did they build that' moment. It also needs no WebGL, so it is light, robust at 375px and simple to make reduced-motion safe, and it can't clash with the colored-square look of the Rubik's and Minecraft worlds.

world: #10 JEE (age 18): ~2 years of JEE prep, IIT didn't happen. The failure chapter, written honestly and deliberately different in tone from the worlds around it.

concepts.name: The Impression
concepts.oneLiner: A neon-drenched exam sheet takes ~2 years of graphite, gets red-penned and erased to blank. Then a pencil rubbed across the empty page shows what the pressure left behind: a galaxy of ghost formulas and, pressed deepest of all, 'The person doesn't.'

palette.role: Exam-sheet cream: the paper world and background
Graphite: formulas, the pencil hatching, the rubbed field
Highlighter yellow: dominant neon of the grind
Highlighter pink: second neon; where it overlaps yellow, multiply mixes them into orange-reds
Red pen: the strike through IIT. It is the only color the eraser can't lift
Site lime: the final highlighter swipe on 'The person doesn't.', the first color back after the drain

concepts.typography: Kalam (Indian Type Foundry's handwriting face, 300/700) sets every formula, the plan 'IIT' and the pressed statement. Formulas 'write' with left-to-right mask reveals along each baseline, with ±1.5° per-glyph rotation jitter. 'THE PERSON DOESN'T.' never appears as DOM type. It exists only as a Kalam 700 groove in the height map (~14vw on desktop, broken over 2–3 lines on phones) and is read as negative space in the graphite. Instrument Serif (regular + italic) sets the printed exam lines and the honest copy ('IIT didn't happen.'). These print in with an ink-spread settle (blur 2px→0, tracking +0.04em→0), not flashy motion. Geist Mono (the site's) sets 'Q.10 · AGE 18', the A/B/C/D answer-bubble letters and labels.
concepts.atmosphere: Cream exam paper fills the frame edge to edge, with procedural fiber grain, a faint blue 5mm graph grid (#8FB3E8) and a red margin rule. Soft top light; a contact shadow under one lifted corner; highlighter bleed and graphite dust at the edges. The sheet 'breathes' with a 0.3° curl. After the verdict the whole world is greyscale and nearly silent: a blank grey page carrying one surviving red line. For the rubbing, the light drops to a low raking angle, so grooves cast hairline shadows and graphite glints silver.
concepts.heroMoment: THE RUBBING: a graphite rubbing that reveals indentations. Once the eraser has left the sheet blank, a full-viewport shader paper (fbm fiber noise for tooth, the grid faded to grey) hides a height map built at runtime on an offscreen canvas. It holds every formula from the grind beat at shallow depth, the struck 'IIT' a little deeper, 'THE PERSON DOESN'T.' in Kalam 700 deeper still, and the next world's portal icon deepest of all, blurred 2px into groove profiles. Before any graphite goes down, the cursor works as a low raking light (shading from the height map's gradient), so faint grooves glint wherever it passes. Then scroll drives an SVG pencil, tilted 20°, hatching the page in a deterministic diagonal zig-zag. The zig-zag path is baked once into a reveal-time texture: each pixel stores the earliest t at which the brush touches it. That makes per-pixel coverage O(1) (smoothstep(t−ε, t, progress) × paper tooth) and exact when the user scrubs backwards, because nothing accumulates. Graphite is held back from grooves (× (1 − smoothstep on depth)), so every pressed line comes up as a bright negative inside silvery hatching with a graphite specular sheen. By ~85% the sheet is a dark field full of white ghost formulas, like a galaxy. The deepest groove, THE PERSON DOESN'T., reads brightest, and a lime (#C5FF3D) highlighter swipe lands on it. Pointer and touch rubbing add strokes to a half-res FBO for anyone who wants to do it by hand, but scroll alone always completes the reveal.
supporting: Neon highlighter overload: five chisel-tip highlighters (yellow, pink, green, orange, blue) slash across the formulas in mix-blend-mode: multiply, and their overlaps mix new colors. Rough, bleeding edges are pre-generated jittered SVG paths (no live SVG filters). The swipes get faster and messier as the grind accelerates.

Answer-bubble drumroll: a column of generic A/B/C/D bubbles fills with scribbled graphite (stroke-dash scribble paths) in a ripple that speeds up like a drumroll, synced to the page blizzard. No real exam-board layout or branding.

Page blizzard: 6–10 recycled CSS-3D sheets flip over the top edge faster and faster, each one denser with formulas (generic F = ma, PV = nRT, ∫eˣdx = eˣ + C, λ = h/p) and highlights. ~2 years compressed into a few scrolls.

The verdict and the color death: one red-pen line drags through 'IIT' and pools into an ink blot. A full-bleed grey layer with mix-blend-mode: saturation then drains every neon to grey in one long breath. The red line sits above that layer and stays red.

Eraser storm: a giant plain white eraser (no brand sleeve) sweeps the sheet in scroll-scrubbed arcs, baked into the same reveal-time texture approach. Graphite smears along its leading edge, then lifts. Rubber crumbs (150 on desktop, 40 on mobile, in a tiny verlet sim) roll and tumble off the edge of the sheet.
Raking-light cursor: on the blank page the site cursor becomes a low grazing light, and grooves catch hairline highlights wherever it passes, a hint that something is still in the paper.
scrollBeats: 0–10%: The portal lands on a cream exam sheet. 'Q.10 · AGE 18' sits in mono at the top. A giant handwritten JEE takes a single yellow highlighter swipe, and '~2 years of JEE prep. Attempt all questions.' prints in below.

10–40%: The grind. The plan is written in capitals in the top margin: IIT. Then the sheet goes maximal: formulas write themselves across the grid, five neon highlighters slash through in multiply, the answer-bubble column fills in an accelerating drumroll, and sheets flip faster and faster in the page blizzard.

40–52%: The verdict. Everything freezes. One red-pen line strikes through IIT and pools into a blot, and every neon drains to grey in one breath. Copy, plain and unanimated: 'IIT didn't happen.' then 'This one didn't work.'

52–68%: The eraser. A giant white eraser sweeps the sheet in scroll-scrubbed arcs. Graphite smears and lifts, and crumbs tumble off the edge. The page ends blank, grey and quiet, except for the red strike, which no eraser lifts. Printed copy: 'Some plans end.'

68–92%: HERO, the rubbing. The cursor becomes a raking light that shows faint grooves. On scroll, a pencil shades the blank page diagonally and white ghosts of every erased formula surface in the graphite. The deepest handwritten groove reads 'THE PERSON DOESN'T.', and a lime highlighter swipes it.

92–100%: The deepest impression of all, the next world's icon, rises as a glowing groove at center. Its interior turns transparent (alpha = groove × uPortal), it punches through the paper, and the shared SVG portal mask takes over for the dive.

It is a generic pencil with no brand stripes. The zoom origin sits on the sharpened cone, so the cone and body flood the screen in the first third of the dive.

concepts.tech: A pinned section of ~3.5 viewport heights, driven by one GSAP master timeline (ScrollTrigger with scroller '#scroll-container', lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update), scrub 1, a label per beat). The grind beat is DOM/SVG: formulas revealed by animated clip-path masks, highlighter swipes as pre-generated jittered SVG paths in multiply, bubble fills as stroke-dash scribbles, and the blizzard as recycled CSS-3D sheets (perspective 1200px). The color death is a single saturation-blend layer tweened 0→1, so no children repaint, with the red line z-indexed above it. The eraser, rubbing and exit all live in ONE lazy-loaded full-viewport WebGL2 fragment shader: a raw full-screen triangle with no new dependency, or an orthographic R3F plane if the shared R3F chunk is already loaded. Its uniforms are paper-noise params, the height-map texture (offscreen canvas, rebuilt on debounced resize with phone line breaks) and two reveal-time textures (eraser arcs and rub zig-zag), each baked once by drawing path segments from last to first so every pixel keeps its earliest t. That keeps the shader O(1) and exact when scrubbed in either direction. Graphite sheen comes from a raking light whose azimuth follows the pointer. Eraser crumbs run in a small verlet sim on the same gsap.ticker (one clock). Mobile at 375px: DPR capped at 1.5, half the formulas, 5 blizzard sheets, the statement broken onto 2–3 lines, and touch rubbing off (a tap stamps a small rub burst), so vertical scroll never fights the gesture. Reduced motion: no pin and no scrub. The end state renders once (rubbed sheet, ghost formulas, red-struck IIT, lime-highlighted statement) and all copy appears as static semantic text. The canvas is aria-hidden, with a parallel h2/p for every line. No-WebGL fallback: a CSS graphite gradient with the statement as cream SVG text.
concepts.risk: The climax could read as a familiar scratch-card gimmick, or go unseen if it depends on the user's effort. Mitigation: scroll alone performs a deliberate, beautiful hatching pass that always finishes the reveal by 92%. The payoff is made much bigger than a scratch-off: raking light shows the grooves before any graphite goes down, a whole galaxy of ghost formulas surfaces rather than one hidden word, and the graphite glints. Hand-rubbing is a bonus layer, never a requirement.

concepts.name: Projections
concepts.oneLiner: Under a single desk lamp, ~2 years of colorful books pile up until their shadow spells IIT. The lamp dies. When it relights from a new angle, the exact same pile casts a brand-new shape: the portal to what's next.

palette.role: Midnight room: background and the full lights-out beat
Tungsten lamp: key light, volumetric cone, label glow
Lit plaster: the walls the shadows land on, and the color of the confessional copy
Magenta covers: the dominant book color in the pile, and the dusk strobe in the window
Cobalt covers: secondary book color; it also tints the violet-blue shadow fill
Site lime: the rim glint when the new shadow snaps into focus, and the underline under 'The person doesn't.'

concepts.typography: Anton is used only for the shadow letterforms. 'JEE' and 'IIT' are rasterized from Anton into the carve masks so the condensed bars cast razor-clean shadows, and these words never appear as DOM type. Fraunces (variable: opsz, wght, SOFT, WONK) sets the confessional lines in plaster cream. During lights-out they appear with zero motion. At the snap, 'The person doesn't.' hardens from SOFT 100 / wght 300 to SOFT 0 / wght 700, in sync with the shadow coming into focus. Geist Mono (the site's) sets labels like 'AGE 18 · ~2 YEARS OF JEE PREP', uppercase with +0.12em tracking, visible only where lamplight falls through a CSS radial mask that tracks the lamp's projected screen position.
concepts.atmosphere: A dark room corner at night: two plaster walls and a desk surface, everything under ~5% luminance except the tungsten cone. The lamp sits LOW, its shade at desk height, so shadows throw upward and tower over the pile: the classic shadow-sculpture composition, small pile at the bottom of the frame and a giant silhouette on the wall above. Details: a volumetric, noise-textured cone with slow-drifting dust motes; violet-tinted shadows against warm plaster; fine film grain; a faint ±3% lamp-hum flicker. During the build-up a small high window cycles through skies. Lights-out is total black. At the end, the icon shadow glows with the next world's palette.
concepts.heroMoment: THE NEW ANGLE: a dual-shadow sculpture. One pile of colored books and notebooks (an InstancedMesh of ~1–3k slabs) sits in a room corner. It is carved at runtime so that a low lamp at position A (right side, shade at desk height, ~1.5 units away) throws a towering, crisp IIT up the left wall, and the same lamp at position B (front, 90° around the arc) throws the next world's portal icon up the back wall. The carve: take each voxel center c in a 48³ grid, perspective-project it from A onto the left-wall plane and from B onto the back-wall plane, and keep c only if both projections land inside their 128² masks (Anton 'IIT', and the icon's SVG path). A validator back-projects every mask pixel and adds support voxels wherever coverage is missing. Runs of voxels are then greedy-merged into book-shaped slabs. After lights-out, the lamp re-ignites ~20° off its old spot, so IIT only flickers as a warped ghost and never re-forms. Scroll then swings the lamp along the arc toward B. Both walls fill with tangled, meaningless shadow while the pile does not move a millimeter. Within 3° of B, a magnetic snap eases the lamp home; on desktop the pointer adds a ±6° wobble, so you can feel the shape slide in and out of focus. The icon locks in razor-sharp with a lime rim glint, a 120ms camera trauma kick and an optional switch click on the shared audio clock. The plan was only ever a projection; the person is what casts it.
supporting: Shadow title card: the first thing you see is 'JEE' cast on the wall by a small, messy stack (the same carve pipeline with one silhouette), which teaches the visual grammar before it matters.

concepts.tech: A pinned section of ~3.5 viewport heights. The R3F scene is lazy-loaded through next/dynamic (ssr: false) and mounts when the section is within one viewport (IntersectionObserver rooted on #scroll-container). It runs with frameloop='never' and is stepped by advance() from gsap.ticker, so Lenis, ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container') and WebGL share one clock. Scene: a room corner made of two wall planes and a desk plane in plaster MeshStandardMaterial; one SpotLight as the lamp (castShadow, mapSize 2048 on desktop / 1024 on mobile, PCFSoftShadowMap, tight penumbra at the two reveal angles); a faint violet hemisphere fill; ACES Filmic tone mapping; an additive cone mesh; dust as Points. The carve runs in a Web Worker on mount. OffscreenCanvas rasterizes 'JEE' and 'IIT' (Anton) and the next world's icon (its SVG d-string as Path2D) into masks. The worker then does the perspective carve, the coverage validator with support voxels and the greedy merge, and returns transferable instance data (start/end position and scale, cover color, delay). Books are one InstancedMesh whose shader paints cover color on the top and bottom faces and cream page lines on the sides. The fall and restack animate in the vertex shader from one uBuild uniform, mirrored in customDepthMaterial so the shadows move with the books. The lamp's position on its arc is a GSAP proxy. The shadow-as-window effect is a duplicate back-wall plane built from ShaderLib.shadow: it reads getShadowMask() and outputs the next world's gradient with alpha = shadow × uPortal. Perf: ~1–3k instances on desktop and under 1k on mobile (32³ grid); one shadow caster; DPR clamped to [1, 1.5]; no postprocessing on mobile (CSS grain overlay instead); an FPS probe steps down grid and shadow resolution; paused offscreen; everything disposed on unmount. Mobile at 375px portrait: the towering shadows suit the frame, and the camera frames one wall at a time (left wall for IIT, a pan to the back wall for the hero). Reduced motion: no scrub. A single still renders with two lamps: a dim one casting IIT faintly on the left wall, and a full one casting the next icon crisply on the back wall. All copy shows as static DOM, and the portal becomes a plain crossfade. No-WebGL fallback: a flat SVG diorama of that same still. The canvas is aria-hidden, and every line lives in semantic DOM.
concepts.risk: Everything depends on two shadows reading instantly. A gappy IIT, a mushy icon, or a pile that looks like a voxel blob (and echoes the Minecraft world) would kill it, and real-time shadows are the heaviest thing on the page. Mitigation: carve at runtime with a coverage validator and automatic support slabs; require a bold silhouette with filled pixels on every row (pad or scale the next world's icon if needed); use heavy condensed Anton; use 2048 shadow maps with tight penumbra at the two reveal angles; greedy-merge voxels into book slabs with page-edge sides and cover colors so the pile reads as a desk of study books, not cubes; keep an FPS probe that steps quality down; guarantee a static SVG diorama fallback.

why: Projections turns the chapter's line into a single physical image. The plan was a shadow, the person is the pile that casts it, and a new angle makes a new shape, so the honest beat and the portal handoff become literally the same mechanic. The Impression is beautiful, but its rub-to-reveal is familiar scratch-card territory; a pile whose shadow changes meaning is a genuine 'how did they build that'.

concepts.name: Whorl of Worlds
concepts.oneLiner: Skim low through rainbow canyons as every world rewinds beneath you at hyperspeed, then the camera cranes straight up and you realize the canyons were ridges all along: every world braided into one giant fingerprint. Josh's pattern.

palette.role: Void: canyon floor and page background, the dark that frames the print
Josh lime (the site accent coming home): the live outer ridge, the pen tip, the scan result and the Back-to-home thumbprint

concepts.typography: Big Shoulders Display 900 for the title card and headline. It is condensed enough to stack as 'I KEEP / TRYING / THINGS.' at 375px. Geist Mono (the site's own mono) carries the forensic HUD: uppercase, 0.14em tracking, scramble-decode type-on. Instrument Serif Italic carries the human lines (the honest line and each value sentence), the only soft voice in a forensic world. During the rewind, each world's name pops for one beat in that world's own display face, pulled from its tokens.
concepts.atmosphere: Violet-black void. Inside the canyons it is dusk: crests glow in their world colors, ultraviolet fog eats the distance, dust motes drift down the grooves (max 180 on desktop, 60 on mobile), and the camera breathes with a slight handheld wobble. After the reveal the grade snaps to crisp black. The print floats with a soft ink-bleed bloom, a second ridge layer offset 0.6 degrees adds a live moiré shimmer (op-art from pure math), and procedural film grain sits on top. Cyan corner reticles and a faint scan grid frame the print like a biometric reader. Restraint: the HUD stays thin cream lines, and only the print carries color.
concepts.heroMoment: THE CRANE REVEAL: one continuous camera move that turns a canyon flight into a fingerprint. Build: a single R3F plane (1 × 1.35 units; 256×345 segments on desktop, 112×151 on mobile) with one ShaderMaterial. A Web Worker strokes ~26 hand-authored SVG ridge paths onto an OffscreenCanvas as soft layered strokes. The paths include a whorl core, one delta, and a deliberate bifurcation, lake, spur, ridge ending and island near the core. The worker outputs an RGBA DataTexture: R = ridge height; G = band id 0–10, with Anchoring innermost and Hackathons at the rim; B = the unfinished outer lime ridge. The vertex shader displaces by R and takes normals from finite differences. The fragment shader paints each band in its world's hero color with that world's procedural micro-pattern (scanlines, mow stripes, 3×3 sticker checker, dot grid, placard hatch, tape chevrons, chunky voxel steps, speed streaks, knurl crosshatch, graph grid, glyph hash) and adds an emissive crest rim. Scroll 14→42%: the camera skims at crest height + 0.012 on a straight rim-to-core line, terrain-following with a damped look-ahead. Distance is mapped through power3.in, so ridge crossings accelerate from one world per beat into a blur: the rewind, Hackathons → Anchoring. Scroll 42→54%: trauma-shake and a hard stop at the core. Then the camera pitches from −8° to −90°, rises from 0.02 to 1.65 units and narrows its FOV from 75° to 32°. The canyons shrink into ridges and the whole rainbow fingerprint snaps into frame, centered and portrait-shaped so it fits a phone naturally. Scroll 54→62%: a cyan scan bar sweeps, the HUD prints PATTERN MATCH, and 'I KEEP TRYING THINGS.' stamps in.
supporting: Unspooling portals: the 11 previous portal silhouettes orbit the title card. GSAP MorphSVG then unravels each outline into a single strand that dives into the terrain, and a per-band reveal uniform ignites that world's ridge band. Every portal on the page literally becomes part of the print.
Ridged type: the title card and headline use stacked concentric strokes in world colors, so the type looks printed by the same fingertip, and the rings ripple outward when the scan hits.

Banknote microprint and loupe: the 9 domains (Sports · Content · Gaming · Speaking · Academics · Building · Business · Design · Technology) run as 6–7px microtext along the ridges via SVG textPath. A lerped cyan loupe follows the cursor and magnifies them until they are legible. On touch the loupe rests on the print and can be dragged.

concepts.tech: Craziness level L4–L5a, kept deliberately light. Total length is ~3.6 viewport heights: a 2.2vh pinned hero plus a 1.4vh evidence board. The 3D is one R3F/drei <Canvas>, lazy-loaded with next/dynamic (ssr:false) and prewarmed while the Hackathons world is on screen. Live 3D is used only because skimming needs real parallax and occlusion between ridges. It is one plane, one ShaderMaterial and one draw call, with no GLB and no image files: the ridge texture is generated in a Web Worker from the same SVG paths the 2D print uses. One clock: Lenis (wrapper #scroll-container) runs on gsap.ticker with lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update). A single ScrollTrigger (scroller '#scroll-container', pin, pinType 'transform', scrub 0.6) drives one GSAP timeline. Its progress feeds both the DOM HUD and a ref read in useFrame, so there are no React re-renders; frameloop is 'demand' with invalidate(). Finishing layer, desktop only: ACES tone-map plus crest bloom, grain and vignette in one EffectComposer, a per-act grade swap (dusk-violet → clean black), a breathing camera and trauma shake on the core hit. At the top-down frame, under the scan bar, the canvas crossfades into a pixel-matched SVG print (same viewBox) for crisp microtext and callouts, then unmounts to free the GPU. Mobile: 112×151 segments, a 512px texture, DPR capped at 1.5, no post-processing, 60 motes and a shorter flight; the evidence board stacks the sticky print in the top 50svh with cards beneath. Low-end devices and no-WebGL get a 2.5D fake: the SVG print on a CSS-3D plane goes from rotateX 80° to 0° and scale 6 to 1. Reduced motion: no pin, flight or scan, just the static top-down print with the headline stamped, every callout visible and the live ridge ending in a still lime dot. The canvas is aria-hidden, and all copy is semantic DOM: an h2, uls for values, currently and next, and a real <a href='/'>. Band colors are luminance-matched and label pops are throttled to at most 3 per second, so the rewind never strobes.
concepts.risk: Biggest risk: the low skim can cause motion sickness, and the final top-down print could read as a vinyl record or a maze instead of a fingerprint. Mitigation: clamp the camera's angular velocity, keep the horizon visible, never roll, ease the speed ramp, and give reduced-motion users the static print. Hand-author the ridge layout with an unmistakable whorl, delta and ridge endings inside an oval vignette. Prototype the crane reveal at 375px first, and confirm the 3D-to-SVG handoff is seamless before building anything else.

concepts.name: The Try Machine
concepts.oneLiner: A giant scroll-powered chain-reaction machine bolted together from every world's leftover parts. A lime marble (Josh) drops through it, and each contraption it touches floods from blueprint line art into full color while physically acting out one of his values, until the track runs out into blueprint that hasn't been built yet.

Blueprint chalk: grid, line art, dimension lines, stencil labels

Tomato: built parts and impact flashes

Bubblegum: built parts, door bursts, control-panel LEDs. Each built part also takes its own world's hero color token

concepts.typography: Bungee, with Bungee Shade layered behind for extrusion, for the crane-stacked sign. Each letter is a physical block that drops with squash-and-stretch (fast attack, back.out settle) and stacks as 'I KEEP / TRYING / THINGS.' on mobile. Saira Stencil One for stenciled part names and value headers, revealed through a spray-paint noise mask. Caveat for Josh's handwritten margin notes (the honest line and each value sentence), wiped on behind a moving pencil tip. Geist Mono (the site's mono) for the engineering title block, specs and dimension labels.
concepts.atmosphere: Cobalt blueprint paper with a white 8px/40px grid (CSS gradients), eraser smudges and pencil hatching from a runtime-generated noise tile, and section marks, center lines and dimension arrows everywhere. Built parts pop off the paper with flat saturated fills, chunky 3px ink outlines, halftone shading and hard offset shadows (neo-brutal grounding). Idle micro-motion keeps the built machine alive: gears tick, a pendulum swings, cables sag and wobble, LEDs breathe. Everything unbuilt stays perfectly still. Restraint is built into the system: color means done, blueprint means not yet.
concepts.heroMoment: THE RUN: blueprint becomes real in the marble's wake. The section pins for ~250vh, and a 100svh camera window translates a tall SVG machine so the lime marble always sits at about 42% of viewport height. One master route path drives the marble (MotionPathPlugin) through a piecewise easing table derived from v = √(2gh) per segment. The marble is slow and legible at each mechanism, gravity-fast on drops, squashes and stretches on impact, and rolls at an angle of distance / radius. Every part is a <g> with two layers and a contact t: white blueprint line art, and a flat saturated fill with a 3px ink outline and hard offset shadow. When the marble arrives, a CSS clip-path circle() expanding from the exact contact point reveals the color layer, and the part performs its value action on the same scrubbed timeline. Scroll back and everything un-builds to blueprint. By the bottom you look up at a maximal, fully colored machine that your own scroll powered, and its last stage cranes the headline into place.
supporting: Five values as five mechanisms. CURIOSITY is a peek rail past 9 hinged doors (the domains), each flipping open in CSS 3D and firing a burst of color. OBSESSION is a funnel that grabs the marble and spirals it deep through a counter-rotating op-art vortex. EXPERIMENTATION is a pegboard where the marble splits into 5 translucent ghost tries and one lime survivor exits. ADAPTABILITY is a moving-box track that buckles and collapses more than once, and each time a packing-tape roll unrolls a fresh track. BUILDING is a hopper labeled CONSUME, a lever flipped to MAKE, and a crane that stacks the sign.

Parts from every world, matched to each world's final portal icon: mic-stand lever, ball counterweight, puzzle-cube gear, phone dominoes, gavel hammer, moving boxes, chunky voxel steps, rocket booster, dumbbell seesaw weight, pencil ramp, laptop trigger. Each is stenciled with its world name and painted in its world's color when built.
Dimension-line jokes: blueprint dimension arrows are labeled with words, never invented numbers: 'DEEP' on the funnel, 'MORE THAN ONCE' on the collapse, 'NOT YET' on the unbuilt wing.
The 2026 control panel: a chunky panel bolted to the machine's base with 6 lit toggles (CS + AI/ML, College, Startups, Building, Learning, Training), all ON, with LEDs pulsing at different rates.

The unbuilt wing: past the panel the track continues as pure blueprint. A pencil sketches 5 dashed contraptions (stroke-dashoffset) labeled with the NEXT goals, and they never get color. The marble stops at the last built edge, wobbling.

The last lever: a big lime lever labeled BACK TO HOME. Drag or tap it and the marble is flung up a launch tube and out of frame, then the route changes. Underneath it is a real <a href='/'> for keyboard and screen-reader users.
scrollBeats: 0–8%: The gear portal irises open onto the title-card blueprint, where the whole machine waits as faint line art. A lime marble drops from the hub hole into the first chute, and the camera window starts following it.

8–22%: CURIOSITY. The marble rolls along the peek rail and the 9 domain doors flip open in sequence, each firing a burst of color and pattern. The rail floods from blueprint to built behind the marble.
22–34%: OBSESSION. The funnel grabs the marble, which spirals down a counter-rotating op-art vortex, faster and deeper, while the camera zooms in with it (dimension line: DEEP).
34–46%: EXPERIMENTATION. The pegboard splits the marble into 5 ghost tries on pre-baked paths, with pegs flashing on contact. One lime survivor drops out.

58–72%: BUILDING. The marble falls into the CONSUME hopper, a lever flips to MAKE, and the bucket lifts a crane that stacks block letters into 'I KEEP TRYING THINGS.' The margin note writes itself beside the sign. The pin releases.

concepts.tech: Craziness level L2 (the Antic tier) with zero WebGL, so there is no 3D bundle. Total length is ~3.4 viewport heights: a 2.5vh pinned run, then an unpinned 0.9vh panel and unbuilt wing. The stack is SVG + GSAP (ScrollTrigger + MotionPathPlugin) + Framer Motion, all on gsap.ticker with Lenis, ScrollTrigger scroller '#scroll-container' and pinType 'transform'. One master timeline owns the marble, the camera translateY, every part reveal and every mechanism, so reverse scroll un-builds perfectly. The plinko ghost paths are pre-baked once with a seeded matter.js run at dev time and committed as JSON point arrays, so there is no runtime physics. Sign letters are DOM spans in Bungee, dropped with GSAP. Color reveals use CSS clip-path circle() on per-part wrappers. No SVG filters run while anything moves; paper grain is a tiny runtime-generated noise tile set as a CSS background. Mobile at 375px: a single-column zig-zag machine, doors in a 3×3 grid, a narrower pegboard, idle gears paused offscreen, and fewer than 400 SVG nodes live. Reduced motion: no pin or scrub. The whole machine renders already built (except the NEXT wing) as a static annotated poster with the marble at rest at the edge, and every value, current item and next goal is a readable DOM list.
concepts.risk: Biggest risk: it is heavy on illustration and choreography, and it could balloon into a slow, kiddie toy that reads as one more themed world instead of the finale. Mitigation: cap it at 5 mechanisms of at most 0.5vh each, and build parts as bold geometric shapes rather than detailed drawings. Blueprint precision, stencil type and dry dimension-line jokes keep it witty, not childish, and gravity-derived easing keeps the marble physical so it never feels like a slideshow.

why: Whorl of Worlds turns the whole portal-dive spine into the answer: the portal you enter becomes the canyon, every world becomes a ridge, and one camera move proves 'up close it's chaos, from far away it's a pattern', so 'I keep trying things' lands as Josh's identity rather than a slogan. The Try Machine is cheaper and charming, but it reads as one more themed world rather than the convergence of all eleven.
